docs.title: Zenith Filer Manual v2.0.0
docs.text:
Everything Zenith Filer can do, one article per feature. This is the same manual that ships inside the app.

Download the latest release Back to the Zenith Filer page

docs.title: About Zenith Filer
docs.text:
Zenith Filer is a dual-pane tabbed file explorer for Windows, designed for efficient file operations. It maintains an intuitive feel similar to the standard Explorer while offering advanced customization features for power users.

How to use this manual: The manual is split into one article per feature. Pick a category and an article in the table of contents on the left to open it, then click one of the headings listed under the article to jump straight there. The search box at the top searches every article at once and shows how many matches each article has.

First launch: After a short setup (language / theme / keymap / license agreement), a "First 5 steps" card appears at the bottom right of the main window. It lists "Open a folder and get where you need to be", "Move files by drag and drop", "Add a folder you often visit to Favorites", "Try the Ring Launcher" and "Find anything in the Command Palette", and each one checks itself off when you actually do it. Nothing is locked, so you can keep using the app as usual. "How to" on each row opens the steps for that action below the heading (mouse and keyboard, using the keys currently assigned) and briefly highlights where to do it, if there is a place to show; press it again to hide them. When all five are done, a small celebration plays and the card folds away. The ∨ at the top right collapses the card. Pressing × first asks, on the card itself, whether to close it and reminds you how to bring it back. If you quit halfway, or even before the card appears, it picks up where you left off next time. To bring it back after closing it, or to start over, use Control Deck > General > Show "First 5 steps".

First launch after an update: A card summarises what changed in that version — the version number and its one-line summary at the top, then every change in that version grouped under Added, Changed and Fixed, one line each, with a count beside each heading. A long list scrolls inside the card, which never grows past the edge of the screen. If you skipped a few versions, the newest is shown in detail and the ones in between get a line each. "View details" opens the full history. Close it with Esc, a click outside, or the Close button; ticking "Don't show this again" stops it for good. Control Deck > General > Show what's new on startup brings it back, and "Show now" on the same page replays it at any time. It is not shown on a first-ever launch.

docs.title: Confirmation & Error Dialogs
docs.text:
Confirmation dialogs and error messages within the app are displayed using custom app dialogs rather than standard Windows MessageBoxes.

Their background and text colors follow the theme you are using, and with rounded corners and a drop shadow they match the rest of the app.

Icons (info, warning, error, confirm) and buttons (OK / OK-Cancel / Yes-No) automatically switch based on the dialog's purpose. You can press Esc to cancel and drag the title bar area to move the dialog.

The buttons can be chosen from the keyboard too. When the dialog opens, the default button (Yes, for the delete confirmation) is already selected; ← and → (or Tab) move to the neighbouring button, and Enter presses the selected one. While you use the keyboard, the selected button is outlined. Pressing past the last button wraps around to the first.

  • Reporting an error: When an unexpected error occurs, the error dialog shows a "Report problem" button.

    It opens the feedback page in the Control Deck with the error message and the details of where it happened already filled into the subject and body. You can read and edit them before sending. The Windows user name in paths (the C:\Users\<name> part) is replaced with <user>, just as in the logs you attach.

docs.title: File Panes (Pane A / Pane B)
docs.text:
The main area consists of two independent file display regions (panes) arranged side by side. Each pane supports tabbed browsing.

  • Tab feature: Open multiple folders as tabs and switch between them while working.

  • Pane A (left) / Pane B (right): Each operates independently. Switch focus by clicking, or with ← → (in Details view) or F6. With the "Zenith standard" keymap Tab works too (in "Zenith 2", the default for new installations, Tab moves through the controls on screen instead).

    The focused pane (A/B only; the nav pane is excluded) has a slightly darker background.

    The upper menus (tab header, action row, address bar) are displayed in a slightly darker shade than the list area, making it easy to identify which pane is active.

  • Pane header: the header at the top of each pane has two rows, the action row (buttons and the search bar) and the address bar row. When the pane is narrow (under 1000) or when Search → Move search bar to second row in dual-pane mode is on with two side-by-side panes, the search bar moves down from the action row to a row of its own, making three rows (as in the image above). This gives the search bar the full width so the search history list is not cut off.

    • Row 1 (action row): When the toolbar's "Number of buttons" is "Standard", the buttons come in 6 groups separated by dividers.

      • Navigation: Back / Forward / Up / Refresh
      • Shortcuts: Home / Desktop / Downloads
      • Create: Create folder / Generate folder structure with AI
      • Manage: Open in Explorer / Import folders / Rename the selected items in one pass / Compare folders (pane A and pane B)
      • View modes: Details / Small, Medium and Large icons (List, Tiles and Content are hidden by default)
      • View Settings: Sort by / Column width (opens the "Column width" menu; the icon shows the current mode) / Folders first

      A new installation starts with "Fewer", which shows 9 buttons: Back, Forward, Up, Refresh, Create folder, Details, Medium icons, Large icons and Sort by. The others can be shown as described under "Customization" below. - Customization (Pro): The icons in this action row can be reordered by drag-and-drop and shown or hidden per button from Settings → Toolbar. "Add separator" lets you insert dividers anywhere to group buttons your way (separators can also be removed). Changes apply instantly to both panes and persist across restarts. "Reset to default" restores the original layout at any time (at least one button always remains). In the free version reordering and showing / hiding are shown locked, but "Number of buttons" still lets you choose "Fewer" (the 9 buttons File Explorer also has) or "Standard" (every button). New users start with "Fewer". The buttons hidden by default include the List, Tiles and Content view modes and, matching File Explorer's command bar, Cut, Copy, Paste, Rename, Delete, Undo, Properties, Select all, Invert selection and Select none (they act on that pane's list). - Buttons that do not fit ("≫"): When a pane is too narrow for all the icons, whatever does not fit is collected under a "≫" button. Press it to see them as a list with icon, name and assigned key, ready to run. The check runs per pane, so a "≫" appears only on the side that is narrow. Widen the splitter and it disappears again. Buttons you hid stay hidden, including inside the "≫" list. If the search box itself is what feels cramped, consider Search → Move search bar to second row in dual-pane mode as well. - The Home button navigates to the folder set in app settings ("A Pane Home" / "B Pane Home" under General). If not configured, Pane A goes to Desktop and Pane B goes to Downloads. - On the far right (while the search bar is on the action row) is a search box. Type a keyword and press Enter to execute the search (results appear in a new tab or the current tab depending on your search behavior settings). Inside the search box on the right, the hit count is displayed in real time. - While searching, the list column layout switches to a dedicated set (Name, Location, Path, Date Modified, Size). Click headers to sort, drag header borders to adjust column widths, and double-click a border to fit that column to its content. The column width mode is shared with normal lists (dragging switches to Set by hand; see "Column width" in View Options). The Path column is optimized for width and prioritizes showing the end of the path. - Row 2 (address bar row): Shows where you are as a breadcrumb, and lets you go somewhere by typing a path. See Address Bar and Breadcrumb for how to use it and how it works. - During a search, the address bar is replaced by a filter bar that lets you narrow search results by file type. - Search history dropdown: When you focus the search box, past search keywords (up to 100) are displayed in a dropdown. - Icons: A magnifying glass icon indicates normal search history; a lightning bolt icon indicates index search history. - Separate entries: The same keyword is shown as separate entries for normal vs index search. Entries with different size/date filter conditions are also recorded separately. - Restore: Selecting an item (click or Enter) automatically switches back to the search mode (normal/index) and filter conditions recorded at the time, and re-executes the search. - Keyboard operation: While the history is displayed, press the down arrow to move focus to the list, then use up/down arrows to navigate and Enter or click to select. The up arrow while the search box is focused does not move to the history. - Pressing Enter to execute a search automatically closes the history dropdown.

    • Search filter bar: When a search is executed, the row-2 address bar is replaced by a filter bar.

      You can narrow results by file type using checkboxes for Folders, Excel, Word, PPT, PDF, TXT, EXE, BAT, JSON, Images, and Others. "Select All" shows all types; "Deselect All" hides all. Files of unchecked types are not shown in the search results.

      Filter selection state is saved to settings.json and automatically restored on the next search and after app restart. Clear search conditions with the X button on the right of the search bar or the Esc key. By default Esc is two-step (first press clears the text, second clears the size/date filters and scope); turning on Settings → Search → "One-press full reset with Esc" clears everything in a single press.

  • Horizontal scrolling: In areas that can scroll horizontally (file list, breadcrumb bar), use the mouse wheel's left/right tilt.

  • Overlay scrollbar: The vertical scrollbar overlays the content (e.g., the Size column), so the file name column width remains stable even when the scrollbar appears. The thumb has a minimum size, so it never collapses into something you cannot grab, however many thousands of files a folder holds — the floor applies to every scrollbar in the app.

  • Top-bottom dual-pane split: The layout toggle button on the status bar supports a top-bottom split in addition to side-by-side. You can also switch to single-pane mode (shortcuts: Ctrl+Shift+Q single, Ctrl+Shift+W side-by-side, Ctrl+3 top-bottom; with the "Zenith 2" keymap, Ctrl+B followed by 1 / 2 / 3).

docs.title: Help & Document Viewer
docs.text:
You can open the app's help window (comprehensive document viewer) from the "Manual" icon on the right side of the main window's title bar.

The document viewer does not block the main window. You can keep it open and go on using the file list and the menus, so you can read a procedure and try it out at the same time. Its size and position are remembered, so once you park it on a second monitor or off to one side, that is where it opens next time. Choosing "Manual" or "Changelog" again while it is already open does not add a second window — the existing one comes to the front and switches to the tab you picked.

  • Comprehensive document viewer: A viewer that lets you switch between viewing "User Manual" and "Changelog" within a single window.

    Scroll positions are maintained independently for the manual and changelog, so switching tabs resumes from where you left off. - Top header: - The app name and document icon (BookOpen) are displayed on the left. - Two segment buttons, "Manual" and "Changelog," are in the center area; click to switch content. The selected mode is highlighted with the same accent color (blue) as the file list. - A keyword search box is on the right. Matches in the article on screen are highlighted, and Previous / Next step through them. In the manual, every article is searched at once: each article in the table of contents shows its number of matches, and articles with none are dimmed. Pressing Next after the last match of an article moves on to the next article that has matches. - The "X" button on the far right closes the window, just like the Esc key. - Left pane (Table of contents): - In manual mode, the list shows categories (such as "Screen Layout" and "Basic Operations") with their articles beneath. Choosing an article shows just that article on the right, and its headings unfold under it in the list. Choosing a category opens its first article. If you switch to the changelog and back, the article you were reading opens again. - In changelog mode, there is one heading per version (with its summary, where the version has one), newest first. - In both modes, clicking an item smoothly scrolls the right pane to the corresponding section, and the currently viewed section is automatically highlighted as you scroll through the body text. - The left pane width is adjustable via splitter, and the scrollbar is positioned on the right edge. The window and left pane are displayed large by default, making long headings less likely to be truncated. - Right pane (Body text): - A common Markdown-based rendering engine is used for both the manual and changelog, providing unified styling with a touch of blue accent color, table padding, kbd-like shortcut notation, line spacing, and bullet design. - "Added," "Changed," "Fixed," and other list items in the changelog also have the same readable line spacing and blue dots as the manual, delivering a consistent documentation experience. - Scroll to the end of an article and a "Next article" bar appears at the bottom. Keep turning the wheel down — there is no need to stop first — and the bar's gauge fills; when it is full the next article opens. Turning the wheel up at the top of an article shows a "Previous article" bar instead, and the same steps take you back to the end of the previous article. Clicking a bar works too. Right after a move, the wheel has to stop once before another move can start while you are still at an edge, so you will not skip straight through a short article or bounce back to the one you just left. On the keyboard, PageDown / Space at the end and PageUp / Shift+Space at the top do the same. - Clicking a link in the text takes you to the right place: a link to another article opens that article at the linked heading, and a link to a heading in the same article scrolls there. Web links (http / https) open in your default browser. Any other kind of link — to a local file or program, for example — is not opened. - Controls and shortcuts: - Press Esc or the "X" button on the header right side to close the window. - Manual/Changelog switching is done by mouse click (keyboard shortcuts do not interfere with those on the main window side). - The document viewer stays in front of the main window. You can click straight through to the app when you want to operate it; when it is in the way, move it aside or close it with Esc (it also closes together with the main window).

docs.title: Nav Pane
docs.text: The areas on either side of the file list that hold "views". Choose from about 20 views, such as Favorites, the tree, History and the terminal, put the ones you use in whichever slot you like, and call them up with a key.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
To do this Do this Switch views Click an icon in the icon bar, or use its key (see "The views" below) Show or hide a nav pane Ctrl + Shift + [ (left) / Ctrl + Shift + ] (right); with the "Zenith 2" keymap, Ctrl + B followed by [ / ] Stack two views Drag an icon to the top or bottom edge of the view area Move a view to the other side Drag its icon to the other icon bar, or to the window edge Rearrange everything at once ∨ at the right end of the icon bar → "Edit All Pane Slots", or a preset (Ctrl + Shift + J; Ctrl + B → N in Zenith 2) Put it in its own window The detach button

There is a nav pane on the left and on the right, and each can be split into a top and a bottom zone, so up to four slots can show different views. Out of the box, the left is a single tier showing Favorites, and its icon bar holds only the 7 views an ordinary file manager has (Favorites, Tree, History, Recent Files, Drives, Index Search and Properties); the right has Recent Files on top and Recent Folders below, but the right nav pane starts closed (open it with the right-nav button on the status bar).

docs.title: The views
docs.text:
View Zenith standard key Zenith 2 key What it does More Favorites Ctrl+Shift+1 Ctrl+K → F Register and open the folders and files you use often Favorites Tree Ctrl+Shift+2 Ctrl+K → T Browse drives and the folder hierarchy "Tree" below History Ctrl+Shift+3 Ctrl+K → H Look back at the folders you opened, by date "History" below Index Search Ctrl+Shift+4 Ctrl+K → I Manage the folders index search covers Index Settings Working Set Ctrl+Shift+5 Ctrl+K → W Save and recall combinations of tabs Working Sets Recent Folders Ctrl+Shift+6 Ctrl+K → Shift+R Your most-opened folders, most first "Recent folders and files" below Recent Files Ctrl+Shift+7 Ctrl+K → R Up to 100 files you opened "Recent folders and files" below Properties Ctrl+Shift+8 Ctrl+K → P Details of what you selected "Properties" below Terminal / Terminal 2 — Ctrl+K → C / Shift+C The built-in terminal Terminal Sites — Ctrl+K → N Register and open FTP and SFTP servers FTP/SFTP Search Presets / Search History — Ctrl+K → S / Shift+H Recall saved and past searches Search Presets Tab Management — Ctrl+K → L Reorder, move and close the A/B tabs in one place "Other views" below Preview — Ctrl+K → V Always show the selected file's contents "Other views" below Drives — Ctrl+K → D The list of drives — Macros — Ctrl+K → M Run a series of steps at once Macros AI Manual / AI Folder Analysis / AI Tab Management — Ctrl+K → / / O / Shift+L Ask the AI, or have it suggest how to tidy a folder or your tabs AI Features

A new installation uses the "Zenith 2" keymap (see Keyboard Shortcuts). You can change the keys in Settings → Shortcut Keys, including for views that have no key in the table.

App settings (Control Deck) open not from the nav pane but from the gear icon in the title bar (Ctrl + Shift + O). They open in their own window, which you can move and resize and which remembers its position. The main window is not dimmed behind it, so you can compare theme changes on the spot. Close it with Esc or × (see All App Settings).

docs.title: Switching views
docs.text:
• Icon bar: the icons of the views placed on a nav pane are lined up above it. Click one to switch to that view. When they do not all fit in the width of the nav pane, a ≫ appears at the right end. Click it to list the views that did not fit, and pick one to switch to it (the view being shown is highlighted). The lower icon bar works the same way. The ∨ next to it does not show more icons; it opens the menu for managing where views are placed.
  • Keys (Zenith 2): Ctrl + K followed by one key opens that view and moves the focus into it. Press the same keys again and the focus goes back to the file list, with the view left open. A hidden nav pane is shown, and a view that is on neither icon bar is added to the end of the left icon bar first. Opening a view from the Command Palette or the Ring Launcher works the same way.
  • Keys (Zenith standard): Ctrl + Shift + 1–8 switch the slot where that view is placed (see "How it works"); the focus stays in the file list. Pressing the key of a view placed on neither nav pane changes nothing.
  • Moving keyboard focus: F6 / Shift + F6 move keyboard input between the nav panes and Panes A and B.

Each view shows its name at the top, with that view's buttons (the tree lock, the button that clears History and so on) on the right of the heading. Views that use AI carry a purple AI badge, and Pro features an orange Pro badge (the badge dots are off at first; turn them on with Display → Show AI / Pro badges).

docs.title: Arranging views
docs.text:
• Stack two views: drag an icon and drop it on the top or bottom edge of the view area to put it in that zone. Drop it in the middle to remove the split. The top zone always keeps at least one view.
  • Swap sides: drag an icon to the other icon bar. If there is no right nav pane yet, dropping near the right edge of the window (within 60px) creates one.
  • Reorder: drag icons left or right within an icon bar.
  • Rearrange everything at once: ∨ at the right end of the icon bar → "Edit All Pane Slots" opens a cross-shaped layout window where you decide what goes in each of the four slots (see Presets).
  • Fit the bottom zone to its content (dock): the button at the right end of the bottom zone's heading fixes that zone to exactly the height of its content and gives the rest to the top zone. Handy for views with a set height, such as Properties.
  • Auto-hide: turn on "Auto-hide" for either side under General, and that nav pane hides when you are not using it and comes back when the mouse reaches the window edge (within 12px). It also comes back if the mouse rests for a second a little further in, within 32px of the edge. The pin in the heading keeps it out.

docs.title: Detaching and arranging windows
docs.text:
Detaching the nav pane (floating window): The detach button at the top right of the nav pane (left of the ∨) turns the nav pane into a standalone window. While it is detached, the space it occupied in the main window collapses, so the A and B panes get that width back. Move it to a second display and you can keep the nav pane in view without giving up any file-list space. The left and right nav panes detach independently, and a running terminal keeps its session across the move. The window's position and size are remembered, and if you quit with a pane detached, it comes back detached next time. To bring it back, press the button in the same spot in the detached window (its icon changes to a pane shape), or simply close the window. While a pane is detached, its show/hide toggle shows and hides that window instead.

How a detached window stacks: While a pane is detached, a stacking button appears next to the detach button. Click it to choose one of three options. The choice is shared by the left and right nav panes and is kept the next time you start the app.

Option What it does Always on top (above other apps) Stays in front of every other app's windows. It is minimized together with the main window In front of the main window (default) Always stays in front of the main window, and stacks with other apps like any other window Normal window (can go behind the main window) Can go behind the main window. It also appears on the taskbar so you can find it when it is hidden

The button's icon shows the current choice (a pin for always on top, stacked layers for in front of the main window, a crossed-out pin for a normal window).

Arranging them side by side (snapping and docking): A detached window snaps to screen edges and corners like a magnet, exactly as the main window does. Windows also snap to each other, so you can line up the left nav pane, the main window with its A and B panes, and the right nav pane with no gaps between them. Joining an edge lines up the top or bottom edges at the same time, so the row comes out even. Once windows are joined, dragging any one of them moves the whole set. To pull a single window out, hold Alt while dragging — a reminder appears on screen when you start moving a joined set. Snapping is controlled by Settings → General → "Snap window to screen edges". Crossing between displays with different scaling can leave a gap, since the windows change size as they go.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text: Ctrl + Shift + J (Ctrl + B → N in Zenith 2, or the nav pane layout presets at the bottom right of the status bar) switches the whole nav pane layout at once. Four are built in, Standard, Compact, Dual and Author's Layout. Standard is the same layout as when the app is first started (7 views on the left nav pane, shown as a single tier with Favorites; History, Recent Files and more are placed on the right nav pane, which starts closed); pick it to get back to the original layout from another preset. Open the right nav pane with the button at the bottom right of the status bar (or the key assigned to "Toggle Right Pane"). You can also save the current layout under a name. Presets cover only the arrangement and width of the views; they never touch your favorites.

docs.title: Tree
docs.text:
A view for browsing drives and the folder hierarchy. At the top level are the drives that are ready (those that answer within 0.5 seconds), devices such as phones and cameras, and finally the Recycle Bin.

Action What happens Click Selects only (nothing is shown in a pane) Click ▶/▼ Expands or collapses only (nothing is shown in a pane) Double-click the folder name / Enter Shows it in the active pane (the tree stays as it is) Ctrl + double-click Shows it in the other pane (switches to two panes if needed) Shift + click / Shift + Ctrl + click Shows it with large icons in the active / the other pane Right-click "Show in A Pane", "Show in B Pane", "Rename", "Delete" ("Refresh" on empty space)
  • Follows the current folder: while the tree is shown, it expands and selects the folder open in the active pane (also when you switch tabs).
  • Keeps up with file operations: folders created, renamed, moved or deleted in the app appear in the tree right away.
  • OneDrive: as in File Explorer, "OneDrive - Personal" and "OneDrive - " are listed at the top of the tree, above the drives. They cannot be renamed, deleted or dragged (dropping into them works).
  • Folder display names: folders such as "Documents" and "Downloads" are shown with Windows' display name for them, as in File Explorer (tab headers and the breadcrumb too). Renaming acts on the real name.
  • Quick access: shown at the very top of the tree (like Home in File Explorer's navigation pane). Expanding it lists the folders you pinned in File Explorer, in the same order (it is read only when expanded, so changes you make to the pins in File Explorer show up the next time you open it). Right-click a folder inside it for "Unpin from Quick access". Turn it off with "Show Quick access in the tree" in Settings (on by default).
  • Network: expanding it lists the computers on your network (read only when expanded, with a 15-second limit). Expanding a computer lists its shares, and picking one shows the share list in the pane. Toggle it with "Show Network in the tree" under Control Deck → "General" → "Nav pane" (shown by default).
  • Libraries: shown when "Show Libraries in the tree" is on (off by default, as in Windows 11's File Explorer). Expanding it lists Documents, Pictures, Music, Videos and other libraries, and picking one opens its default save location (for Documents, C:\Users\<name>\Documents). Dropping files on a library puts them in its default save location.
  • Quick access, Network, Libraries and the nodes under them cannot be renamed, deleted or dragged.
  • Recycle Bin: double-click, Enter or right-click "Open in Explorer" opens File Explorer's Recycle Bin (not in an app pane). It cannot be expanded, renamed, deleted or dragged.
  • Lock: the padlock in the heading stops moving by drag within the tree, renaming, deleting, and drops from the file list. If you try one of these, the status bar says it could not be done while locked and the area near the padlock flashes for about 3 seconds (no pop-up). Click the padlock to unlock at once. The lock is kept the next time you start the app, and is separate from the Favorites lock.
  • For the rules on dropping onto the tree, see Drag & Drop.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The folders you opened, grouped by date, newest first. Only today's group starts expanded, and groups you open or close yourself stay that way.

  • Double-click (or Enter) opens a folder in the active pane. Right-click offers "Show in A Pane", "Show in B Pane" and "Remove".
  • Typing in the search box removes the date grouping and filters the list: entries whose name or path contains what you typed, and names within one or two typos of it. Only the 50 newest entries loaded into the list are searched.
  • The trash button to the right of the heading clears the whole history (you are asked first).

docs.title: Recent folders and files
docs.text:
• Recent Folders: the 10 folders you opened most, most first (Name, Date, Count and ☆ columns). Folders on the exclusion list in General are left out. ☆ adds one to Favorites.
  • Recent Files: up to 100 files opened in Panes A and B. Sort by the column headings (Name, Opened, Count) and filter by name or path with the search box. Right-click offers "Open again", "Open containing folder" and "Show parent folder in A/B Pane". The heading's button clears the list (without asking).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• Properties view: The "Properties" drop item in the nav pane displays properties (full path, size, type, modified date, created date, attributes) for the selected file or folder in the A/B pane. For a single file it also shows what is inside on one line (dimensions, camera and date taken for images; for music, video and documents, whichever of dimensions, length, artist, album, year, title, authors, page count, tags and rating have values — like File Explorer's details pane; not read for online-only cloud files, network locations or slow locations).

    The full path field has a fixed 6-line height; longer paths can be scrolled. A copy button allows copying the path to the clipboard.

    Selecting a shortcut (.lnk) adds a "Target" field showing the target's full path, with its own copy button. A warning is shown if the target can no longer be found.

    When one file is selected, "Edit properties" appears below. It opens a window for the title, tags, rating, authors and comments (the same five fields as the Details tab of File Explorer's Properties). Tags and authors take several entries separated by ";", and the rating is 0 to 5 stars. The values are written into the file, so File Explorer and the Photos app see them too, and Ctrl+Z undoes a save. Only formats Windows can write properties to (JPEG, Office, MP3 and so on) are editable; for others, such as text files, the values are shown greyed out. Read-only, online-only (kept in the cloud) and network files are never written to. Editing happens in a window rather than in the pane itself because the pane follows the selection, and a change of selection while typing would throw the input away.

    When no item is selected, it automatically shows the active pane's current folder properties.

  • Startup greeting: For 5 seconds after launch, a time-based greeting message (6 patterns: morning, late morning, afternoon, etc.) is displayed, then fades out to show current folder properties.

  • AI greeting: Open settings via the gear icon in the Properties header and enable "Generate message with AI" to have AI create an original motivational message matching the time of day.

    The message is output in the language matching your app's language setting.

    While waiting for the AI response, "Preparing..." is shown, then the message smoothly fades in and displays for 5 seconds. - Greeting tone adjustment: Adjust the AI greeting tone across 7 levels (casual to formal). Configure this from the Overview tab in AI settings. - Settings are accessible from the gear icon in the Properties view header and are restored on next launch.

docs.title: Other views
docs.text:
• AI Folder Analysis: A view where AI analyzes the focused pane's current folder and suggests organization actions (folder creation, file moves, renames).
  • Analyze: Press the "Analyze" button to send all items in the folder (name, type, size, date) to AI for organization suggestions. You can also type additional instructions (e.g., "organize photos by year and month") in the text input.
  • Proposed Actions: AI proposals are displayed as a checklist. Three action types are available: folder creation, file move, and rename, each individually selectable. The "Select All" button toggles all at once.
  • Execute: Press "Execute" to batch-execute selected actions. A confirmation dialog appears before execution, and the glow bar on the status bar shows progress.
  • Undo: Executed operations can be undone all at once with Undo (Ctrl+Z).
  • Safety: Validates that paths are within the current folder, checks for name conflicts at destinations, and verifies the folder path matches between analysis and execution time.

  • AI Manual: A chat-style help view where you can ask questions about the app in natural language.

    Answers are generated by automatically searching the manual. Responses are rendered in Markdown (headings, bold, bullet lists, code blocks), and long answers are split into multiple bubbles by section. Beneath each answer, the articles it drew on are listed; clicking one opens that article in the manual.

    Retains conversation history (last 3 exchanges). Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day).

  • AI Tab Management: A view that scores tab usage patterns (access frequency, dwell time, recency) and suggests tab organization.

    Visualizes each tab's status with lock recommendation (green indicator) / close recommendation (orange indicator). "Apply all" enables batch operations.

    Also performs working set auto-detection (A+B pane co-occurrence patterns) and related folder suggestions (detected from co-occurrence history). Each suggestion type can be individually toggled ON/OFF. Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day).

  • Tab List View: Lists all tabs from Pane A and Pane B, with drag-and-drop reordering.

    Tab activity (time spent) is visualized with progress bars, and AI-recommended tabs are marked with dot indicators. If the current tab layout matches a saved working set, a badge is displayed and you can save it with one click.

    In single-pane mode, only the tabs of the pane on screen (A or B) are shown. Each pane header includes a + button for creating new tabs. Double-clicking empty space in a list adds a tab to that pane as well — the same gesture the pane tab bars use. Tabs can also be closed with a middle click.

    Tabs can also be dragged from the pane tab bars into the Tab List view for reordering and cross-pane moves. You can drop folders from Explorer or the nav pane (favorites, history, frequent folders, tree) to create new tabs. - Preview View: A persistent preview pane for the currently selected file. Supports images, text, PDF (first page), SVG, and video thumbnails. Code files and Markdown are shown as text with syntax highlighting (for formatted Markdown, use the Space quick preview). Online-only cloud PDFs and large PDFs on slow locations are not drawn; only the file information is shown. For image files, the dimensions, camera and date taken appear in the Properties view.

docs.title: Where a view appears when you call it by key
docs.text:
• Views are looked up left, then right, and shown in the zone (top or bottom) where they are placed on the side where they are found. With the Zenith standard keys Ctrl + Shift + 1–8, a view that is already showing in a slot stays in that slot.
  • If a view is placed on neither side: the Zenith standard keys change nothing (the diagram above). Zenith 2's Ctrl + K, the Command Palette and the Ring Launcher add it to the end of the left icon bar and open it.
  • A view appears in only one place at a time. If the same view is placed on both sides and you open it on the side where it is not showing, it moves there and the other slot is left empty. Terminals are the exception: each side has its own terminal, and "Terminal 2" lets a side show one on top and one below (up to four in all).
  • While the nav pane is hidden: the Zenith standard keys Ctrl + Shift + 1–8 do not bring it back (use Ctrl + Shift + [ / ]). Zenith 2's Ctrl + K shows the hidden nav pane and opens the view.

docs.title: When views are created
docs.text:
• Only five views are created at startup: Favorites, Tree, History, Index Search and Properties.
  • The others are created one at a time once the window is up and the app is idle, so startup stays fast. Terminals and Sites are created the first time you open them.
  • A list's contents (History, Recent Folders and so on) are reloaded the first time it is shown or after they change; several changes in quick succession are combined into one reload within 0.5 seconds.

docs.title: How the history is kept
docs.text:
• Every time you open a folder, how many times and when you opened it are recorded. Back / Forward and reloading search results do not count.
  • The history is tidied at most once a day: entries older than a month, broken paths that can't be opened, and anything beyond the 500 newest are removed.
  • The same record feeds Recent Folders and the ranking of the Favorites "Frequent" section. Clearing the history empties those too, for the time being.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Favorites — the Favorites view
  • Terminal — the terminal view
  • Presets — deciding the nav pane layout at once
  • Navigation — moving around in a pane
  • Drag & Drop — dropping onto the tree and Favorites

docs.title: Status Bar
docs.text:
The area at the bottom of the screen displays the following information and allows setting changes.

  • Notification messages (center): When operations such as file copy, move, or favorites registration are completed, a message fades in at the center. By default it disappears after 3 seconds; change this with General → Display Duration in the Control Deck (Short 1.5s, Standard 3s, Long 5s).
  • Window placement controls: Buttons on the left end of the status bar let you quickly change window placement. From left to right:
  • Snap bottom-left: Snaps the window to the bottom-left quarter of the screen.
  • Snap left: Snaps the window to the left half of the screen.
  • Maximize: Expands the window to fill the screen (press again to restore original size).
  • Snap bottom half: Snaps the window to the bottom half of the screen.
  • Snap right: Snaps the window to the right half of the screen.
  • Snap bottom-right: Snaps the window to the bottom-right quarter of the screen.
  • Window Position Presets: the button to their right (Ctrl + Shift + L; Ctrl + B → L in Zenith 2) saves the current window position and size under a name and brings it back later.

  • Behavior when dragging out of maximized state: When dragging the title bar to undock from maximized state, the window resizes to the previous normal size if available, or to approximately 75% of the current display's work area width with a roughly 16:10 aspect ratio.

    The window position is adjusted so the mouse cursor is near the horizontal center of the title bar, allowing seamless continued dragging.

  • Automatic rescue in multi-display environments: Zenith Filer detects when the display configuration differs from the previous session.

    If the saved window position does not intersect any currently connected display, it is determined to be "off-screen" and the window is automatically repositioned to the center of the main display's work area at an appropriate size.

    You never need to use Alt+Space+M to find the window, whether transitioning from a 3-monitor home setup to a 2-monitor office or a single-monitor cafe.

    This also applies while the app is running: unplugging an external display is detected automatically, and the window is restored to the main display, maximized. If the disconnect event is ever missed (e.g., right after resuming from sleep), the same off-screen check runs again the next time the window becomes active — so at worst, simply clicking the taskbar icon brings it back. - Item information: Displays the number of currently selected files and the total file size. - Screen split: three buttons on the right of the status bar (Single pane, Dual pane and Dual pane (vertical)) switch between one pane, two panes side by side and two panes one above the other. The button for the current layout is highlighted. When you switch to single-pane, the pane you were working in (A or B) stays on screen. The default is single-pane mode with Pane A (switch to dual-pane to move files between Pane A and Pane B or compare them side by side). The keys are Ctrl + Shift + Q / W and Ctrl + 3 (Ctrl + B followed by 1 / 2 / 3 in Zenith 2). - Nav pane visibility toggle: Left and right nav panes can be independently shown or hidden with the left-nav and right-nav toggle buttons on the status bar. The right nav pane starts closed, so open it with the right-nav button. When hidden, the file panes expand to fill the freed space. - Nav pane layout presets: the button to their right (Ctrl + Shift + J; Ctrl + B → N in Zenith 2) switches the whole nav pane layout at once (see Nav Pane). - Working sets: the folder button lists your saved working sets so you can bring one back (Ctrl + Shift + S; Ctrl + B → W in Zenith 2; see Working Sets). - Macros: the circle button starts recording a macro and stops it when pressed again; the lightning button runs a saved macro (see Macros). - AI on/off: the sparkle button turns the AI features on or off. Long-press it to open the AI settings. - Progress indicator types: Zenith Filer uses 3 types of progress indicators depending on the nature of the operation. - Spinner: A small rotating animation on the right side of the status bar (to the left of the log folder button). Displayed during general async operations with indeterminate duration, such as file search, loading, and CSV export scanning. - Scan bar: A horizontally expanding line at the very top of the status bar. Accompanied by status messages like "[CSV Export Preparing] Physically scanning folder for latest information..." and displayed during large-scale scans where completion time is unpredictable. May appear simultaneously with the spinner. - GlowBar: A thin glowing progress bar (accent color + cyan glow) displayed at the very top of the status bar during file copy and move operations. Reflects progress in real time based on byte and item counts. During copy, a single status line below the bar shows the file count, transfer speed, ETA, and current file name, e.g. "Copying 120 / 500... — 85.3 MB/s — ETA 0:42 — photo_2026.jpg" (the ETA appears starting 2 seconds after the copy begins). When canceled, the bar rapidly accelerates back from its current position to 0% with a "vacuum" effect (reverse animation) before fading out.

  • Indexing indicator: During index creation, a progress message ("Updating index: XX items") with a rotating animation is displayed on the right side of the status bar.

    Separate from the general loading indicator, a dedicated progress display appears during creation. If resumed after interruption, the count continues from the previously registered number, making it clear that processing was resumed partway.

    Clicking this icon displays a confirmation dialog; selecting "Yes" cancels the index creation.

    After restarting the app, incomplete indexes for registered folders are automatically resumed. When creation completes, the status bar shows "Added XX items to index."

  • Always on top: Click the pin icon to keep the window always in front of other windows.

    Popups opened from the app (rename input, manual, changelog, etc.) still appear in front of the main window when pinned.

  • Log folder: the document button opens the log folder. Long-press it to view today's log.

  • View mode toggle: In each pane's toolbar (icon group above the address bar), to the left of "Sort by", there are buttons for Details and three icon sizes (small, medium, large). With the "Fewer" toolbar the small-icon button is hidden; set "Number of buttons" to "Standard" under Settings → Toolbar to show it.

    • Details: Clicking switches to the detailed list (columns for Name, Date Modified, Type, Size, etc.).
    • Small / Medium / Large icons: Clicking switches icon display size; the selected mode is highlighted. The three buttons act as presets that snap back to a familiar size - if Ctrl+wheel has left you somewhere in between, pressing one returns you to that step.
    • Fine-tuning the size (Ctrl+wheel): Hold Ctrl and turn the mouse wheel over the file list to resize icons steplessly (15 steps from 32 to 256 pixels) - up to 2.6x what "large icons" used to be.
      • The other view modes are part of the same range (in File Explorer's order). Scrolling down past the smallest icons goes to List → Details → Tiles → Content, and scrolling up goes back the other way (the step after List is the smallest icons), so you can move between them without reaching for a button.
    • List, Tiles and Content (the same three as File Explorer): choose them from the empty-space right-click "View ▶". Their toolbar buttons are hidden by default and can be shown from the toolbar settings. List shows small icons with names in columns that grow to the right (horizontal scrolling; ↑↓ step through the items in order, so ↓ at the bottom of a column goes to the top of the next and ↑ at the top goes to the bottom of the previous; ←→ move to the neighbouring column). Tiles shows a medium icon with name, type and size beside it, packed side by side. Content shows one item per row with the name in bold and the type, and the date modified and size on the right (←→ switch panes). Tiles and Content show picture thumbnails too. Selection, range selection, renaming and dragging work as in icon views, and the mode is remembered per folder and in working sets.
      • The size is remembered per pane and per folder - photo folders extra large, document folders small, and it survives a restart (the per-folder memory applies when "Restore per-folder view settings" is enabled). Working sets store it too.
    • Icon mode layout: Explorer-like layout with clear size differences, comfortable margins from pane edges. Items are packed together with whitespace collected at the right edge. Text is normal size; long names are truncated with "...".
    • Non-image items (folders, documents): Fixed card height with icons and file names aligned. File names up to 4 lines, rest truncated.
    • Image and video files (jpg, png, gif, bmp, webp / mp4, mkv, avi, mov, wmv, etc.): The thumbnail sits at the top of the card at its original aspect ratio so the whole picture is visible, with the file name always shown below it (the same arrangement as folder and document cards). Names wrap onto up to 4 lines and are elided beyond that. Size and modification time appear on hover. The full file name appears as a tooltip after ~2 seconds. Thumbnails are fetched for the rows in view first and re-evaluated as you scroll or resize, with no per-folder cap. Files already downloaded from OneDrive and similar services are included (online-only files are skipped so as not to trigger a download).
    • Documents and folder contents: PDFs, Office documents and any other format whose thumbnail provider is installed in Windows show their content too (as in File Explorer); documents that return no image (such as Office files saved without a preview) appear as a large icon. In Large and Extra large icons, folders holding pictures show a peek at their contents (as in File Explorer), except in OneDrive, Box, network and slow locations. Turn this off with "Show folder contents as thumbnails" under Control Deck → "Display" → "File list" (on by default).
    • Shortcut arrows and app marks: shortcuts get the arrow at large sizes too. Overlay marks that apps such as Git and Dropbox put on icons appear on the visible items shortly after a folder opens when "Show app marks on icons" is turned on on the same page: on the small icon in Details and List, and at the lower left of the large icon or thumbnail in icon views, Tiles and Content (off by default because it asks Windows about each item; local locations only; turning it off removes the marks straight away).
    • Folders and files without a thumbnail (documents, etc., including videos whose format your PC has no playback support for): Icon at top (no border), file name always shown at a fixed position below. A high-resolution icon is fetched from Windows, so these stay sharp at large sizes (each distinct icon is fetched only once, so nothing gets slower).
    • Layout density: Few files are packed from the top with the same density as many files.
    • Selection: Only the card (thumbnail + name) is clickable; whitespace outside does not select.
    • Keyboard ops in icon view: The same keys work as in detail view. Arrow keys move the selection, Enter opens, Backspace goes to the parent folder, Delete deletes, F2 renames, F5 refreshes, and type-ahead search works too - all on the same bindings as detail view. The one difference is Left / Right, which move the selection sideways rather than between panes (use F6 for that, or also Tab with the "Zenith standard" keymap).
    • Persistence: View mode and icon size persist across restarts, saved independently per A/B pane (e.g., if Pane A is list and Pane B is icon, both reopen in the same state). New tabs inherit the pane's view mode.

  • Tooltips: Hovering over buttons and icons displays a tooltip concisely describing the action performed by clicking. For buttons whose state changes (lock, pin, view toggle, etc.), the tooltip text dynamically updates to reflect the current state.

docs.title: Title Bar
docs.text:
The main window's title bar displays the app name and version, followed by the full path of the folder in the currently focused pane (e.g., Zenith Filer - C:\Users\...\Desktop).

When the path is empty or immediately after startup, only the app name and version are shown. Switching to the other pane also changes the displayed path. To leave the path out, turn off Display → Show folder path in title bar in the Control Deck (only the app name and version remain).

  • Level Banner: Your level (Lv.), calculated from challenge XP, is shown in the title bar.

    Click it to open the challenge page. It is off at first; turn it on with Display → Show level banner in header bar in the Control Deck. When you level up, the banner pulses with an accent-colored glow effect.

  • Epithet Banner: AI-generated epithets earned through challenges are displayed in the title bar.

    Hover to see the backstory tooltip. Click to open the epithet history directly. It is off at first; turn it on with Display → Show challenge title banner in header in the Control Deck.

    When a challenge is completed, the epithet banner also pulses with an accent-colored glow effect.

  • Icon Hover Color: Title bar icon buttons (settings, manual, etc.) change to a theme-aware color on hover.

  • Snap Layouts: Hover over the maximize button at the right end to bring up Windows 11 Snap Layouts (the picker for arranging the window on screen). Pick a spot and the window fits into it. Clicking the button still maximizes or restores the window as before.

    To turn the picker off, use Windows Settings > System > Multitasking > Snap windows. It does not appear on Windows 10. To move the window to a fixed position in one click, you can also use the window layout buttons on the status bar.

  • Icon buttons on the right: from left to right:

    Button What it does Gear Opens the app settings (Control Deck) (Ctrl + Shift + O) ☰ Opens the Command Palette (Ctrl + Shift + P), where you can find and run any action by name Book Opens the manual (see Help & Document Viewer) Robot speech bubble Opens the AI Manual Scroll Opens the changelog Trophy Opens Challenges Speech bubble Opens the feedback page in the Control Deck

  • Window Recovery Menu: The title bar system menu (right-click) includes "Move to main monitor" and "Move to current monitor" options. Use these to recover the window when it moves off-screen.

    The same options are available from the taskbar right-click JumpList and the tray icon menu.

docs.title: Address Bar and Breadcrumb
docs.text: The bar that shows where you are and takes you somewhere else with a click or by typing. For Back, Forward, Up and the PC view, see Navigation.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
To do this Do this Jump several levels up at once Click a folder name in the breadcrumb Go to a sibling folder Click the "›" after a folder name and pick from the list Go somewhere by typing Click the location icon on the left, click an empty part of the bar, or press Ctrl + L (or Alt + D), then type a path and press Enter Open a server or a web page Type sftp://…, https://… and so on, then press Enter See what kind of place you are in The icon on the left (local, network, Box, cloud, remote, device, inside an archive) Send files up the tree Drop them on a folder name in the breadcrumb Keep the current location ★ adds it to Favorites; the copy button puts the path on the clipboard

The address bar is the bottom row of the pane header. Normally it shows where you are as a breadcrumb (one button per level), and it turns into a text box only when you want to type.

docs.title: The location icon on the left
docs.text:
The left end of the bar shows an icon for where the current folder is: a local drive, a network share, Box Drive, the cloud (Box on the web, SharePoint / OneDrive), a remote server (FTP / SFTP), a device such as a phone or camera, or the inside of an archive (read-only). Hover over it to see the name of the place. Everything in a folder is in the same place, so it is shown once here instead of as a column in the list (search results mix files from different places, so they keep a Location column).

The same icon is also the button that switches between the text box and the breadcrumb (see "Typing a path" below).

docs.title: Moving with the breadcrumb
docs.text:
• Click a folder name to go to that level. The "PC" at the start takes you to the PC view.

  • Click "›" to list the folders inside that folder, then pick one to go there. The "›" points down while the list is open. The list stays open when you move the mouse away; it closes when you click outside it, press Esc, click the same "›" again, or pick a folder (as in File Explorer). Clicking another "›" while a list is open switches to that list. The last level (the folder you are in) has no "›".

    The "›" after "PC" lists your drives, with the same names as the PC view (such as "OS (C:)"). - Long paths: when the path does not fit, the bar keeps the current folder (the right end) in view and lets the leading levels slide off to the left. When levels are hidden, a "«" button appears at the left end of the bar. Press it to list the hidden levels ("PC", "OS (C:)", "Users" and so on) and pick one to go there, as in File Explorer. You can also turn the mouse wheel over the breadcrumb to slide it sideways (up moves toward the upper levels). A very long folder name is cut off with "…". - Hover over a folder name: its path appears, so you can match Windows display names (on some systems C:\Users is shown in the system language) to the actual path.

docs.title: Typing a path
docs.text:
1. Switch to the text box in any of these ways. The whole path is selected, so you can press Ctrl + C to copy it or just type over it.

    • Click the location icon on the left
    • Click an empty part of the bar (anywhere that is not a folder name)
    • Press Ctrl + L or Alt + D (the default keys; change them in Settings → Shortcut Keys)

  2. Type a path and press Enter to go there.

  3. To go back to the breadcrumb, click the location icon on the left again, or press Esc in the text box. If you go back without pressing Enter, whatever you had typed is dropped and the bar shows the current location again.

While the text box is on, the icon on the left looks pressed in. Moving the mouse off the address bar keeps the text box, so you can go and copy a file name from the list and come back to paste it. If you prefer typing, you can leave it switched on. Each pane (A and B) remembers whether it shows the text box or the breadcrumb, including the next time you start the app.

docs.title: What you can type
docs.text:
Type Example Result A folder path C:\Users\Public, D: Opens the folder (D: is treated as D:\) A network share \\server\share\folder Opens the folder A path relative to the current folder .., ..\docs, .\img, img, \temp Opens it, counted from the current folder (.. is one level up, a bare folder name is inside the current folder, and a leading \ starts from the root of the current drive) A path with environment variables %USERPROFILE%\Desktop Expands them and opens the folder PC PC Opens the PC view A remote server sftp://user@host/var/www, ftp://…, ftps://… Opens the folder on the server (see FTP/SFTP) A web address https://example.com, 192.168.1.1 Opens it in your default browser A shell name shell:startup, shell:Downloads Opens that folder (places with no folder on disk, such as the Recycle Bin, open in File Explorer) A command name cmd, wt, powershell, pwsh Starts it in the current folder (the address bar goes back to showing the current folder) A file path C:\Users\Public\memo.txt Opens the file in its associated app (you stay where you are rather than going to the file's folder)
  • Web addresses: anything starting with https:// or http:// goes to your default browser. A bare IP address such as 192.168.1.1, as used for router or NAS admin pages, works too: http:// is added for you (it also works with a port such as 192.168.1.1:8080 or a path such as 192.168.1.1/admin). Nothing is added to the history, and the address bar goes back to showing the current folder.
  • Command names: if the current folder contains a folder with the same name (say, a folder called cmd), that folder opens instead. Nothing starts in places with no folder on disk, such as the PC view or a remote server.
  • What does not open: a bare host name such as example.com (it cannot be told apart from a folder with the same name, so add https://).
  • When the folder is not found: you stay where you are and a "Folder not found" notification appears. What you typed stays in the box, so you can fix the typo and press Enter again.
  • Server suggestions: after 3 characters, up to 8 of your registered remote servers whose name, host or address contains what you typed appear under the box. Press ↓ to move into the list, then Enter or a click to open that server.

docs.title: Dropping files on the breadcrumb
docs.text:
Drag files or folders selected in the file list onto a folder name in the breadcrumb and release them to copy or move them into that folder.

  • Left-drag with no key held: moves within the same drive, copies to another drive or a server
  • Hold Ctrl to copy; hold Shift to move
  • Right-drag: when you release, a menu offers "Copy here", "Move here" and "Create shortcut here"

Dropping an Outlook email saves it as a file, and dropping an address from a browser creates a .url shortcut. See Drag & Drop for the details.

docs.title: ★ and copying the path
docs.text:
• ★ (add to Favorites) opens a dialog to add the current folder to Favorites. Enter a name and an optional description; once it is added, the nav pane switches to the Favorites view and briefly highlights the new entry. This works even while the Favorites view is locked. If the folder is already there, the ★ turns red and a short message next to it tells you it could not be added.
  • The copy button copies the current folder's path to the clipboard and shows a notification. In the PC view it copies "PC" (typing "PC" in the address bar takes you back there).

docs.title: Where typed text goes
docs.text:
When you press Enter, the text is checked in this order, and the first match wins.

  1. Remote? If the part before :// is sftp, ftp or ftps (in any letter case), it opens as a folder on that server. If the server is not registered yet, the registration screen opens, pre-filled with what you typed. If the address cannot be read (an invalid port, a missing host and so on), a notification tells you why. Addresses with a password in them (user:pass@host) are refused: addresses are kept for tab restore and in the history, so the password lives, encrypted, in the connection settings instead.
  2. Web address? Anything starting with http:// or https:// that has a host, and IPv4 addresses such as 192.168.1.1. An IP address counts only if all four numbers are between 0 and 255, and leading zeros such as 192.168.01.1 are refused (some software reads them as octal, which could take you somewhere you did not mean to go). The browser is started on a background thread, so a slow browser launch never freezes the window.
  3. Anything else is a folder. Before opening it, the app checks that the folder exists and stops only when it is confirmed missing, telling you the folder was not found (opening from Favorites or the history does not show this notification). The check waits at most 2 seconds (0.3 seconds for network folders); if there is no answer by then, it tries to open the folder anyway, so a slow network folder is never blocked just because the check timed out.

Folder paths are tidied up before opening: D: becomes D:\, and a trailing \ is removed (except at a drive root).

docs.title: How the breadcrumb is built
docs.text:
The breadcrumb is rebuilt on a background thread each time you move. What comes first depends on the kind of location.

Location Breadcrumb On a drive PC › OS (C:) › Users › … A network share \\server › share › … (no PC at the start) A remote server user@host › var › www … (click the first one to go to the top of the server) A phone or camera PC › device name › Internal storage › … Inside an archive PC › OS (C:) › … › archive file name › folder inside the archive › … (click the archive file name to go to the top of the archive)

Each name comes from Windows, the same one File Explorer shows (drive labels such as "OS (C:)" included). If Windows cannot supply a name, the parts of the path split at \ are shown instead.

docs.title: The "›" list
docs.text:
• The list is built on a background thread when you click "›", by reading that folder. It is sorted by name (ignoring letter case) and has no size limit.
  • Folders that cannot be read are left out. Hidden folders appear only when Display → Show hidden files and folders is turned on in Settings. Folders Windows protects (with both the hidden and system attributes) stay out while "Hide protected operating system files" on the same page is on (the default).
  • Inside an archive, "›" lists the folders in it too.
  • For remote servers, phones and cameras, and a bare \\server, the folder cannot be read this way, so clicking "›" opens nothing.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Navigation — Back, Forward, Up, the PC view, and moving to and from File Explorer
  • Favorites — organize the folders you added with ★
  • Drag & Drop — the copy and move rules
  • FTP/SFTP — register remote servers
  • File Panes — the other rows of the pane header (buttons and search)

docs.title: Batch Rename
docs.text:
Renames the selected files and folders in one pass according to a set of rules. There are three ways to open it.

Entry point Action Context menu Right-click the selection → "Batch Rename" Shortcut Shift+F2 (rebindable in the key binding settings) Toolbar The "Batch Rename" button in the toolbar at the top of the pane. It is not shown when the toolbar is set to "Fewer" buttons (the default for a new installation); choose "Standard" under Settings → "Toolbar" to show it (available in the free version too)

All three require at least one item to be selected. The free version allows three uses a day. The main window is disabled while the batch rename window is open, so the selection can never change out from under you while you are composing the rules.

docs.title: Top: rename mask
docs.text:
This field defines the skeleton of the new name. Left empty, the original name is used as-is. The buttons insert variables for you.

Variable Meaning $N Original name without the extension $N2-5 / $N2- Characters 2-5 / from character 2 onward of the original name $E Extension, without the dot $P / $G Parent folder name / the folder one level above that ${} Counter. Tunable per occurrence as ${start=10;increment=2;padding=3} $YYYY $YY $MMMM $MMM $MM $M Year and month ($MMMM and $MMM are month names, which follow the Windows region settings rather than the app's display language) $DDDD $DDD $DD $D Day-of-week name and day (day names also follow the Windows region settings) $hh $h $mm $m $ss $s Hour, minute, second (24-hour clock) $$ A literal $

The notation follows PowerToys PowerRename, the Windows-standard tool. Date variables read the modified timestamp by default; the dropdown switches them to the creation timestamp.

Below the buttons sits an always-visible legend of the variables, and under that a worked example using the files you actually selected (e.g. report.txt → report_20260813.txt). You can build the mask while watching what it really does, without having to remember what each symbol means.

docs.title: Middle: search / replace and options
docs.text:
• Use regular expressions: interprets the search field as a regular expression. The replace field accepts back-references $1, $2 (for example (\d{4})(\d{2})(\d{2}) → $1-$2-$3). While the expression is invalid, an error appears under the field and the preview is not updated

    Ticking it reveals pattern insert buttons and a legend underneath. \d+ (one or more digits), \s+ (whitespace), .* (any sequence), ( ) (group), ^ (start), $ (end) and \. (a literal dot) go into the search field; $1, $2, $3 go into the replace field. The legend is always visible, so you never have to hover to remember what a symbol means.

    On top of that, the "before" column of the preview highlights whatever the search matched. You can see at a glance why you got the result you did, which is what you need when a pattern is not behaving as expected. (No highlight is shown when a mask is also in use, since the search then no longer operates on the original name.) - Replace all matches: turn it off to replace only the first occurrence - Match case - Apply to: name only (default) / extension only / name and extension. The mask, the search-and-replace, and the case conversion all operate on this range. Folders are never split at a dot, so a name like v1.2 stays intact - Letter case: no change / lowercase / UPPERCASE / sentence case / Title Case - Counter: default start, step and digit count. Each ${} can override them individually - Include: toggles whether files and folders are each included

docs.title: Bottom: before → after preview
docs.text:
Check the outcome line by line before anything runs.

  • Clear the checkbox on the left to exclude that row individually (excluded rows do not consume a counter value)
  • "Show changed only" hides the rows that stay the same
  • Rows whose names would collide, that contain characters Windows cannot use, a reserved name (CON, NUL, …), or a trailing dot or space, whose path would be too long, or that clash with an existing item outside the selection, are shown in red with the reason in a tooltip
  • The execute button stays disabled while even one problem remains

The counts (selected / changed / issues) are shown at the bottom right. The preview is recalculated in the background as you type, so operations never stall however many items are selected.

docs.title: Executing and undoing
docs.text:
• Swaps such as a → b, b → a do not break — a temporary name is used internally
  • If one item fails part way through, the rest still run and the resulting counts are reported
  • Afterwards, a single Ctrl+Z reverts the entire batch

docs.title: Presets
docs.text: Save a rule set under a name and recall it later. The save button asks for a name; picking an entry from the dropdown at the bottom left loads it into the fields. Saving under an existing name overwrites it. To remove a preset you no longer need, select it and press the trash button.

docs.title: Command Palette
docs.text:
Find and run any action by name. Open it with Ctrl+Shift+P or the ≡ button at the right of the title bar.

It serves the purpose of the menu bar at the top of a conventional file manager, but occupies no screen space at all.

  • It reaches actions that have no key bound. Shortcuts mean "the common actions have keys", not "every action can be reached from the keyboard". Through the palette, every action is reachable by name regardless.
  • Everything is listed under group headings (global / window / tab / search / sidebar / file list and so on). Your saved macros are listed too, under "Macros", and can be run from here.
  • The filter works from the action name, its description, or the key. "copy" finds it, and so does Ctrl+C (the + is optional).
  • The current binding is shown at the right of each row, so using the palette teaches you the shortcuts. Actions with no binding show no badge.
  • Controls: Up / Down to select, Enter to run, Esc to close. Double-clicking a row runs it too. Clicking outside the palette (on the main window) closes it without running anything.
  • Pane-dependent actions apply to whichever pane was active when the palette opened.

docs.title: Right-Click Menu
docs.text: The menu that opens when you right-click in the file list. There are two kinds: the app's own lightweight menu and the standard Windows menu (Explorer-compatible). From the app's own menu you can also reach the items Windows and cloud apps add.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
To do this Do this Pick a common action right away Right-click (the app's own menu) Show the standard Windows menu Shift + right-click Open the menu from the keyboard The Menu (Application) key, or Shift + F10 Use items that 7-Zip, VS Code and others add "OS standard menu ▶" in the app's own menu Get Box or SharePoint links "Copy share link with path" and "Cloud Menu ▶" in the app's own menu Sort or create new items Right-click an empty part of the list

The app's own menu shows items to match the kind and number of things you selected. Actions with a key assigned show it on the right (for example "Copy Ctrl+C"). If you change a key in Settings → Shortcuts, the menu follows.

docs.title: Choosing between the two menus
docs.text:
• The app's own menu (the default, recommended): a lightweight menu of the common actions that opens the instant you right-click.
  • The Explorer-compatible menu: the standard Windows right-click menu, as is. Items that shell extensions (such as 7-Zip) add to File Explorer appear too.

Choose the one you use normally in General → Context Menu. Even with the app's own menu selected, you can bring up the Explorer-compatible menu for the moment:

  • Hold Shift while right-clicking (or while pressing the Menu key)
  • Choose "Show Explorer context menu" at the bottom of the app's own menu

The Explorer-compatible menu can only be shown for items in one folder (that is how the Windows menu works). If your selection spans several folders, as it can in search results, you are told so and the app's own menu is shown instead.

From the keyboard: the Menu key (changeable in Settings → Shortcuts) or Shift + F10 opens the menu at the bottom-left of the selected row, or at the top-left of the list if nothing is selected.

docs.title: Right-clicking files and folders
docs.text:
The menu is divided by separators into the groups below. Common actions are on the first level; less frequent ones are under "More actions ▶".

Group Item Shown when Open Open (Enter) Always (not with several items selected) Open in new tab / Open in other pane One folder is selected Open in text editor Only text-like files are selected Compare Text (in A pane) Two text-like files are selected Compare Text (A ↔ B pane) One text-like file is selected, and one text-like file is selected in the other pane too Open in painter Only images are selected Clipboard Copy (Ctrl+C), Cut (Ctrl+X), Paste (Ctrl+V) Always Edit Delete (Delete) Always Rename (F2) One item is selected Batch Rename (Shift+F2), Batch timestamp and attributes Always Change permissions Only items on a server (FTP / SFTP) are selected Archive ▶ Always (see "Archive ▶" below) Names and paths Copy file name / Copy full path (Ctrl+Shift+C) Always; one per line for several items. Full paths are each wrapped in double quotes (like File Explorer's "Copy as path") More actions ▶ (see the table below) System Recount size A folder is selected (not shown where the contents cannot be walked, such as a server). Recounts only the selected folders (F5 recounts the whole list) Properties (Alt+Enter) Always; with several items, shows combined properties Copy share link with path / Cloud Menu ▶ Always; disabled outside Box, SharePoint and OneDrive (work or school) folders OS standard menu ▶ Always (see "OS standard menu ▶" below) Go Quick Jump (Ctrl+P) / Show Explorer context menu Always

Where Paste goes: right-click a single folder and choose Paste, and the items go into that folder (as in Explorer). Right-clicking a file or several items, and Ctrl+V, paste into the folder you are viewing. If the cut items are already in the destination, nothing is moved; you get a notice and the items stay cut.

"More actions ▶" contains:

Item Shown when Copy BOX share path Inside a Box folder Add to favorites (Ctrl+D) / Remove from favorites One item is selected Create shortcut Always Compute and verify hash Files are selected Search this folder with index search / Export folder tree to CSV / to Excel / Set this folder as A or B Pane home One folder is selected Convert to PDF and save to same folder One convertible file is selected Convert to PDF, merge and save to same folder Several files, all convertible, are selected Send selection to Claude / Insert selection paths into the terminal Always

Features that have reached their limit in the free version show a padlock and "(limit reached)", and cannot be clicked.

docs.title: Right-clicking an empty part of the list
docs.text:
Right-clicking an empty part of the list shows a menu for the folder you are looking at.

  1. View ▶: large icons, medium icons, small icons, list, details, tiles or content, plus switches for showing hidden files and folders and showing file name extensions (the same as File Explorer's View menu). Hidden items are shown semi-transparent. Except in search tabs, Optimize this folder for ▶ underneath (General items, Documents, Pictures, Music, Videos) picks the folder's view template, like "Customize" in File Explorer's folder properties. Sort by ▶: name, date modified, type, size, extension or date created, ascending or descending, and "Show folders first". The icon views have no column headers, so this is where you sort them (the toolbar's sort button opens the same menu). Group by ▶: (None), name, date modified, size or type. "Collapse all groups" and "Expand all groups" can only be used while group header bands are shown (in the details view). Refresh (F5) Select ▶: Select all (Ctrl+A), Invert selection, Select none
  2. Paste / Paste shortcut (creates shortcuts here to the files and folders you copied; shown only when the clipboard holds files) / Undo (action name) (Ctrl+Z; greyed out when there is nothing to undo)
  3. Copy full path
  4. New folder (Ctrl+Shift+N) / New text file / New ▶: you name the new item right away, and cancelling deletes it. "New ▶" lists the new-file templates registered in Windows, such as Word and Excel (they are loaded in the background after startup, so they may be missing just after launch).
  5. More actions ▶: Copy folder listing (names) / (full paths), Copy BOX share path (Box only), Search this folder with index search, Export folder tree to CSV / to Excel
  6. Properties / Copy share link with path / Cloud Menu ▶ / OS standard menu ▶ / in "PC": Map network drive... and Disconnect network drive...
  7. Quick Jump / Show Explorer context menu

"Copy folder listing" copies the list as you see it (with type filters and sorting applied, or the search results in a search tab), one item per line.

docs.title: Archive ▶
docs.text:
If everything you selected is an archive, extract items are listed; otherwise, compress items.

  • Extract: Extract... (choose where) / Extract here / Extract to "name\" (with several: Extract each to its own folder) / Extract to the other pane / Test archive
  • Compress: Compress... (choose where to save and the file name; the format is ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ or 7z) / Compress to "name.zip" / Compress to "name.7z" (made with the tar.exe that ships with Windows) / Compress each to its own ZIP (with several) / Create ZIP in the other pane / Compress with level ▶ (changes the strength for this one time: No compression, Fastest, Standard, Smallest size, Auto)

See Archives for details.

docs.title: The main items explained
docs.text:
• Open in text editor: opens .txt, .md, .json, .html and similar files in the editor set in General → "External apps" → Text editor (VS Code, Notepad++, Sakura Editor, Notepad and so on). With none set, the app associated with .txt in Windows is used. Extensions that are not included by default, such as .csv or .dat, can be added under "Additional extensions" in the same Text editor setting.
  • Compare Text: shows two text files side by side, with added lines in green and removed lines in red. A minimap on the left shows where the differences are in the whole file; click it to jump there. Files up to 5 MB are supported (see Text Comparison).
  • Open in painter: opens .png, .jpg, .bmp and similar files in the app Windows uses for editing images.
  • Convert to PDF: images (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .bmp, .gif, .tif, .tiff, .ico, .webp) and Office documents (.docx, .doc, .docm, .xlsx, .xls, .xlsm, .pptx, .ppt, .pptm) are converted to PDF and saved in the same folder as "original name.pdf". Merged output is named "Combined_timestamp.pdf". Converting Office documents requires Microsoft Office.
  • Export folder tree to CSV / to Excel: reads every file, subfolders included, and produces a table with the columns Name, Size, Type (the extension), Date Modified, Relative Path, Share Path and Open Folder (the CSV is UTF-8 with BOM). "Relative Path" is measured from the starting folder (.\Sub\), so the same table works even where each user's path differs, as in Box. Hidden files are included only while hidden files are set to be shown. In Excel, the "Open Folder" column is a link that opens that folder by its absolute path, and the header row is frozen with AutoFilter.
  • Set this folder as A or B Pane home: it becomes that pane's Home button target and where new tabs open.

docs.title: OS standard menu ▶
docs.text:
The right-click items that apps register with Windows, such as Visual Studio, VS Code, Git, 7-Zip, Sakura Editor, Everything and Microsoft Defender, can be used right from the app's own menu, with their icons. Nested menus such as 7-Zip's open as they are.

  • Items the app's own menu already has (Open, Copy, Delete, Rename, Properties, Create shortcut and so on) are left out. Box, OneDrive and SharePoint items appear under "Cloud Menu ▶" instead.
