docs.title: View Options
docs.text:
• Column width: Choose one of three ways to size the list's columns. The icon at the left end of the column headers always shows which one is in use.
    • Fit to window (icon ↔): The Name column takes the remaining width so the columns fill the window. As the pane narrows, Type, Size and Date Modified are hidden in that order, keeping at least 250px for Name (in search results the order is Location, Size, Date Modified, Name, and the Path column stays to the end). They come back when the pane widens
    • Fit to text (icon: left-aligned bars of different lengths): Each column is sized to fit all of its text, including long names further down the list (up to 60% of the window for Name and half of it for Path). Columns are refitted each time you open a folder, leaving space on the right. Reloading the same folder (F5 and so on) only widens columns, never narrows them. An empty folder leaves widths unchanged
    • Set by hand (icon ✋): Widths never change automatically. Widths you set by dragging column borders are remembered, including after a restart
    • Switching: Each click on the icon at the left end of the headers moves to the next mode: Fit to window → Fit to text → Set by hand. Right-click the icon or any column header for a menu with all three. You can also use the "Column width" button on the pane toolbar or "Switch column width mode" in the command palette. The choice applies to the lists in every pane and tab. When you switch, the columns slide to their new widths
    • Dragging a column: In Fit to window or Fit to text, dragging a column border switches to Set by hand (a notice appears the first time only; after that the icon at the left briefly lights up). Click the icon round to Set by hand again and your hand-set widths come back
    • In Fit to text and Set by hand, a horizontal scroll bar appears when the columns are wider than the window
    • New users start with Fit to text. If you used Zenith Filer before, you get Fit to window if the old "Auto-fit columns" was on, and Set by hand if it was off
  • Showing / hiding columns and fitting one column: Right-click a column header in the list to see the three column width modes followed by "Fit this column to text", which fits only the column you right-clicked, once (in Fit to window it switches to Set by hand). Uncheck a column name below them to hide that column — also the quickest way to make a column narrower. Pick it again to bring it back at a width that matches the current column width mode (the refitted width in Fit to text, the remembered width in Set by hand). The Name column cannot be hidden. The Date created, Extension and Attributes columns are hidden by default and can be shown here (as in File Explorer; attributes appear as single letters: R read-only, H hidden, S system, A archive, C compressed, E encrypted, O offline, L link, T temporary). In Fit to window, these three and the "More columns" below are the first to go when space runs short. Columns for information stored in files (date taken, dimensions, camera maker / model, length, bit rate, artist, album, genre, year, title, authors, tags, rating, pages, company and comments: 17 in all) are under "More columns ▶" in the same menu (like File Explorer's "More columns"; all hidden by default). Values are read starting from the rows on screen, so folders open just as fast. Sorting by one of them reads every item first and puts files without a value at the end (a progress bar appears for large folders and can be cancelled; 10,000 items take about a minute). Online-only files, network locations and archive contents are not read. Hidden columns apply to the lists in every pane and tab and are kept after a restart. Search results show the same menu, where the Location, Path, Date Modified and Size columns can be hidden. The Location column appears only in search results (in a normal list, the icon at the left end of the address bar shows what kind of place you are in).
  • Optimize this folder for: in the empty-space right-click "View ▶ Optimize this folder for ▶", pick General items, Documents, Pictures, Music or Videos (as in File Explorer). The folder's view changes and is kept for next time: Pictures is large icons sorted by date taken (oldest first), Music is details by name, Videos is large icons by name, Documents is details with the newest first, and General items is details with the default sort and no grouping. Column visibility is one setting for the whole app, so it is not changed per folder.
    • Applying it automatically: turn on "Adjust the view to each folder's contents" under Control Deck → "Display" → "Sort order" (off by default), and folders you have never opened get a type picked from their file extensions when you open them (when there are at least 3 files and the most common kind is at least half). Folders you have opened before keep the view remembered then (use the menu above to change them). Sorting Pictures by date taken re-sorts after the dates are read, once the list is shown.
  • Group by: right-click empty space and choose none, name, date modified, size or type from "Group by ▶" (like File Explorer's "Group by"). In Details view each group starts with a header band such as "Today (12)". The groups are: for dates, Today, Yesterday, Earlier this week, Last week, Earlier this month, Last month, Earlier this year, Last year and A long time ago; for sizes, Empty (0), Tiny (up to 16 KB), Small (up to 1 MB), Medium (up to 128 MB), Large (up to 1 GB), Huge (up to 4 GB) and Gigantic; for names, the first letter (symbols, 0 – 9, A – H, I – P, Q – Z, the kana rows and kanji); for types, the type name. Items within a group keep the current sort order, and the sort direction also flips the order of the groups (date modified, descending puts Today first). For size and type, the folder group comes first when folders are sorted first. The arrow (▾) at the left of a band collapses that group so only the band remains (click again to expand it). Clicking elsewhere on the band selects every item in the group (hold Ctrl to add them to the selection). Right-clicking a band shows the empty-space menu, where "Collapse all groups" and "Expand all groups" under "Group by ▶" switch them all at once. Collapsed groups stay collapsed while you stay in the folder, even as files come and go, and everything expands again when you move to another folder. The choice is remembered per folder. Icon views show no bands but keep the group order. The bands are hidden while type-to-filter is active, and collapsed groups show all their items during that time.
  • Cloud sync status: In sync folders such as OneDrive, Box Drive and Dropbox, Details view shows a mark next to the name (the same three as File Explorer's Status). A cloud means "online-only" (downloaded when opened), an outlined check means "available on this device" and a filled check means "always available on this device". Hover over the mark for a description. "Available on this device" appears only in Box Drive and OneDrive / SharePoint sync folders (other sync apps do not mark files with that state).
  • Folders first: Toggle between always showing folders above files or mixing them in name order.
  • Folder sizes: When you open a folder, the sizes of the folders inside it are counted in the background and shown in the Size column. They are counted the same way as Explorer's Properties, so the values match (hidden and system files are counted, the targets of junctions and symbolic links are not, and hard links are counted once per link). While counting, a small spinning mark appears in the Size column for folders that don't have a size yet.
    • Normal and dimmed text: Only sizes counted while you are viewing the folder appear in normal text. Sizes remembered from an earlier count (kept even after you close the app) and sizes from the index are dimmed until counting finishes, then switch to normal text. Dimmed text means the value may be out of date
    • Tooltip: Hover over a size to see the exact bytes, the number of files and folders inside, and when it was counted, such as 5.86 KB (6,001 bytes) / 3 files, 3 folders / Counted at 14:00, so you can compare without opening Properties. For a dimmed size, it says whether it is a previous value, a value from the index, or whether the contents changed after counting
    • Recounting: Press F5 to recount every folder in the list, or use "Recount size" on the right-click menu to recount only the selected folders, at any time. Places you move, copy, delete or rename in Zenith Filer are recounted on the spot
    • Changes while you're viewing: While a folder on a local drive is open, changes inside it (including changes made outside the app, for example in Explorer) are watched and the changed folders are recounted. Large folders that take a while to count (2 seconds or more last time) are not recounted; their size is dimmed instead (press F5 to recount)
    • Recount interval: A folder's modified date doesn't change when files deep inside it are added or changed, so by default folders are counted every time you open them. With a longer interval, the previous value is simply shown dimmed until that much time has passed
    • Sorting: When you sort by size, folders are ordered by their counted size. Rows don't move while counting is in progress; the list is re-sorted once when counting finishes (your selection and scroll position are kept)
    • Properties pane: When you select a folder, counting starts right away, as in Explorer's Properties; the running total grows in the form 5.86 KB (6,001 bytes), and the number of files and folders is added when it finishes. With multiple items selected, folder sizes are included in the total
    • Places that aren't counted: Network drives (\\server\share or mapped drives) and cloud-synced folders (Box Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint) aren't counted by default: network drives are slow and the counting puts load on the server, and in cloud folders the sync app has to respond for every folder, which tends to be slow (file contents are never downloaded). Servers (FTP / SFTP) are never counted. Even where sizes aren't counted, indexed locations show the index value dimmed
    • Indexed locations: The index value is shown dimmed at first and replaced with the same value as Properties once counting finishes (the index can differ from Properties because of its exclusion rules and update lag; see Index search)
    • If some folders inside couldn't be opened and only part could be counted, the size is shown with "≥", such as ≥ 12.3 GB (the real size is larger; Properties shows the smaller value without any mark)
    • Counting runs as a single low-priority background task that doesn't get in the way of other disk activity. It stops as soon as you move to another folder, and it doesn't start right after launch
    • Under Control Deck → "Display" → "File list", "Count folder sizes automatically", you can choose whether to count automatically (on by default), the recount interval (every time / 10 minutes / 1 hour / 1 day; every time by default), whether to also count on network drives, and whether to also count in cloud folders (both off by default, chosen separately)
  • Per-folder view settings auto-restore: Remembers the sort order, view mode, icon size, whether folders come first and the grouping for each folder, and applies them again when you come back. Toggle it with "Auto-restore folder display settings" under Control Deck → "General" → "Startup and exit" (on by default).
  • Second search bar row: An option that moves the search bar onto the second row of the header, but only in a side-by-side dual-pane layout. Freed from sharing a row with the icons, the search field and its filters get much more horizontal space. Toggle it with "Move search bar to second row in dual-pane mode" under Control Deck → "Search" → "Search bar" (off by default). With a single pane, or when panes are stacked vertically, the layout stays on one row regardless of the setting. Note that when a pane is too narrow for the search bar to survive on one row, it moves to the second row automatically, whatever the setting says — the history suggestions open at the width of the search box, so in a cramped bar the delete button at the right end of each row would be out of reach.
  • Alternate row colors (zebra striping): Tints every other row in the list a very subtle color, making rows easier to track in wide listings or listings with many rows (Control Deck → "Display" → "File list", "Alternate row colors"; off by default). Rather than a bold striped look, the shading stays subtle enough to never compete with hover/selection colors.
  • File-type coloring: Colors file names by category — images, videos, audio, archives, executables, documents, and code (7 built-in categories) (Control Deck → "File type colors", off by default). A recommended set of extension/color pairings ships out of the box, but every rule's extensions, color, and enabled state are fully editable, and you can add or remove rules freely.

  • Neither of these colors is a fixed value — both are computed automatically against the current theme's background color, so they always look natural whether you're on a bundled theme, an AI-generated theme, or a theme downloaded from the Theme Store.

  • Spotting what's new: Recently modified files and folders show their date in bold, and anything touched just now (within 10 minutes by default) gets a ✨ mark to the right of its name — the mark clears itself once the time passes. Pick the range under Control Deck → "Display" → "Markers", in "Spotting what's new": off, today, 24 hours, 3 days or 7 days; the ✨ mark can be turned off on its own (defaults: 24 hours, mark on). How long the ✨ stays is set just below, in "How long the ✨ mark stays", by typing a number and choosing minutes or hours (1 minute to 7 days; 10 minutes by default). If it is longer than the highlight range, the ✨ stays after the range ends. It exists to stop an old file being sent in place of the current one.

  • Network location marker: While a network folder is open, the tab and the address bar are tinted with the theme's accent and the tab icon becomes a globe. It recognises share paths such as \\server\share as well as mapped drives like Z:, so a shared server is never mistaken for your own machine (Control Deck → "Display" → "Markers", "Show when the folder is on a network"; on by default).
  • Shortcut target on hover: Hovering a shortcut (.lnk) shows its target's full path in a tooltip, and hovering an internet shortcut (.url) shows its URL, in both detail and icon view. A warning is shown if a shortcut's target can no longer be found. Since targets and URLs are read in the background after the list loads, they may appear a moment after the list itself shows up. A shortcut's (.lnk) target is also shown in the Properties view.

docs.title: Effects Categories
docs.text:
In-app animations are grouped into categories that you can toggle individually via Control Deck → "Effects". If you want maximum speed, you can turn them off per category or all at once.

Category (as named on the Effects page) Target UI / animation A. Startup & Global Welcome animation, the light around the card and the rippling title when you finish QuickStart, growing-bar animations (favorites, file sizes and so on) B. GlowBar Progress bar fade, interpolation, glow C. Scan Bar Scan bar while a folder loads D. Tab Operations Tab underline that follows as a light, fades when tabs open and close and on tab hover, insertion marker while dragging a tab E. Pane Transitions Pane fade, Control Deck opening and closing, width animation when switching between one and two panes and opening or closing the nav pane F. Theme Theme switch overlay, theme apply toast H. Quick Preview Hover thumbnail fade (moving to the next or previous file does not move the contents) I. File List Row hover, result glow, light that follows the selection, light on the row selected after a delete, fades for search pop-ups, the tab list, right-click menus and the key guide L. Drag & Drop File name label while dragging, drop target highlight, glow on the receiving folder, drop suck-in Feedback on actions Loading line on folder moves, colour change of the active pane, light on pane switching, light that follows the selected mark in Settings and the nav pane, buttons, dialogs, toasts, Quick Jump, the command palette and Quick Preview appearing

Press Play under See the effects at the very top of the Effects page to watch, on a small sample, the light following the tab underline, the light on a landing row, the ring of light on ★, and the light running around a notice with its name rippling, one after another (they run on the same parts as the real screens).

Turning on Turn off all effects (instant display) at the top of the Effects page stops D, E, F, H, I, L and Feedback on actions together. Whether the mascot is shown is set on the Stickman page.

Automatic reduction on slow environments: When Automatically reduce effects on slow systems (on by default) is enabled, the app detects remote desktop sessions (RDP/VDI), software rendering, and environments where screen transitions are measurably slow, and disables the six decorative categories (D Tab Operations / E Pane Transitions / F Theme / H Quick Preview / I File List / L Drag & Drop) and Feedback on actions in one go. A toast notification is shown on detection. Progress indicators (B GlowBar / C Scan Bar) and A Startup & Global are not affected. The ON/OFF settings of each category are not modified, so turning this setting off makes effects play according to your settings as before. The same effects also stop when "Show animations" is turned off in Windows.

Effects that make everyday actions feel smoother: The file list, tabs, drag and drop and more have effects that make it easier to see what just changed. They all follow the same idea: only a thin light moves, never the contents. The light comes from where the change started (the previous tab, pane or row), catches up as if following your hand, and melts away. When the same light repeats within a short time, the second one is fainter and shorter and from the third on it does not appear, so holding a key never makes the screen busy. It is the same motion as the ring launcher's light. They are built never to get in your way: the selection, the focus and the contents of the list are settled immediately regardless of any effect, and keys and clicks keep working while an effect is playing. Every one of them can be turned off on the Effects page.

  • Turn off all effects (instant display): At the top of the Effects page. When on, it stops the effects of D Tab Operations, E Pane Transitions, F Theme, H Quick Preview, I File List, L Drag & Drop and Feedback on actions, as well as the motion of the ring launcher and notifications, and switches the display instantly. While it is on, the per-category settings are greyed out (they are kept). A Startup & Global, B GlowBar and C Scan Bar follow their own settings. The mascot, even when turned on, does not walk while this switch is on, in lightweight mode, or when Windows' "Show animations" is off.
  • Feedback on actions: When you move to another folder, the list and the breadcrumb simply switch over with no motion (motion on every move gets in the way). Only when loading the destination takes 0.15 seconds or longer does a thin line run along the top of the list. When you switch to the other pane, a light runs along the new pane's edge from the side of the previous pane and melts away (the top edge when the panes are side by side, the shared edge when they are stacked). In the left navigation of Settings and the view icons of the nav pane, the selection mark moves at once and a light catches up from the previous position. Changing the colour of the pane you are working in, the button hover colour and a slight press-in when clicked, and dialogs, toasts, Quick Jump, the command palette and Quick Preview appearing also belong to this category. None of them move or resize anything; they appear by opacity alone (buttons do not grow on hover, and toasts do not rise but have a light run around their edge). When you expand a folder tree, its children appear at once.
  • D Tab Operations: When you switch tabs, the contents appear at once and do not move; the tab underline catches up from the previous tab with a short trail (it stretches on the way and shrinks to the tab's width when it arrives). A tab you open fades in, and a tab you close leaves an afterimage that fades away (closing itself does not wait). The fill when you point at a tab also fades in and out.
  • E Pane Transitions: Switching between one pane and two side-by-side panes opens and closes the panes with a width animation. The same happens when you swap A and B while staying on one pane, and when you open or close the nav pane in docked mode. Nothing moves at startup. Switches involving the top-and-bottom split and the auto-hiding nav pane behave as before.
  • I File List: When you move the selection to the next row with the arrow keys and similar keys, a light follows along the left edge of the list from the previous row to the new one and melts away. The selection itself moves the instant you press the key, so holding or tapping the key never makes you wait. It does not appear when you select with Shift or Ctrl held down, with the mouse, or when the move jumps off screen (PageDown, End and so on). The hover fill on rows fades in and out. After pasting, moving, creating or renaming, a light runs along the bottom edge of the affected rows from the left and melts away. For several rows it runs from top to bottom, each a moment after the last; when there are very many (more than 12), a single light outlines the whole list instead. The light uses whichever of the focus ring colour and the accent colour stands out more against the background. Rows you add to Favorites or index search light up the same way, as does the row the selection moves to after a delete. Right-click menus and the key guide also fade in.
  • L Drag & Drop: The highlight on the target folder fades in and out. When the folder receives the drop, a light spreads along the bottom edge of its row from where you released, and a snapshot of the rows you were dragging shrinks into it. Copying or moving starts the moment you drop and never waits for this effect. The suck-in does not appear for drops from outside the app, such as from Explorer, or for right-button drags.

For new users, Feedback on actions is off by default (you can turn it on from the Effects page).

docs.title: Working Sets
docs.text:
A feature that saves the entire state of the A/B panes (tabs, how the screen is split, each tab's sort and view, selected items, scroll positions) as a "working set," allowing instant switching between "projects."

Display it via the briefcase icon in the nav pane. The key is Ctrl+K then W with the "Zenith 2" keymap (the default for new installs), or Ctrl+Shift+5 with "Zenith standard". The briefcase is not on the icon bar at first, so open the view with the key or place it with the cross-shaped layout window (opening it with the key also adds it to the icon bar). A guide text briefly describing the feature's purpose is shown at the top of the view.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Click the "Save current state" button at the top of the nav pane and enter a name to save the complete state of both A/B panes.

Data is persisted in settings.json and the entire list is preserved even after app exit and restart.

docs.title: What is saved
docs.text:
Item Saved and restored Screen One or two panes, how two panes are split (side by side or top and bottom), and which pane you were using (including showing B in single-pane mode) Folder tabs Location, lock, each tab's sort (column, direction, folders first), view (details or icons and their size), selected items (up to 100), and scroll position. The selected tab of the pane you were using also gets keyboard focus back Terminal tabs Reopened as terminals, in the folder you moved to with cd. The previous screen text and a running Claude Code conversation come back too (see Picking up terminal work)
  • A tab that was searching comes back as the folder without the search (selection and scroll position on search results are not kept).
  • Sets saved by earlier versions still work. Their sort comes back only on the tab that was selected when the set was saved (earlier versions kept only one sort per pane).

docs.title: Preview and Commit (Rollback Feature)
docs.text:
Click a saved set in the list to instantly switch the A/B pane contents to that set's state.

The key feature is that "the original state is not affected until you commit."

  • Preview state: Clicking a set enters a temporary "preview" state, and a dedicated footer bar (its color follows the theme) appears at the bottom of the view.
  • Apply: Press the "✔ Apply this set" button in the footer to commit that state as your current working state.

  • Cancel (Rollback): Press the × button at the right end of the footer (tooltip "Revert to the state before loading"), or switch to another view (favorites, etc.) in the nav pane, to automatically restore to the state immediately before loading the working set (all tabs, selection positions, scroll state).

    This makes context switching extremely smooth, such as "checking Project B materials while working on Project A and quickly returning."

  • Folders that can't be found still open as registered. If a folder can't be found at the moment you recall the set, it is not replaced with Desktop or anything else: its tab keeps the registered path. What the tab shows depends on why the folder can't be found.

    • For Box Drive and SharePoint folders, or when the whole drive or share can't be found (before syncing starts, or before you plug in an external drive or connect a network drive), the tab shows "This location is not available yet. Waiting for it to come online…". When the folder appears, it opens on its own within about 2 seconds. The notification says how many folders are not found yet and will open when they appear. If it still hasn't appeared after 2 minutes, the tab stops waiting and switches to "This folder can't be found". A registered drive root (such as D:\) is handled the same way.
    • When the drive or share is there but the folder itself is gone, waiting won't bring it back (it was deleted, moved or renamed), so the tab shows "This folder can't be found" right away, without waiting. The notification also says how many folders can't be found. Open the right location and use Overwrite to register it again.

    Either way the tab keeps the registered path, so using Overwrite as it is does not change what you registered.

docs.title: History before switching
docs.text:
When you switch to a set, the state of your work before switching is kept automatically. Open "Before switching" under the working sets in the nav pane to see them, newest first (up to 30). Click a row to go straight back to that state.

  • Go straight back: When you switch, a toast at the top says "Switched to working set ...". Click Undo to go straight back to the state before switching (it closes after 8 seconds, and stays while the mouse is over it).
  • What is kept: The same things as a set (tabs, sort, selection, scroll position, how the screen is split). Each entry is labeled by where you switched to, such as "Before switching to \"Work\"".
  • Go back and forth: Restoring from the history also keeps the state before restoring, labeled "Before restoring from history", so you can undo it too.
  • No clutter: If the state is exactly the same as the set you switch to (tabs, sort, view, two or more selected items, and scroll position all match; a single selected item counts as just the cursor position), nothing would be lost, so nothing is kept. A toast then says "nothing was kept in the history because the state before switching was the same" (it closes after 6 seconds). If the state matches the entry kept just before, that entry is refreshed instead of adding a new one.
  • Nothing is kept when you leave a preview with "Revert", because nothing is lost.
  • If you close the app while previewing, the work before the preview is kept as "Before closing while previewing". You can go back to it after the next start.
  • Right-click to Save as a set (name it and add it to the list), Remove from history, or Clear all (with confirmation). The Delete key also removes an entry.
  • Keeping history and restoring from it do not count toward the free version's limits. "Save as a set" counts the same as saving a set.
  • Free version limits: you can keep up to 5 sets, and saving plus overwriting sets is limited to 3 times a day in total. Switching sets (previewing and applying) does not count.
  • The history is saved in data\working_set_history.json in the app folder (separate from settings.json).

docs.title: Picking up terminal work
docs.text: When a set includes terminal tabs, they come back in two ways so you can carry on after switching away and back.

docs.title: While the app is running: kept running in the background
docs.text:
Terminals taken out by switching sets are not closed; they keep running in the background. Recalling a set or history entry that includes one, or leaving a preview with "Revert", brings back that same terminal as it was. A running build or Claude Code has not stopped, and output produced while it was in the background is on its screen.

  • How many: Set by "Terminals to keep running in the background" in the working sets gear settings (3 by default; 0 keeps none, closing terminals on switch; up to 8).
  • Which close first: Beyond that number, idle ones are closed oldest first. Ones running a command (a build, Claude Code, and so on) are not closed. If running ones alone exceed the number, they stay, and are closed at the next switch after they finish. While previewing, the terminals from before the preview are not closed for the count.
  • Ones with no way back are closed right away: terminals that no set or history entry includes (such as one opened by a preview and never used).
  • How many are kept: Below the table of the working sets on the status bar, a count such as "2 terminal(s) running in the background (Claude Code 1)" appears. Close all closes them, including running ones.
  • Background terminals use memory (tens to hundreds of MB each). While Claude Code runs in the background, it keeps using your usage allowance.
  • When a terminal comes back in the other pane, its display is rebuilt, so the screen text from when the set was taken is written back (the process carries on).
  • Closing the app closes all background terminals.

docs.title: After reopening the app: screen text and Claude Code conversation
docs.text:
Saving, overwriting, and switching sets also keep each terminal tab's screen text (up to the last 3,000 lines). The history before switching keeps it too. After a background terminal is closed, or after the app is reopened, terminals come back this way.

  • Previous screen written back: When a set comes back, the terminal opens a new shell and the previous screen text is written above it in gray, followed by a divider such as "Screen up to 10/18 09:00 (working set "Work")", with a fresh prompt below. Scroll up to read the commands and output from before. Colors are not kept.
  • Resuming a Claude Code conversation: For a terminal that was running Claude Code, a resume command is placed in the input line at the first prompt. It is not run; press Enter to resume the conversation.
    • If the Claude Code status line integration is registered, the conversation ID is known, so claude --resume <conversation ID> is placed and the terminal opens in the folder where the conversation started.
    • If the ID is not known (the integration is not registered, or no reply has arrived yet), claude --continue is placed instead. It opens the latest conversation in that folder, so if you had another conversation in the same folder, that one may open.
  • What does not continue: Programs that were running (a build, or Claude Code itself) stop, and the terminal starts a new shell.
  • Screen text is stored in data\working_sets\screens in the app folder, one file per tab, and is removed once no set or history entry uses it.
  • To keep it off the disk, turn off "Also keep terminal screen text" in the gear settings (the Claude Code resume command is still placed when it is off).
  • Output produced while a terminal was in the background is not kept once the app closes (what is kept is the screen from when the set was taken or switched).

docs.title: Management
docs.text:
• Overwrite: The save button at the right end of each row replaces that set with the current A/B pane state — the same thing the right-click "Overwrite" entry does.
  • Rename: Right-click a set and select "Rename" to edit the set name.
  • Delete: Right-click a set and select "Delete," or select the item and press the delete button (trash can icon) to remove the set. You are asked to confirm first, since rebuilding a set means saving it again from scratch.

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text:
Clicking a column heading (name / date / A-B) sorts by that column. Each click moves it on: sorted → reversed → off, and turning it off returns the list to the order you arranged by dragging. Which way it starts depends on the column: name begins ascending, while date and A-B begin descending so the largest comes first. An arrow on the heading shows which column is in use and which way it runs.

  • Sorting changes only what you see. The stored order does not change, so the numbers (1 to 9) in the status bar quick access stay in the order you arranged.
  • Dragging to reorder is disabled while a sort is active, so the stored order cannot be rewritten while the view refuses to move. Turn the sort off and you can rearrange freely again.
  • Overwriting a set while sorted updates its date but leaves the row where it is. Click the heading again to re-sort.
  • The sort lasts for the session only; the next launch starts with it off.

docs.title: Working from the keyboard
docs.text:
Opening working sets with the key (Ctrl+K → W in "Zenith 2", Ctrl+Shift+5 in "Zenith standard") puts the focus straight into the list. Choosing a set, checking it, and getting back to work is one loop that never needs the mouse.

Key Action ↑ ↓ Move between sets Enter Open the selected set as a preview; press again to commit it Esc Roll back if previewing; otherwise hand focus back to the file list Ctrl+S Overwrite the selected set with the current state F2 Rename Delete Delete (with a confirmation) Insert Save the current state as a new set

With "Apply on click" turned on (the gear button), a single Enter goes straight to committing. Committing hands focus back to the file list, so the opening key → ↓ → Enter takes you from switching to working again.

The row being previewed is marked, so it is obvious that pressing Enter once more will commit it.

docs.title: Quick access from the status bar
docs.text:
Click the working sets button on the status bar (Ctrl+B → W in "Zenith 2", Ctrl+Shift+S in "Zenith standard", or the bottom slot of the Ring Launcher) to open the same table as the nav pane. You can pick and switch right there without opening the nav pane.

  • Table: Columns for number, name, date, A/B (tab counts), and an overwrite button. Click a column header to sort (kept separately from the nav pane's sort, and only while it is open). Click a row to switch immediately, without a preview. Right-click to overwrite, rename, or delete.
  • Numbers: The first nine sets are numbered 1 to 9. Press that digit to apply the set immediately, without arrowing down to it. The numbers follow the stored order you arranged and do not change when you sort or filter the table ("3" is always the same set).
  • Filter: Type part of a name in the box at the top right to narrow the table. Typing while the table has focus moves to the box and enters the text (Ctrl+F also moves there). In the box, Down goes to the table and Enter applies the top row. Esc clears the text, or closes if it is empty.
  • History before switching: "Before switching" is listed below the table (see History before switching). Click an entry to go back to that state.
  • F2 (rename), Delete (delete), Ctrl+S (overwrite), and Insert (save the current state) work the same as in the nav pane.
  • Closing: Click outside the table (for example on the file list), press Esc, switch to another app, or click the working sets button again.

docs.title: Quick Jump
docs.text:
Press Ctrl+P to open the Quick Jump dialog. It incrementally searches across your entire trajectory — favorites, frequently used folders, the full navigation history, tabs you actually opened (ranked by dwell time), and recently opened files — plus every indexed file and folder (dynamic search as you type). Selecting a folder navigates to it; selecting a file opens it in the OS default app.

  • Search: As you type, candidates are filtered in real time based on name, path, and description. Scoring is tiered: exact match > prefix match > word-boundary match > substring match, and entering multiple whitespace-separated words narrows results to candidates containing all of them (AND search). Favorites with custom display names are also found by their real folder name, and matching favorites are always included in the results regardless of the display cap.
  • Source badge: A badge showing the source ("Favorites," "Frequent Folders," "Recent Folders," "Active Tabs," "Recent Files," "Index," etc.) is displayed on the right side of each candidate, with a source-specific color and icon (Favorites = amber ★, Frequent = green, History = blue, Tabs = purple, Recent Files = slate, Index = teal) so the origin is recognizable at a glance. Favorites and frequent folders appear instantly; history, tabs, and recent files are appended asynchronously right after; and the index is searched dynamically once you type 2+ characters (none of which block startup or interaction).
  • Folders only / include files toggle: A slide toggle limits search candidates to folders, or includes files (recent files and indexed files) as well. Defaults to folders only; the state is remembered across sessions.
  • Keyboard navigation: Use Up/Down arrows to move between candidates, Enter to confirm, and Escape to close.
  • New tab / overwrite toggle: A slide toggle lets you choose between opening the selected folder in a new tab or overwriting the current tab. Defaults to new tab.
  • Click outside: Clicking outside the dialog automatically closes it.
  • The dialog appears near the mouse cursor position.

docs.title: How Index Search Works
docs.text: This article explains what index search does behind the scenes, from a user's point of view. If you only need to operate it and choose settings, Index Search and Index Settings are enough.

docs.title: Where the Index Lives
docs.text: The index is kept in data\index inside the app's folder. The registered folders and their lock state, the time of the last full rebuild, and the time of the last scheduled update are kept there too, so everything carries over when you close the app or restart the PC.

docs.title: What Gets Recorded
docs.text: For every file and folder under a registered folder, the index records its name, location (full path), size and date modified. File contents are not recorded. To search for text inside files, use file content search (grep) in the search bar (see Search).

docs.title: Name Matching
docs.text:
Keywords are matched against the name (not the path; which folders are searched is decided by the search scope).

  • Japanese is split into words: "議事録" finds "第3回議事録.docx"
  • Partial matches are added: letters, digits and katakana that cannot be split into words are still found when they match part of a name
  • Spaces mean AND: results must contain every word. If nothing is found and the keyword contains a space, the search runs again automatically, matching any of the words (OR)
  • * and ?: work as wildcards (a leading one such as *report is allowed). The partial-match side treats them as literal characters, though, so to narrow reliably by extension use a regular expression as below
  • **Regular expressions (".*" on in the search bar)**: a .NET regular expression is applied to the name including its extension, keeping the original upper and lower case (for example \.xlsx$). If matching a single name takes more than 0.1 seconds, matching stops for the rest of that search, so an overly complex pattern cannot freeze it
  • Size and date filters: the size and date set in the search bar are applied while results are taken from the index

docs.title: Result Limits and Order
docs.text:
• Index search takes up to 500 results, newest date modified first
  • Looking at a folder's contents with "Confirm index registration" on its right-click menu (no keyword) shows up to 1,000 items

docs.title: Normal Search vs. Index Search
docs.text:
Item Normal search Index search Scope The current folder and everything under it The registered folders (those chosen in the search scope) What it reads Scans the disk on the spot The index (does not read the disk) Matching Partial name match and wildcards; regular expressions when ".*" is on As described in Name Matching Number of results No limit (added as they are found) 500 How current Always the disk as it is now As of the last index update

Normal search does not use the index. It can search folders you have not registered, but deeper folders take longer. Index search covers all registered folders together and returns results without reading the disk.

docs.title: How the Index Is Built
docs.text:
• One folder at a time: only one indexing job runs at once; the rest wait their turn (their status shows "Waiting")
  • Box Drive is walked first: for Box Drive locations, the folders are opened once beforehand so Box prepares the actual files, which keeps them from being skipped as unreadable
  • Unreadable items are skipped: folders you have no access to, and items with the system or temporary attribute, are not read
  • Your work comes first: indexing runs at a lower priority and pauses briefly after writing each batch. The pause is shortest for local drives; with "Process network drives with lower priority" on it is longer for network and Box Drive locations, and "Update index in eco mode" lengthens it further
  • Recorded when done: the finish time and item count are saved, and the status shows "N items" (or "Complete")

docs.title: What Is Not Indexed (Exclusions)
docs.text:
The following are skipped automatically even inside a registered folder.

  • Folder names: .git, .svn, .hg, node_modules, bower_components, .vs, obj, bin, .nuget, __pycache__, .mypy_cache, .pytest_cache, .tox, venv, .venv, .next, .nuxt, .gradle, $Recycle.Bin, System Volume Information, $WINDOWS.~BT, $WINDOWS.~WS, $WinREAgent, $SysReset, Recovery, PerfLogs, MSOCache, Config.Msi, INetCache, Temporary Internet Files, and every folder whose name starts with $
  • Locations: anything under AppData\Local\Temp (the temp folder) and under the internet caches (AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache, Temporary Internet Files)
  • File names: desktop.ini, Thumbs.db, ehthumbs.db, ehthumbs_vista.db, .DS_Store, .localized, .Spotlight-V100, .Trashes, NTUSER.DAT, ntuser.dat.LOG1, ntuser.dat.LOG2, ntuser.ini, UsrClass.dat, UsrClass.dat.LOG1, UsrClass.dat.LOG2
  • Other files: Office temporary files starting with ~$, files with the extension .tmp, .temp, .bak, .swp or .swo, and files with no extension

docs.title: How Changes Are Picked Up
docs.text:
• The app's own operations are reflected at once: moves, copies, deletions and renames done in Zenith Filer are reflected in the index as soon as they finish, whatever the update mode. Records for places that are gone are removed along with everything under them, and new places are added along with everything under them (only under registered folders that are not locked). A batch rename's "A → temporary name → B" is applied in order. A folder with no record in the index shows its size as blank (unknown), not 0
  • Changes in open folders: when the update mode is "Auto-detect changes" or "Update at regular intervals", changes made outside the app to a folder open in a tab (creating, renaming, deleting, rewriting a file) are reflected too. With "Update only when needed" they are not. Changes in folders that are not open are not picked up this way
  • Scheduled updates: with "Update at regular intervals", registered folders are read again at the chosen interval. The last run time survives closing the app; if the interval has already passed when the app starts, the update runs 2 minutes after startup. For each folder, "Index Detailed Settings" lets you set the days, the time and the update mode
  • Incremental updates do not notice deletions: an incremental update ("Incremental update" on the right-click menu, and the default for scheduled updates) adds new and changed items only; records of files that have disappeared stay. To clean those up, use "Rebuild index", or set the folder's update mode to "Always full rebuild"

docs.title: Idle Execution (CPU load avoidance)
docs.text:
You can keep scheduled updates from starting while the CPU is busy with other work.

  • Setting: in Control Deck → "Index", turn on "Update index only when CPU load is low" and pick the "CPU usage limit" below it (10% / 20% / 30%; 20% by default)
  • When it applies: before a scheduled update of "Update at regular intervals" starts. While CPU usage is above the limit, it measures again every 10 seconds and waits. Searching works as usual while it waits
  • Minimum interval between full rebuilds: choosing "Full rebuild" sooner than the "Minimum Full Re-index Interval" (6 / 12 / 24 hours; 24 hours by default) does nothing and tells you "Full rebuild was already executed within N hours"

docs.title: Index Search
docs.text:
Chapter summary Index search records the file names in the folders you register ahead of time, so you can find things instantly even among huge numbers of files. Changes in open folders and the app's own operations are picked up automatically, and settings such as holding scheduled updates while the CPU is busy or processing network drives with lower priority keep the impact on other apps small.

This article explains what index search is and how to use it. The settings are covered in Index Settings, and what happens behind the scenes in How Index Search Works.

docs.title: What Is Index Search
docs.text:
Index search is a feature that pre-stores file information from folders in a database (index), enabling instant search results even from massive numbers of files.

Search Mode Characteristics Best suited for Normal search Scans the folder on the spot. Always current, but slow for large folders. Searching within small to medium folders that are currently open. Index search Uses a pre-built index. Extremely fast, but requires tuning for "when and how much to update." Cross-folder searching across multiple registered folders.

Zenith Filer's index feature uses a search engine based on Lucene.NET (the .NET port of Apache Lucene) and splits Japanese file names into words so they can be searched naturally. The index holds names, locations, sizes and dates modified; file contents are not included (use file content search to look for text inside files).

docs.title: Index Lifecycle
docs.text:
Indexes are managed through the following flow, from folder registration to updating and rebuilding.

  • Registration: Adding a folder in the Index Search view of the nav pane (Ctrl+Shift+4 in Zenith Standard, Ctrl+K then I in Zenith 2) registers it as a search target. No index is created at this point.
  • Initial indexing: Pressing "Build unindexed" scans disk files and creates indexes only for folders that have never been indexed.
  • Incremental update: Depending on the configured update mode, indexes are updated from changes seen in open folders, by periodic rescanning, or only when you run an update yourself. Periodic rescanning keeps counting from the last run even while the app is closed; if the interval has already passed when the app starts, it runs a few minutes after startup.
  • Operations in the app: whatever you move, copy, delete or rename in Zenith Filer (including paste, drag and drop, batch rename, Ctrl + Z undo, the AI folder organizer and macros) is reflected in the index right away, whatever the update mode. Entries for places that are gone are removed, and new places show up at once in search and in folder sizes (places outside the index and locked folders are left alone).
  • Changes in the open folder: under "Auto-detect changes" or "Update at regular intervals", changes made from outside the app, such as in Explorer, to the folder you have open (creating, renaming or deleting files and folders) are reflected too. Under "Update only when needed" they are not.
  • Full rebuild: Choosing "Full rebuild" from the menu (three dots) and answering "Yes" re-indexes every registered folder (except locked ones) from scratch. If you choose it sooner than the "Minimum Full Re-index Interval", nothing runs and you are told "Full rebuild was already executed within N hours".
  • Pause and Resume: "Pause" stops new index creation, and "Resume" resumes it. Existing indexes remain usable, and searching is available while paused.

Index states are shown in the Index Search view as follows.

"Index Status" at the top of the view (overall):

State Meaning Complete No indexing work is in progress. Updating... Some folder's index is being created or updated. Paused Index updates are stopped with "Pause". Searching with the existing index still works.

Each folder in the list:

State Meaning Not created No index has been created yet. The folder is not included in search results. Waiting Waiting for another folder's indexing to finish. Creating... (N items) The index is being created. N items (or Complete) Indexed. The number is how many items are recorded. Archived A locked folder ("Lock index updates" on the right-click menu) that has no items recorded yet. Locked folders are left out of batch and scheduled updates (with items recorded, they show "N items"). Currently unavailable The folder cannot be reached right now, for example on a network or external drive.

docs.title: Search Execution Flow (Normal Search vs. Index Search)
docs.text:
What happens when you press Enter in index search:

  1. First, only the existing index is used to fetch results, and they are shown in the list.
  2. If there are no results and some folder is still being indexed, the search runs again as indexing progresses and the list is replaced.
  3. With "freshness priority" on, an incremental update of indexed folders and creation of not-yet-created ones start in the background, separately from the search. The current results do not wait for them; later searches benefit.

Normal search does not use the index; it reads the current folder and everything under it from the disk on the spot. It works in folders with no index, but deeper folders take longer.

docs.title: Search Result Freshness Warning Bar
docs.text:
The yellow bar at the top of index search results ("Some folders are not yet indexed. Please run "Build Unindexed" in the Index view.") is a notice that some folders are missing from the results.

  • It appears only when some registered folder has never been indexed (not while a folder is merely being indexed).
  • The index itself is safe to use, but creating indexes once with "Build unindexed" will stabilize future search results.
  • If the message is unnecessary, close it with the X button on the right of the bar, or turn off "Show a message when the index may be outdated" under "Index" in Control Deck.

docs.title: Troubleshooting and Best Practices
docs.text: Issue Possible Cause Action File not found in search results Index has not been created yet, or the target folder is not registered. Register the folder in the Index Search view and run "Build unindexed." Results are clearly outdated Files deleted or moved outside the app are still in the index (an incremental update does not remove what has disappeared). Right-click the folder and run "Rebuild index." Warning bar appears frequently Unindexed folders are registered. Close the warning with "X," or turn off "Show a message when the index may be outdated" under "Index" in Control Deck. Alternatively, run "Build unindexed" once to prevent future warnings. Server becomes slow / concerned about background load Freshness priority or automatic updates are running frequently. Set the update mode to "Update only when needed" or turn off "freshness priority," and turn on "Process network drives with lower priority" for network drives. To hold scheduled updates while the CPU is busy, turn on "Update index only when CPU load is low." Keyboard shortcuts stop responding Focus is stuck on the terminal pane or a specific control. Restart the app. Clicking on another pane or file list to return focus may also resolve the issue.

docs.title: Index Search Settings View Details
docs.text:
The Index Search view in the nav pane (Ctrl+Shift+4 in Zenith Standard, Ctrl+K then I in Zenith 2) is where you register/remove search target folders, check status, and manually update.

Your registrations (target folders and lock state) are saved immediately each time you add, remove, or lock an entry. The registrations survive a forced shutdown, crash, restart, or log-off, and are restored exactly as they were on next launch.

  • Adding and removing folders: "Add folder" lets you select from the tree; "Add current folder" adds the folder currently displayed in Pane A/B. You can also drop a folder from a pane onto the view.

    Select an item in the list and use the "Delete" button or "Delete" on the right-click menu to remove it.

  • Right-click menu:

    • Confirm index registration: Lists what the index holds under that folder in a search results tab (up to 1,000 items).
    • Rebuild index: Completely deletes the folder's index and rescans disk files from scratch. Use this when you need to reflect deleted files.
    • Incremental update: Maintains the existing index and reflects only new and updated items (records of files that have disappeared stay). For routine "I want to pick up recent changes" cases, prefer this option.
    • Lock index updates / Unlock: A locked folder is left out of "Build unindexed", "Full rebuild", scheduled updates and the reflection of the app's own operations; it keeps being searched with the index it has. Meant for archive folders that no longer change.
    • Detailed settings: Opens "Index Detailed Settings" (see Per-Folder Settings).
    • Delete: Removes the folder from the search targets.

  • Index Status block: Shows the overall state (Complete / Updating... / Paused) and the total count. Each folder's own state appears in the list (see Index Search for what each state means).

    If no search target folders are registered, the total count shows as 0.

    "Build unindexed" manually indexes only unindexed folders, and "Pause" / "Resume" control index creation. "Full rebuild" and "Open index settings" are on the menu (⋯).

docs.title: Per-Folder Settings
docs.text:
"Detailed settings" on the right-click menu, or "Open detailed settings" in "Per-Item Settings" under "Index" in Control Deck, opens "Index Detailed Settings" for that folder.

  • Archive (Lock): The same as "Lock index updates".
  • Schedule: Choose the days (Mon to Sun) and the "Time:" for scheduled updates. When a scheduled update falls outside the chosen days and time, that folder is skipped. "Reset schedule" clears the choice.
  • Update Mode: Choose "Follow global settings", "Always incremental update" or "Always full rebuild". With "Always full rebuild", the folder's index is deleted and rebuilt at every scheduled update, so no records of vanished files are left behind.

"Per-Item Settings" lists each registered folder with its update mode and schedule.

docs.title: App Settings "Indexing & Search Result Freshness" Details
docs.text: In Control Deck (Ctrl+Shift+O) > "Index" category, you can configure options for index update timing, load, and freshness.

docs.title: Index Update Timing and Load
docs.text:
The default is "Update at regular intervals" (every 2 hours).

Option Best suited for Internal behavior Auto-detect changes (Recommended) Folders you keep open in tabs and want to search in their latest state. Changes in folders open in a tab (creating, renaming, deleting, rewriting a file) are reflected in the index as they happen. Changes in folders that are not open are not picked up, and there is no periodic rescan (use "Incremental update" on the right-click menu or similar to bring them in). Update at regular intervals Shared folders with batch changes overnight, or frequently updated but real-time accuracy not needed. Besides reflecting changes in open folders as they happen, re-reads the registered folders at the chosen interval (Every 1 hour / Every 2 hours / Every 4 hours / Every day) and brings in the differences. CPU/disk load spikes temporarily but update frequency is controlled. Update only when needed When you want to minimize background processing or avoid loading shared servers. No automatic updates; indexes are updated only when you run "Build unindexed", "Full rebuild", or "Rebuild index" / "Incremental update" from the right-click menu (the app's own moves, copies and so on are still reflected).

docs.title: Performance and Load
docs.text:
• Update index in eco mode (on by default): Lengthens the pause inserted after each batch to avoid sustained CPU/disk usage.
  • Process network drives with lower priority (on by default): Applies longer wait times when scanning UNC and mapped drives and Box Drive than for local disks, reducing network bandwidth and server load while updating indexes.
  • Minimum Full Re-index Interval (6 hours / 12 hours / 24 hours; 24 hours by default): Choosing "Full rebuild" sooner than this does nothing and tells you so.
  • Update index only when CPU load is low (off by default) and CPU usage limit (10% / 20% / 30%; 20% by default): Before a scheduled update starts, checks CPU usage and waits while it is above the limit (see Idle Execution).

docs.title: Search Result Freshness
docs.text:
• Keep as up-to-date as possible (freshness priority) (off by default): When ON, executing an index search triggers the following background operations, separately from the search.

    • Already-indexed folders → incremental update
    • Folders never indexed → automatically executes processing equivalent to "Build unindexed"

    The goal is to gradually bring the index up to date while maintaining search result delivery speed.

  • Show a message when the index may be outdated (on by default): When ON, a yellow warning bar is shown at the top of the search results screen only when all of the following are met.

    1. Index search mode is active
    2. The search target folders include folders that have never been indexed

    When OFF, the warning bar is never shown regardless of index state. Displayed warnings can be temporarily dismissed with the × button (effective only within that search tab).

docs.title: Size Filter Details
docs.text: Click the balance icon in the search bar (tooltip "Filter by size") to open the size filter popup. Specify a file size range to narrow search results. Folders are not affected by the size filter. While the filter is on, the button is filled with the selection color. Right-click the button to clear just the size filter. The filter is kept when you close the app and comes back on the next launch. It applies to normal, index and content searches (it cannot be used during Filter in place).

docs.title: Input Method
docs.text:
Specify a range with two text boxes: Min (minimum size) and Max (maximum size). The Min text box is auto-focused when the popup opens.

  • Unit suffixes: Append k (KB), m (MB), or g (GB) after the number to specify the unit
  • Default unit when unspecified: Values without a suffix are interpreted as MB
  • Unit switch: Click "KB / MB / GB" to the right of the box to change the unit of the number you typed (500 → 500k and so on). The switch follows what you type, so a plain number shows "MB" as selected — you can always see which unit the filter will use
  • Decimal values: Decimals like 2.5g (= 2.5 GB) are supported
  • Examples:
Input Interpretation 500k 500 KB 10 10 MB (no suffix = MB) 2.5g 2.5 GB 100m 100 MB

docs.title: Real-time Preview
docs.text: As you type, the conversion result is shown in real time on the right (e.g., 500k shows -> 500 KB). Invalid input turns the text box border red. When Min exceeds Max, an error message "Min exceeds Max" is displayed.

docs.title: Quick Tips
docs.text:
Four buttons for commonly used size ranges are provided for one-click input.

Chip Range set < 100 KB Max = 100 KB (Min is empty) 100 KB ~ 10 MB Min = 100 KB, Max = 10 MB 10 MB ~ 1 GB Min = 10 MB, Max = 1 GB > 1 GB Min = 1 GB (Max is empty)

docs.title: Keyboard Operations
docs.text:
• Tab: Move from Min to Max text box
  • Enter: Close the popup
  • Escape: Close the popup

docs.title: Reset
docs.text: Click the "Reset" button in the upper right of the popup to clear Min and Max values and remove the filter.

docs.title: Date Filter Details
docs.text: Click the calendar icon to the right of the size filter button in the search bar (tooltip "Filter by date") to open the date filter popup. Specify a date range for file modification dates to narrow search results. While the filter is on, the button is filled with the selection color. Right-click the button to clear just the date filter. The filter is kept when you close the app and comes back on the next launch. It applies to normal, index and content searches (it cannot be used during Filter in place).

docs.title: Input Method
docs.text:
Specify a date range with two text boxes: Start and End. The Start text box is auto-focused when the popup opens. The following flexible date formats are supported.

Format Example Interpretation yyyyMMdd (8 digits) 20260228 2026/02/28 MMdd (4 digits) 0228 02/28 of the current year yyyy/M/d 2026/2/28 2026/02/28 yyyy-MM-dd 2026-02-28 2026/02/28 M/d or MM/dd 2/28 02/28 of the current year

docs.title: Real-time Preview
docs.text: As you type, the conversion result is shown in real time on the right (e.g., 20260228 shows -> 2026/02/28). Invalid input turns the text box border red. When the start date exceeds the end date, an error message "Start exceeds End" is displayed.

docs.title: Preset Chips
docs.text:
Nine business-oriented preset chips for commonly used date ranges are arranged in 3 rows. Click to instantly apply to the start and end text boxes.

Category Chips Short-term Today / Yesterday / Last 3 days Medium-term Last 7 days / Last 14 days / Last 30 days Period This month / Last month / This year

docs.title: Calendar Integration
docs.text:
A calendar is always displayed at the bottom of the popup. Text input and calendar operations are bidirectionally synchronized.

  • Text to Calendar: When a valid date is entered in a text box, the corresponding date range on the calendar is automatically highlighted
  • Calendar to Text: When a date is clicked or dragged on the calendar, it is written back to the text box in yyyyMMdd format. It is reflected in the currently focused text box (start or end)

docs.title: Keyboard Operations
docs.text:
• Tab: Move from Start to End text box
  • Enter: Close the popup and return focus to the search box
  • Escape: Close the popup

docs.title: Reset
docs.text: Click the "Reset" button in the upper right of the popup to clear start and end values and remove the filter.

docs.title: Search Presets
docs.text:
Click the star icon in the search bar to open the search preset popup. The presets that come with the app are at the top, and the ones you have saved are listed below a divider under "My Presets". Saved presets are kept after you close the app.

Right-click the ★ to clear the search text, size, date and scope all at once.

docs.title: Built-in presets
docs.text:
These eight come with the app and cannot be deleted. The date presets are calculated from the current day each time you apply them, so the range is always up to date.

Preset Conditions Modified today Modified today; newest first Modified in last 7 days Modified in the 7 days up to and including today; newest first Modified in last 30 days Modified in the 30 days up to and including today; newest first Large files (100MB+) 100 MB or more; largest first Image files Type filter set to "Image" only; newest first Office documents Type filter set to "Excel", "Word", "PPT" and "PDF" only; newest first Executables & scripts Type filter set to "EXE" and "BAT" only; newest first Small files (10KB or less) 10 KB or less; smallest first

The built-in presets have no search words. Applying one fills in its conditions only (the search box is emptied), and the search mode (normal, content or index search) stays as it is. Type words and press Enter to search with those conditions.

docs.title: Saved Conditions
docs.text:
A preset you save holds the following conditions.

Item Content Mode Normal search, content search or index search (saving during Filter in place stores it as normal search) Keyword Search text Size Min / Max size filter values Date Start / End date filter values Type filter On/off for each of Folder, Excel, Word, PPT, PDF, TXT, EXE, BAT, JSON, Image and Other Sort Sort column and direction (ascending ↑ / descending ↓) Scope Which folders index search looks in *"." and "Aa" Whether to search with regular expressions and whether to match case (see Searching with regular expressions)

docs.title: Saving a Preset
docs.text:
1. Set search conditions, then click the star icon to open the popup
  2. Click the "Save current conditions" button at the bottom of the popup
  3. A preset name input dialog appears
  4. Enter a name and confirm; a confirmation dialog shows the conditions to be saved
  5. Click "OK" to save the preset; a toast notification confirms the save

Presets are split into ones for index search and ones for everything else (normal and content search). The popup only shows the presets that suit the current search mode.

docs.title: Applying a Preset
docs.text: Click a preset in the list to bring back all its saved conditions at once. A preset with a keyword searches straight away. The search mode (content search for a preset saved in content search), ".*" and "Aa" also return to how they were when the preset was saved. The size and date buttons immediately reflect the applied conditions. A notification says "Preset "name" applied".

docs.title: Preset Preview
docs.text: Hover over a preset in the list to view its saved conditions in a tooltip. Displayed items include keyword, size, date, filter, scope, and sort; only items with values are shown. Size is displayed in 1 GB format and dates in yyyy/MM/dd format.

docs.title: Deleting a Preset
docs.text: Hover over a preset under My Presets to reveal an X button on the right. Clicking it immediately deletes without confirmation, and a toast notification confirms deletion. Built-in presets cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Condition Reset
docs.text:
Click the "Reset conditions" button on the lower left of the popup to reset all current search conditions to their initial state at once.

Item State after reset Keyword Cleared to empty Size filter Min / Max both cleared Date filter Start / End both cleared Sort Date Modified descending (default) Type filter All types re-enabled Search mode Not changed (maintained) Scope Not changed (maintained)

A toast notification "All search conditions reset" is displayed upon completion.

docs.title: Search Features
docs.text:
The four buttons at the left end of the search bar choose how you search.

Button How it searches Key Search Normal search. Finds items by name in the current folder and all its subfolders Ctrl+F (or Ctrl+E) Grep Content search. Finds text inside the files in the current folder Ctrl+Shift+G Index Index search. Finds items by name across all the folders you have registered Ctrl+Shift+F Filter Filter in place. Narrows the current list to what you type Ctrl+I

Ctrl+F moves to the search box, and brings you back to normal search if you are in index search. Type words in the search box and press Enter to search. Where the results appear is set by "Search Behavior" (Search Behavior).

docs.title: Normal search (Search)
docs.text:
• Scope: The folder you have open and every subfolder inside it, searched on the spot by walking the folders.
  • Syntax: Separate words with spaces for AND (must contain all), with | for OR (any of them), use -word to exclude, ext:pdf to pick an extension, and wildcards such as *.pdf and report?.txt. You can also filter by type, date modified and size (Filtering by properties). Turn on ".*" in the search bar to treat everything you type as a regular expression (Searching with regular expressions).
  • Results: Both files and folders are found, newest modified first. Click a column heading to sort differently, by name for example. Above the results are type filters (Folder, Excel, Word, PPT, PDF, TXT, EXE, BAT, JSON, Image, Other) and the count.
  • Windows index: A setting lets normal search also look inside files through the Windows index (Searching file contents with the Windows index).
  • Second search bar row: When enabled, the search bar moves to the second row of the header only in a side-by-side dual-pane layout, giving the search field and filters more width (View Options).

docs.title: Index search (Index)
docs.text:
• Scope: Every folder registered in the "Index Search" view of the nav pane, searched together wherever you happen to be. Open the view with Ctrl+Shift+4 (with the "Zenith 2" keymap, Ctrl+K then I).
  • Both files and folders are indexed. Files without an extension (temporary files, caches and the like) are not indexed, so index search cannot find them (normal search can). Large working folders such as .git and node_modules are skipped as well.
  • Results: Up to 500, newest modified first.
  • Narrowing the folders (scope): In index search, a folder icon with a badge (such as 3/10) appears in the search bar. Click it to list the registered folders and tick the ones to search. "Select all" and "Deselect all" switch them all at once. The icon and badge are highlighted while the scope is narrowed. Results refresh as soon as you change the selection, and the selection is kept after you close the app. Locked folders can be selected too and are searched as they were when locked.
  • While the index is being built: What has been indexed so far is already searchable. The status bar shows progress as "Updating index (N)...".

How to register folders, keep them up to date and read their states is covered in Index Settings and Index Search.

docs.title: Content search (Grep)
docs.text:
• Purpose: Finds words in the contents (text) of files in the folder you have open. Unlike normal search, it looks at the text inside files rather than their names.
  • How it works: It uses the copy of ripgrep that comes with the app.
  • Case and regular expressions: Only in content search, an "Aa" button (match case) appears in the search bar. Turn on ".*" to search with a regular expression (Searching with regular expressions).
  • Results: Matching files are listed. The Match column shows the first matching line (line number and text) and how many matches the file has.
  • Limits: Files up to 50 MB are read, and up to 1,000 files are listed. Binary files, anything hidden (hidden files and the insides of hidden folders) and files listed in .gitignore inside a Git repository are skipped. UTF-8 is recognised, as are files with a BOM (such as UTF-16).

docs.title: Filter in place (Filter)
docs.text:
• Purpose: Narrows the list of the folder you have open on the spot as you type. No results tab opens, and subfolders are not searched.
  • How: Press Ctrl+I or the Filter button in the search bar; the cursor moves to the search box and Filter mode starts. Each keystroke narrows the list to items whose names contain what you typed (case is ignored). With ".*" on, only items whose names match the regular expression remain. While the expression you are typing has an error, the list stays as it was filtered last.
  • While in Filter mode, the size and date filter buttons and the search presets button cannot be used.
  • Clearing: Erase the text with the × in the search box or Esc to bring the list back and return to normal search. Pressing another mode's button also clears it.

docs.title: Search history
docs.text:
Click the search box to see your earlier searches. Normal, content and index searches share one history list (up to 100 entries), and the icon on each row shows which kind of search it was.

If a preset, size filter or date filter was in use, "Search Presets: name", "Size: …" and "Date: …" appear to the right of the words. The preset name is found by matching the saved presets' conditions, so it also appears when you set the same conditions by hand.

Choosing an entry brings back the search mode, size filter and date filter as they were and searches again.

docs.title: Clearing the search box (Esc)
docs.text: Pressing Esc in the search box first clears the text; pressing it again also clears the size and date filters and the scope and ends the search. Turn on "One-press full reset with Esc" under Control Deck → "Search" → "Search bar" (off by default) to clear everything with one press.

docs.title: Size and date filters and search presets
docs.text:
• Size and date filters: The size and date buttons in the search bar narrow results by file size and by date modified. They apply to normal, index and content searches, and a button is filled with the selection color while its filter is on. Right-click a button to clear just that filter. See Size and Date Filters.
  • Search presets: The ★ in the search bar saves frequently used conditions under a name and brings them back. Right-click the ★ to clear the search text, size, date and scope all at once. See Search Presets.

docs.title: Filtering by properties
docs.text:
Write name:value in the search box to filter by type, date modified and size as well as by file name (the same idea as File Explorer's search). These combine with plain words, | OR, -word exclusion, ext: and wildcards, and apply to file name search (including subfolders).

Write Meaning kind:folder / kind:file Folders only / files only kind:picture, kind:video, kind:music, kind:document, kind:archive, kind:program Pictures, videos, music, documents (Office, PDF, text and so on), archives, programs date:today, yesterday, thisweek, lastweek, thismonth, lastmonth, thisyear, lastyear Modified today, yesterday, this week (from Sunday), last week, this month, last month, this year, last year date:2026-10-01 / date:>2026-10-01 / date:<=2026-10-01 / date:2026/10/01..2026/10/03 That day, after it, up to it, between them (both ends included) size:empty, tiny, small, medium, large, huge, gigantic File Explorer's size groups (empty, up to 16 KB, up to 1 MB, up to 128 MB, up to 1 GB, up to 4 GB, over 4 GB) size:>10MB / size:<1.5KB / size:>=500 Larger than, smaller than, at least (units KB, MB, GB; bytes without one) name:report The name contains it (same as a plain word) tags:travel A tag starts with it. Only when the Windows index is used (see below) rating:4 / rating:>=4 Rated 4 stars / at least 4 stars. Only when the Windows index is used
  • Japanese names work too: 種類: (kind), 更新日時: or 日付: (date), サイズ: (size), 名前: (name), with Japanese values such as 画像, 今週 and 中.
  • Examples: report kind:document date:thismonth (documents modified this month with "report" in the name) / kind:music | kind:video / ext:pdf size:<1MB.
  • Filtering by size leaves folders out (a folder's size is not known while searching).
  • Values that cannot be read (such as kind:unknown) are matched against the name as plain words.
  • Tags and rating (tags:, タグ:, rating:, 評価:) only filter when "Search file contents with the Windows index" is on in Settings and the place you search is indexed (like File Explorer's search, they use the index's information). Otherwise the status bar tells you so, and the search skips those words and uses the rest (reading each file's properties while walking folders would be very slow).
  • While ".*" (regular expressions) is on, these are taken literally as well.

docs.title: Searching with regular expressions
docs.text:
Turn on "." in the search bar to treat what you type as a regular expression. It works in normal search, index search, Filter in place, and content search (Grep). There is one "." switch per pane, and it stays as it is when you change modes. If searches open in the opposite pane, the pane you searched from passes its setting along.

  • Name searches (normal search, index search, Filter): Everything you type is one expression, matched against the name including its extension. A match anywhere in the name counts (add ^ and $ to match the whole name). Folder paths are not matched.
    • While ".*" is on, spaces (AND), | (OR), -word (exclude), and ext: are taken literally as regular expression text (| works as the regular expression "or"). To narrow by extension, write something like \.pdf$.
    • Case is ignored. To match case, start the expression with (?-i).
    • All .NET regular expression syntax is available (lookahead, lookbehind, backreferences, named groups, conditionals, \p{…}, and more).
  • Content search (Grep): Uses ripgrep's regular expressions. Expressions with backreferences, lookahead, or lookbehind automatically switch to PCRE2. Use "Aa" to match case. Syntax that only .NET has (balancing groups, character class subtraction [a-z-[aeiou]]) is not available.
To find Expression JPEGs starting with IMG_ and 4 digits ^IMG_\d{4}\.jpe?g$ Excel files without old ^(?!.*old).*\.xlsx$ Names with the same digit twice in a row (\d)\1 Only Report with a capital R at the start (?-i)^Report Text files named only in hiragana ^\p{IsHiragana}+\.txt$

When the expression has an error: The search box border turns red as you type, and "Invalid regular expression (near character N)" appears on the right. Point at it to see the detailed reason. Pressing Enter in this state does not search, and a notification tells you so. In content search, if ripgrep rejects the expression, "ripgrep rejected the expression" appears, and pointing at it shows ripgrep's message.

Time limit: Matching each name stops after 0.1 seconds. If an expression is too complex and hits the limit, the search stops there and "Matching stopped because the expression is too complex" appears (matches found until then stay).

Search presets also save the "." and "Aa" states and restore them when applied (see Search Presets). Search history does not save them; picking from history searches with the current "." setting.

docs.title: Search Behavior (Configurable in Control Deck)
docs.text:
In Control Deck (default: Ctrl+Shift+O) > "Search" > "Opening search results", "Search Behavior" offers three choices for where search results appear. The default is "Same pane, new tab". All of them search when you press Enter.
