Option Behavior Best suited for Same pane, new tab Opens a new results tab in the same pane. Typing new words in the results tab and pressing Enter searches again in that tab. Results stay within the same pane, keeping context predictable. Recommended default for beginners. Same pane, current tab Shows the results in the current tab. No extra tabs, and quick switching between search and the normal view. Other pane, new tab Searching in Pane A shows the results in a new tab in Pane B, and vice versa. Switches to dual-pane automatically in single-pane mode. For comparison work and advanced users. Useful when viewing search results alongside the original listing.

Whichever you choose, pressing × at the right end of the search bar ends the search and shows that tab's searched folder again (the tab is not closed).

Turn on Auto-switch to single pane mode when searching ("Search" > "Search bar", off by default) to switch to a single pane when you search, so the results get the full width. A search started in Pane B appears in Pane A. Ending the search brings back the dual-pane layout.

docs.title: Searching file contents with the Windows index
docs.text:
Turn on "Search file contents with the Windows index" under Control Deck → "Search" → "Search bar" (off by default) and normal search uses the Windows index (Windows Search, the same one File Explorer's search uses). Besides names, it also finds files whose contents contain the words (text, PDFs, Office documents and other formats Windows indexes the contents of).

  • The index is used when the place is fully indexed (Documents, Downloads, Desktop and so on; Windows' "Indexing Options" decide what is indexed) and you type plain words. Searches with | OR, wildcards (* ?) or regular expressions (".*"), and places outside the index, still walk the folders and match names as before.
  • kind:, date:, size:, ext: and -word filters apply to the index results too.
  • Up to 5,000 results are shown. Windows builds the index in the background, so a file you have just created may not show up for a while.

docs.title: Path Click Behavior in Search Results (Configurable in Control Deck)
docs.text:
In Control Deck > "Search" > "Opening search results", "Search Result Path Click Behavior" offers three choices for what happens when you click the path column in search results. The default is "Same pane, new tab".

Option Behavior Best suited for Show in same tab Switches from the search results to the normal listing and shows the path in the same tab. Navigate quickly to folders without adding tabs. Same pane, new tab Opens a new tab in the same pane. Keep the search results tab while opening clicked paths in separate tabs. The default, and handy alongside search. Other pane, new tab Results from Pane A open in a new tab in Pane B, and vice versa. Switches to dual-pane automatically in single-pane mode. For comparison work and advanced users. View search results and opened folders side by side.

docs.title: AI Features
docs.text: Every feature here needs a provider set up first in Setting Up Generative AI. The AI views in the nav pane (AI Folder Analysis, AI Manual, AI Tab Management) are not on the icon bar of a new installation; call them with a key or the command palette, or add them to the icon bar (see Nav Pane).

docs.title: AI Theme Diagnosis
docs.text:
• Operation: Control Deck > "Theme" > "Start AI Diagnosis" under "Theme Wizard", or the AI diagnosis button in "Theme Store"
  • How it works: Answer 3-5 multiple-choice questions to receive 3-5 recommended themes (your own themes when started from the Theme page, store themes when started from the Theme Store)
  • Suggests themes with an explanation of why they match, ready to apply
  • Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day from either entry, shared with AI theme generation)

docs.title: AI Theme Generation
docs.text: - Operation: Control Deck > Theme > AI Theme Generation - How it works: Describe in natural language (e.g., "a dark theme inspired by outer space") to generate an original full-palette theme - Live preview for instant verification > request adjustments > save - Becomes available after you have switched themes 30 times - Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day, shared with AI theme diagnosis) - Generated themes are added to the "AI Generated" category, with automatic category classification based on color analysis - A 35-point quality check (body-text contrast, saturation, accent consistency, and more) runs automatically; if a generated theme falls short, an AI-assisted fix-up pass and local auto-correction bring it back within readability targets - Dialog layout: Top to bottom, the dialog is ordered "Basics" > "Colors & palette" > "Tone" > "World & imagery," each section carrying a short explanation of what you decide there. The Generate button sits in the footer (next to Close). Every selection is optional — anything you leave alone is decided by the AI - Tooltips: Hover over any selection button — brightness, vividness, colors, moods or scenes — to see a description of what palette and impression that choice produces, so you can check a tag's effect before committing to it - Basics: Enter the theme name, then a free-text theme description, then set the proper-noun masking option. You cannot generate with both the description and all chips left empty - Colors & palette: Specify colors per UI role (one choice per row; all default to "Auto") - Main color: Backgrounds and large surfaces (base color) - Sub color: Tiles, cards, and section backgrounds. Besides concrete colors, you can specify it relationally as "Same family as main" or "Contrast with main" - Accent: Highlights and active states - Font color: Tendency for all text ("Auto (harmonize with background)," "Clear black," "Clear white") - Available colors include hue families (blue, green, purple, red, pink, orange/brown, gold/yellow, cyan/teal, monochrome, colorful) plus tone and texture families (white & ivory, black & jet black, gray & neutral, pastel & dreamy, dusty & earth tones, vivid & neon, metallic & glossy, clear & translucent) - Tone: Choose brightness (Auto / Light / Dark) and vividness (Auto / Muted / Standard / Vivid) - World & imagery: Select any number of moods (Simple & practical / Emotional / Fantasy & dark) and scenes (Everyday, nature & materials / Sci-fi & technology / Fantasy & otherworldly). Each category carries a short description of its direction - Exclusions (right-click): Right-click a mood or scene tag to mark it as "never include in this theme" (blue background + strikethrough). The AI keeps that direction out of the palette, materials, lighting, silhouette, theme name and descriptions, and won't drift toward the color families it evokes. Exclusions outrank both your selected tags and the free-text description. Right-click again to clear, or right-click a selected tag to flip it straight to excluded. You can generate from exclusions alone (they are not saved as theme tags) - "Clear selections" (to the right of the Colors & palette heading) clears every color, tone, and world selection, returning each row to "Auto" - Blur proper nouns (recommended for rights protection): A checkbox directly below the description field (on by default). When it is on, all proper nouns (character names, work/title names, brand names, real people, and so on) are stripped from the generated theme name and description, leaving only the color scheme and mood. The AI automatically assigns an evocative, proper-noun-free English name (for example, "Eva Unit-01" becomes "Berserker Violet"), and the description is expressed purely in terms of color, light, material, and mood. Masking works as translation rather than deletion: the source's iconic color pairings, materials, light sources, silhouettes and era are each converted into proper-noun-free language, so turning masking on does not make the description shorter or vaguer. When it is off, behavior is as before — the theme name you entered is used as-is and the description reflects your concept — but the generated theme may contain copyrighted or trademarked wording. Personal use is fine, but beware of rights infringement when publishing or sharing. The setting is remembered by the app

docs.title: AI Theme Adjustment
docs.text:
• Operation: Right-click a theme card > "Adjust with AI"
  • How it works: Give natural language instructions for color changes (e.g., "make it darker," "change accent to red tones")
  • Changes are immediately reflected in the preview
  • The customization dialog is non-modal, so you can interact with the app's file lists and nav pane while the dialog remains open, allowing you to verify the applied theme before saving
  • Automatic WCAG contrast validation ensures readability
  • When the "Blur proper nouns" setting is on, customizing an existing theme also strips proper nouns from the description (customization does not rename the theme)
  • Pro feature (free version: 3 uses/day, shared with theme customization)

docs.title: AI Folder Analysis
docs.text:
• Location: AI Folder Organizer view in the nav pane
  • Analysis: Press "Analyze" for an AI-generated 3-section report (📊 Current State / ⚠️ Issues / 💡 Improvement Suggestions)
  • Action generation: Approve with YES/NO to generate specific actions (folder creation, moves, renames). There is no item limit; actions are produced for every file that needs organizing
  • Execution: Select individually via checkboxes > batch execute > Undo (Ctrl+Z) supported
  • Additional instructions can be given in chat format. Markdown export of chat history is also supported
  • Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day)

docs.title: AI Manual (Help Q&A)
docs.text:
• Location: AI Manual view in the nav pane, or from the document viewer dialog
  • How it works: Ask questions about app usage in natural language; the system automatically searches the manual and provides accurate answers
  • Covers app settings, key bindings, theme lists, and more
  • Markdown rendering supported; long answers displayed in split bubbles
  • Beneath each answer, the articles it drew on (up to three) are listed; clicking one opens that article in the manual at the relevant heading. When you are using the dialog, it closes first and then the manual opens
  • If the display language is neither Japanese nor English, the answer is based on the English manual and written in your display language
  • Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day)

docs.title: AI Tab Management
docs.text:
• Location: AI Tab Management view in the nav pane
  • Scoring: Evaluates tabs using frequency 30% + dwell time 30% + recency 40%, suggesting lock/close actions
  • Working set detection: Automatically detects working sets from A+B pane co-occurrence patterns
  • Related folder suggestions: Suggests related folders based on co-occurrence history
  • Indicators displayed on tab headers; "Apply all" for batch operations
  • Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day)

docs.title: AI Usage Statistics Analysis
docs.text:
• Operation: Control Deck > Statistics > "AI Usage Analysis" section at the top
  • How it works: Press "Analyze" to analyze your statistics together (action counts, frequently opened folders, favorites, time spent in tabs and more) and pick 3-7 insights the data supports from the 9 kinds below
  • Kinds of insight: Unregistered frequent folders, hidden workflows, search optimization, quick-flip tabs, underutilized features, dead favorites, operation style bias, dual-pane utilization, AI usage patterns (which AI features you use and how tokens are spent)
  • Each insight is presented as a "finding + specific action suggestion" pair
  • Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day)

docs.title: AI File Name Suggestions
docs.text:
• Location: "AI Suggestions" section within the file/folder rename dialog
  • How it works: Considers parent folder structure, sibling file naming conventions, and rename history to suggest 3-5 candidates
  • Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day)

docs.title: AI Favorite Descriptions
docs.text:
• Location: "Write the description with AI: On / Off" in the Add to favorites window (★ in the address bar / Ctrl + D / "Add to favorites" on the right-click menu), and "Descriptions when adding favorites" in the list of automatic AI functions on the Overview tab of Settings → AI
  • How it works: Writes one short description from the folder's name, parent folders, neighboring folders and contents, and from the way you have written favorite descriptions before, and puts it in the description box. Tags such as "AI: ..." and boilerplate such as "Added automatically after N visits" are not used as examples
  • Behavior: When it is on, the description is written as soon as the Add window opens. Switching from Off to On in the window writes it right away as well. You can edit the result. If you start typing in the description box while it is being written, what you typed wins
  • Remembered choice: The window and the Settings page share one setting, and the next time you add a favorite it is used as is. It is off by default
  • If the neighboring folders are on Box or a network share and take a long time to read, it gives up after 5 seconds and writes the description from the name and location only
  • No usage limits (free)

docs.title: Talk to Stickman
docs.text:
• Location: hover over Stickman on the status bar, and click it once it has said something
  • How it works: sends what you typed, the last three exchanges, and a rough picture of the moment (time of day, the kind of thing you just did) to the generative AI, and gets back a short reply and one gesture for Stickman to act out. No file or folder names or paths are sent. Gestures come only from the moves Stickman has, and nothing in the app is operated. See Mascot (Stickman)
  • Pro feature (5 times a day in the free version)

docs.title: AI Favorites Organization
docs.text:
• Location: Open ⚙ (favorites settings) in the Favorites view and press "Organize favorites with AI" (if your favorites are locked, unlock them first)
  • How it works: Let AI analyze and optimize your favorites structure. Supports container classification suggestions, name improvements, and automatic custom icon assignment
  • Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day)

docs.title: AI Backup Summary
docs.text:
• Location: Runs automatically during settings backup. It is off on new installations; turn it on in the list of automatic features on Control Deck › AI ("Backup AI Summary")
  • What is sent: the old and new values of the changed settings, which can include folder paths such as your favorites and home folders. See the Privacy Policy for what is sent where
  • How it works: When backing up settings, AI automatically generates a natural-language summary of the changes. You can review a summary of each backup version's changes in the backup list
  • Limit: 2 times a day on the free edition. After that, the summary quietly falls back to the plain list of changes without AI

docs.title: AI Folder Creation
docs.text:
You can request AI to generate a folder structure by clicking the ✨ button next to the new folder icon in the pane header. On a new installation (toolbar "Number of buttons" set to "Fewer") this button is hidden; set it to "Standard" under "Toolbar" in Control Deck, or turn this button on. It is a Pro feature (free version: 2 uses/day).

  • Prompt input: Describe the purpose or intended use of the folders you want to create in natural language. The more specific you are (target time period, classification criteria, naming convention preferences, etc.), the better the results
  • Priority chips: Use four chip buttons — "Relevance," "Structure," "Naming," and "Scalability" — to adjust the AI's proposal strategy. If none are selected, the AI decides automatically
  • Self-evaluation: The AI self-evaluates its proposal across 4 axes (relevance, structure, naming, scalability) plus an overall score, displaying star ratings and comments at the top of the preview
  • Integration with existing folders: When existing folders are present, the AI proposes three types of actions: create new (🟢), keep (🔵), and rename (🟡). Renames are only proposed for unifying naming conventions (e.g., adding number prefixes)
  • File pattern analysis: The existing file names and timestamps in the folder are sent to the AI, which detects patterns such as year-month or sequential numbering, and proposes a comprehensive folder structure
  • Regeneration with additional instructions: After the preview is displayed, use the "Additional instructions" button to add conditions and regenerate (e.g., "Create folders for all months from 2024 to 2026")
  • Individual exclusion via checkboxes: Uncheck individual folders to exclude them from execution
  • Undo support: Created folders can be batch-deleted with Undo

docs.title: AI Token Statistics
docs.text: • Under "Statistics" in Control Deck, you can check monthly and per-model token usage and estimated costs

docs.title: AI/Pro Badges
docs.text:
• AI features display a Sparkles badge, and Pro (licensed) features display a Lock badge (their colors follow the theme)
  • Shown in the nav pane icon bar, view headers, and settings screens
  • Toggle with Control Deck > "Display" > "Show AI / Pro badges". It is off on new installations

docs.title: Setting Up Generative AI
docs.text: Zenith Filer includes AI-powered assistance features (listed in AI Features). Configure the API provider and key in Control Deck > AI before use.

docs.title: AI Provider Settings
docs.text:
• Location: Control Deck > AI
  • Supported providers: Claude / OpenAI / Azure OpenAI / Gemini / Ollama / Claude Code (CLI)
  • API key management: Encrypted with DPAPI and stored locally only (never sent externally). Use "Clear" to remove saved keys
  • Test connection: Verify API key validity with the "Test Connection" button in the API key section. On failure, displays HTTP status code-specific guidance (invalid key, insufficient permissions, rate limit, etc.)
  • Model selection: Choose from a dropdown per provider (defaults used when empty)
  • Model validation: Use the "Validate Model" button in the model section to verify whether the selected model is actually available. Catches model name typos and access permission issues before use
  • Response wait time: Set on the Overview tab. The default, "Automatic", picks the wait from what you are talking to (30 seconds for cloud providers, 2 minutes for reasoning models, 4 minutes for Claude Code, 5 minutes for locally run models such as Ollama). A model running on your own PC can spend several minutes just loading itself the first time, so choose 5 or 10 minutes if replies are being cut off
  • Automatic API format handling for OpenAI / Azure OpenAI: Older models like GPT-4.1 require the Chat Completions API, while newer-generation models like the GPT-5 series require the Responses API. The correct format is inferred automatically from the model name, and if that guess turns out wrong, an error response is detected and the request is automatically retried against the other format — so you can just pick a model without worrying about which API it needs
  • AI ON/OFF: Toggle AI features via the Sparkles icon in the status bar. Long-press to open settings directly
  • Ollama (local LLM) provider: Supports the Ollama provider for local execution without an API key. Features one-click automatic installation, recommended model download management, and automatic server start/stop. When Ollama is not installed, the Ollama tab displays a step-by-step setup guide:
  • Install Ollama — One-click automatic download and installation
  • Start the server — Start the server after installation completes
  • Download a model — Select and download from recommended models

Each step updates its display based on completion status. Once the server is running, the guide disappears and the normal settings screen (endpoint, model selection, recommended model list) is shown - Claude Code (CLI) provider: Runs your locally installed Claude Code in headless mode — no API key needed. If you are logged in with a Claude subscription (Pro/Max), all AI features work without configuring a key - Prerequisites: Claude Code CLI is installed, and you have logged in by running claude in a terminal and using /login - Installation detection: The Claude Code tab shows the detection status and version. The CLI is auto-detected from the default install location (%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\claude.exe) and PATH; an executable path override is available if needed - Model selection: Choose from default (the CLI's own default model) / sonnet / opus / haiku / fable - Limitations: The MaxTokens/Temperature settings are not applied with this provider. Responses have a few seconds of startup overhead due to the CLI launch, and behavior may change when Claude Code itself is updated - 7-tab AI settings layout: AI settings are divided into 7 sub-tabs: Overview, Ollama, Gemini, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Claude, and Claude Code. "Auto AI Features" on the Overview tab turns each AI function that runs without you asking on or off individually (AI Greeting, AI Rename Suggestion, Challenge Title Generation, Backstory Generation, Backup AI Summary, Descriptions when adding favorites). The favorite description setting can also be switched in the Add to favorites window (see AI Favorite Descriptions)

docs.title: Macros (Automating Actions)
docs.text: Zenith Filer includes a "Macros" feature for automating the operations you perform most often. Macros are JavaScript under the hood, but you can build them without writing any code — wire parts (blocks) together in Macro Studio, or record your actual operations — so they are approachable even for first-time users. Creation and editing always happen in Macro Studio; the nav pane's "Macros" view is dedicated to listing and running saved macros.

docs.title: Where to Find Macros
docs.text:
• The "Macros" view in the nav pane: A permanent view alongside Favorites, Tree, and the others (its icon is a lightning bolt ⚡). It lists your saved macros — each entry shows its name, badges for any configured triggers, and a ▶ run button. Double-click to run, or right-click for Run / Edit in Studio / Duplicate / Delete. The "+" button in the header opens Macro Studio in a fresh, new-macro state. A new installation does not put this view on the nav pane's icon bar; open it with Ctrl+K then M in Zenith 2 or from the command palette, or add it to the icon bar (see Nav Pane).
  • The two icons on the right side of the status bar: Buttons for invoking macros quickly.
  • ⏺ (Record): Starts and stops action recording.
  • ⚡ (Saved macros): Opens a dropdown of your saved macros; click one to run it directly. "+ New Macro" opens Macro Studio, and each entry's right-click menu offers "Edit in Studio".
  • Macro Studio: The standalone window where macros are created and edited (see Macro Studio).

docs.title: How Execution Works (the zen.* API)
docs.text:
Under the hood, a macro describes app operations using the dedicated zen.* API. The main calls are:

  • Navigate (navigate) / Search (search)
  • Create folder (createFolder) / Move (move) / Rename (rename) / Copy (copy) / Delete (delete, to the Recycle Bin)
  • Notify (notify) / Log (log)
  • Asking at run time (confirm for yes/no, prompt for text, promptFolder for a folder)

  • Calling the app's own features (action): zen.action("FileList.BatchRename") reaches every action listed under Shortcuts in Settings (including ones with no key assigned), so compression, extraction, Grep, folder compare, sync, batch rename, hashing, favourites and the rest are available even though the macro vocabulary has no call of its own for them. Misspelling an action produces an error naming the closest matches. An action is only started, not waited for, so put a "⏱ Wait" after it if the macro goes on to touch the result

  • Safety: File operations (create, move, rename, copy, delete) are confined to the folder currently being displayed, and their safety is validated before they run. Using ..\, writing an absolute path that points elsewhere, or naming a neighbouring folder whose name merely looks similar (work2 while work is open) all stop before anything happens, and escaping through a shortcut — a symbolic link or junction — is closed off the same way. The folder you currently have open cannot be named as the target of a delete, move or rename either. On top of that, a single macro run is capped at 500 destructive operations. Copying a folder into itself is stopped too. When a macro deletes something in a place without a Recycle Bin (a network folder, a USB drive and so on), Windows asks before deleting it permanently.

  • Time limit: A runaway macro (an endless loop, for example) is stopped once the time the macro itself has been running goes over 2 minutes. Time spent answering a confirmation or input box, copying or moving files, or in "⏱ Wait" is not counted.
  • It can be stopped: While a macro runs, Macro Studio's toolbar shows "⏹ Stop". Pressing it interrupts the run on the spot, and everything done up to that point comes back with a single Ctrl+Z. Stop applies to macros started anywhere — the studio's ▶, the nav pane list, the status bar, a keyboard shortcut or the command palette. No macro starts while another is running, which keeps the same macro from being launched twice and fighting itself over the same files.
  • Failures name the line: Errors read ❌ Error: line 3: ..., so where it fell over is part of the message. Typos (syntax errors) report their line the same way.
  • Undo as one step: Everything a macro does can be rolled back together with a single Undo (Ctrl+Z). Deletions (delete) are the exception — sending a file to the Recycle Bin is outside Ctrl+Z elsewhere in the app too, so a macro that deleted anything says so at the end of its output (restore those items from the Recycle Bin). If anything could not be rolled back, the notification reports how many failed and which ones.

docs.title: Action Recording
docs.text:
You can capture your actual operations and turn them into a macro.

  1. Press ⏺ (Start recording) on the status bar.
  2. Work as usual. What gets recorded: navigating folders, searching, selecting items, copying, moving, renaming, deleting to the Recycle Bin, creating folders, and opening and closing tabs.
  3. Stop recording. Macro Studio opens automatically with your operations laid out as nodes (parts), ready for you to add parts or change arguments.

From there you can run it, edit it, or name and save it.

Finer points of recording:

  • Only the final selection is kept. The back-and-forth while you change your selection is not recorded.
  • Copies and moves that leave the current folder are not recorded. A macro's file operations are confined to the current folder, so they could not be replayed (dragging to another drive is one example).
  • Anything that cannot be expressed as a part is kept as a "🧩 Script" part for just that step, so nothing you recorded is lost. Only when not a single step could be turned back into a part does the macro open on the Code tab, as before.

docs.title: AI Integration
docs.text: With zen.ai you can ask the AI to classify files or propose organizing actions, then run operations based on the result (this requires a generative-AI setup; see AI Provider Settings for how to configure it). It's available as the "🤖 AI Organize" block in Macro Studio's parts palette.

docs.title: Saving and Reusing
docs.text:
Name and save your macro from Macro Studio (macros are stored in the macros folder inside the data folder). Editing and saving an already-saved macro overwrites it (use "Duplicate" first if you want to keep it as a separate new macro). Saved macros can be invoked from:

  • The list in the "Macros" view of the nav pane (double-click or ▶ to run)
  • The ⚡ (Saved macros) dropdown on the right side of the status bar (click to run)

docs.title: Triggers (Automatic Execution)
docs.text:
Each saved macro can be given conditions (triggers) for running automatically. Configure them from Macro Studio's properties column (shown only while editing an already-saved macro).

  • Run when the app starts: Tick it to run the macro automatically once the app has started and finished opening its first folder.
  • Run every day at this time: Tick it and choose the hour and minute below. Changing the time saves it right away.
  • Run with a key: Click the box, then press the keys you want (e.g., Ctrl+Shift+M). It is the same control as Shortcuts in Settings, and a warning appears below the box when the keys clash with another feature. Delete removes the key and Esc cancels. Two-stroke keys (such as Ctrl+K, M) work too. The same macro also has a row under "Macros" in Settings > Shortcuts, and changing it in either place changes both.
  • Watch a folder and run when its contents change (hot folder): Ticking it opens a folder picker, and "Choose folder…" picks a different one. A macro started by a watch treats the watched folder as the current folder (not the folder open in your tab). Unticking it keeps the chosen folder so it is used again the next time you tick it. If the watched folder can't be found when the app starts (a USB drive that isn't plugged in, for example), you are told and the watch is not started.

Configured triggers appear as badges in the nav pane's list and in Macro Studio's library column.

docs.title: Using Macros Safely
docs.text:
• Confirm before running: A confirmation dialog via zen.confirm and pre-run validation (dry run) help prevent unintended data loss.
  • Unsaved-change protection: While editing in Macro Studio, switching the library selection, starting a new macro, or closing the window with unsaved changes prompts a discard-confirmation dialog.
  • Free-version limits: AI features and macro execution have a limit on the number of uses in the free version (the Full version is required to use them without that limit).

docs.title: Macro Studio
docs.text:
Macro Studio opens from the nav pane's "+", a saved macro's right-click "Edit in Studio", the status bar's "+ New Macro", and similar entry points. Part names, their descriptions, the example inputs and even the presets are available in all ten languages, following your display-language setting. It's the sole place macros are created and edited, and it's modeless (a separate window), so you can keep browsing and operating on folders in the background while it is open. It has three columns:

  • Left: Library column — The list of saved macros. Selecting one switches the edit target (with a confirmation if there are unsaved changes). Right-click to duplicate, export or delete.
  • Passing macros around: "Export…" in the right-click menu saves a macro as a single .json, and "Import…" in the column header brings one in. Before importing, you see what the macro does — deletes files, moves them, sends a request to the AI and so on — and decide from there. An imported macro does not run: it opens in the studio so you can look it over. Its id is reissued on import, and its triggers (startup, schedule, watch, shortcut) are not carried over, so a macro someone sent you never starts running the moment it arrives.
  • Center: Editing area (Node / Code tabs)
  • Node tab: Build macros by combining parts (blocks) like a puzzle on a large 2D canvas.
    • Let the AI build it: Type what you want in the field above the canvas and press "✨ Generate" — the macro appears on the canvas already assembled (for example, "file the PDFs into monthly folders and notify me"). What comes out is an ordinary macro, so you can keep adding parts and editing arguments. Generating does not run it — look it over, then press "▶ Run". If it isn't what you meant, reword the request and press Generate again. The name of the folder you have open and what is in it (the first 40 items) are sent along, so phrases like "the selected files" make sense to it (the folder's full path is not sent). If the canvas already holds nodes, you are asked before they are replaced. Requires an AI provider (AI Provider Settings). While it works, "Cancel" stops it.
    • Tidy the layout: "≡ Tidy" at the top-left of the canvas re-arranges the cards to follow their connections — a straight run into a single column, a branch sending "yes" down and "no" into the column to its right, and a loop putting its body in the column to the right with what follows it below. It is the same layout the AI generator uses, so hand-built and generated macros look alike. The cards are not rebuilt: connections and the values you typed stay as they are, only the positions move. Cards connected to nothing are gathered in a column at the right.
    • Canvas navigation: Left-drag empty space to pan the canvas. Hold Shift and left-drag to marquee-select a rectangular area, so you can select and move several cards at once.
    • Place parts: Drag & drop blocks from the "Parts" palette on the left onto the canvas (clicking also adds them). Hovering over a part shows a description of what it does. Selecting a card highlights parts that naturally follow its output with a "★ Suggested" badge in the palette, so you always know what to add next (it learns from the combinations you actually use).
    • Connect: Wire the "sockets" (connectors) on the left/right of blocks together to set the run order (upstream → downstream). Connection lines automatically route around cards instead of overlapping them.
    • Configure (in the right pane, just pick): Click a card and its "Part settings" open in the right pane. The card itself only shows what the part is and its current value; you change the value here — far easier than typing inside a narrow card. Depending on the field type, the inputs offer "📁 Browse (folder picker)", a dropdown of the current folder's contents, "{ } Tokens" (insert the date and similar), and "▾ Presets" (commonly used values), so you can configure them with minimal typing. The same place shows what the part does and the JavaScript it produces. The selected card is outlined in the accent colour.
    • Conditional branching: The "🔀 Branch" block has two outlets, "Yes / No". You can split the flow by a condition (has selection / has items / confirmed OK / file exists / custom expression); at run time it is converted to if / else.
    • Repeat: The "🔁 Repeat" block has two outlets, "repeat" and "afterwards". What you connect to "repeat" is the body; what you connect to "afterwards" runs once the loop is done. Choose what to walk over — the folder's contents or the selected items — and optionally add a filter such as *.pdf (filters do not apply to a selection). Inside the loop the current item is available as {item} (name), {itemExt} (extension), {itemPath} (full path) and {itemDate:yyyy-MM} (modified date) — these tokens only mean anything inside a loop. Something like "file all the PDFs into monthly folders" can be built without writing any script. With one loop inside another, {item} after the inner loop still means the outer loop's item. Parts can't be connected in a ring (the line just isn't drawn; repetition is what this block is for).
    • Asking for a value at run time: Writing {prompt:Enter a prefix} in an argument brings up an input box when the macro runs and drops what you type into that spot; {promptFolder} opens the folder picker instead. One macro can then be reused with different values. Cancelling the input stops the macro then and there.
    • Script part: The "🧩 Script" block lets you write JavaScript directly, in the right pane's "Part settings". Use it for anything the other parts cannot express — walking a list and branching on a condition, such as sorting by extension or moving only the files above a certain size. What you write becomes part of the macro as-is (the available calls are the zen.* API in How Execution Works (the zen.* API)).
    • Example parts: Navigate, Create Folder, Rename, Organize-Move, Copy, Delete to Recycle Bin (recoverable), Search, Select, Notify, Log, New Tab, Close Tab, Go Up, Go Home, Refresh, Wait, AI Organize, Sequential Rename, Branch, Repeat, Script.
    • Adjust card width: Drag the grip on the right edge of each node card left/right to change its width. Growing a card, or dragging it to a new position, automatically nudges any overlapping downstream card out of the way.
  • Code tab: Shows the generated JavaScript. Hand-written or freshly-recorded macros (with no node graph) can be edited directly here. Macros that originated from a node graph are read-only here, to prevent an accidental overwrite from a stale hand-edit — edit those in the Node tab instead. Line numbers are shown and keywords, strings, numbers and comments are coloured — the colours come from the theme, so the code stays readable whichever one you use. The "🧩 Script" part's editor looks the same.
  • Right: Properties column — The top section is "Part settings" for the selected card (click a card to open it). Below that you edit the macro's name and description, and for an already-saved macro configure triggers (startup / daily / hotkey / watch). The most recent run output is always pinned at the bottom.
  • Run history: Opening "Run history" below the output lists the last 30 runs, newest first, with the time, the macro's name, whether it succeeded, and how long it took. The mark at the start of each row is where the run came from: ▶ manual / ⏻ startup / ⏰ schedule / 👁 folder watch. Hovering shows a summary of the result — the reason, when it failed. This is where you check whether an automatic run actually happened. The list keeps 200 entries, dropping the oldest, and "Clear history" empties it.
  • Toolbar: "+ New" resets to a fresh new-macro state, "▶ Run" executes, "⏺ Start Recording" / "⏹ Stop Recording" toggles action recording, and "💾 Save" saves (overwriting the macro currently open, if any).

docs.title: How Keybindings Work
docs.text:
Section summary Every key in the app is decided by one table, under "Shortcuts" in Control Deck. Click a row's key and press the keys you want to record them (two-key shortcuts work too); a changed key takes effect immediately, everywhere in the app. Keys you give to macros appear in the same table under the "Macros" group, so a clash with another action shows up right away.

  • Changing a key: as the page says, "Click a key binding and press a key to change it" — click the key at the right end of a row, then press the keys. Typing an action name or a key in the box at the top (for example copy or Ctrl+C) filters the list. The groups are "Global", "Tab", "Search", "Sidebar", "Window", "File List" and "Macros".
  • Clash warnings: a row shows a warning when another action already uses the same key, or when you give it a key that starts a two-key shortcut (such as Ctrl+K) on its own.
  • Where keys work: a changed key works the same everywhere in the app. Only keys that are fixed everywhere — a dialog's Esc / Enter, moving with the arrow keys in a list, and the like — cannot be changed (see Keyboard Shortcut Reference).
  • Export / Import: "Export" writes all the current assignments to a JSON file. "Import" reads such a file, first returning everything to the defaults and then applying the file's assignments (your current assignments are replaced). Use it to carry your keys to another PC.
  • Back to the defaults: a row's "Reset to default" restores just that action, and "Reset all to default" restores every action to the Zenith standard defaults.
  • Tooltips: button tooltips show the current key, as in Rename (F2), and update as soon as you change it.
  • Key schemes (presets): the card above the table applies a whole key scheme at once (see Choosing a key scheme).
  • Actions without a key: anything you can do from the screen can be called by name from the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P), even with no key assigned.

docs.title: Keyboard and Mouse Interaction
docs.text:
• Pane and nav focus switches on click: To move keyboard focus to the nav pane (favorites, tree, history and so on) or Pane A / Pane B, click the target area with the mouse. From the keyboard, F6 / Shift+F6 step through the areas, nav pane included (in Zenith 2, Ctrl+K followed by one key opens that view and moves focus into it). Between Pane A and Pane B, use ←/→ (and Tab in Zenith standard).

    Hovering (just moving the mouse over) does not move focus, ensuring operations target the intended pane.

  • Focus to list: When Pane A or Pane B has focus but the file list does not (e.g., immediately after startup or after clicking a tab or toolbar), pressing arrow keys, Enter, Delete, F2, or similar keys moves focus to the list and the pressed key takes effect immediately.

    When focus is on the path input field or search box, key input is used by those fields as usual.

  • Mouse interference prevention during keyboard operation: When keyboard operations begin (arrow keys, Enter, shortcuts, etc.), the app automatically enters "keyboard operation mode" and the mouse cursor is hidden.

    During this time, hovering the mouse over the list or nav pane does not move selection or focus (preventing accidental focus jumps to items under the mouse cursor).

  • Automatic return to mouse operation: During keyboard operation mode, physically moving the mouse approximately 3 or more pixels from its previous position automatically restores the mouse cursor, returning to normal mouse operation.

    A dead zone prevents recovery from slight vibrations. Opening modal dialogs (like the rename dialog) also auto-restores the cursor when window focus changes, allowing mouse operation within the dialog.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcut Reference
docs.text: Settings > Shortcuts lets you pick a key scheme (a preset). Whichever you choose, every individual key can still be rebound. A new installation starts with "Zenith 2 (two-key)"; if you are upgrading from an earlier version you keep "Zenith standard".

docs.title: Choosing a key scheme
docs.text:
Preset Character Zenith standard One key, one action. The long-standing assignments. If you are upgrading from an earlier version, this is what you have. Choosing it returns every key except macro keys to these defaults Zenith 2 (two-key) Ctrl+K then one key opens a view; Ctrl+B drives the panes and the layout. Hold the prefix a moment and the keys you can press next appear, so there is nothing to memorise. This is the default on a fresh install Explorer style Backspace and Alt+← to go back, Alt+↑ to go up, Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 to switch tabs — the finger habits of Windows Explorer Total Commander style F5 to copy, F6 to move, F8 to delete (Shift+F8 to delete permanently). A function-key-centred scheme AFXW style C to copy, M to move, D to delete, K to make a folder. The single-key scheme of AFXW, a Japanese file manager, with no modifier keys involved

Applying a scheme rewrites only the keys of the actions that scheme defines (keys you changed yourself are replaced too, so before applying you are shown how many keys will change and how many of those were your own). Actions the scheme does not define keep their current keys.

docs.title: Main differences between the schemes
docs.text:
Compared with Zenith standard, these keys change. Anything not listed works as in Zenith standard.

  • Zenith 2: adds the two-key shortcuts under Ctrl+K and Ctrl+B (see Zenith 2 two-key shortcuts). In exchange, the sidebar keys Ctrl+Shift+1–8 are removed, and the pane keys Ctrl+Shift+Q, Ctrl+Shift+W, Ctrl+Shift+`, Ctrl+3, Ctrl+Shift+[, Ctrl+Shift+], Ctrl+Shift+L, Ctrl+Shift+J and Ctrl+Shift+S move to Ctrl+B sequences. Tab no longer switches panes (use ← →)
  • Explorer style: Backspace goes back instead of up (as does Alt+←), and going up is Alt+↑. Ctrl+1–Ctrl+8 jump to the 1st–8th tab from the left and Ctrl+9 to the rightmost tab. Ctrl+Shift+2–8 switch the view instead of the sidebar (2 large icons, 3 medium icons, 4 small icons, 5 list, 6 details, 7 tiles, 8 content; Ctrl+Shift+1 for Favorites stays). Ctrl+3 for the top/bottom split is removed
  • Total Commander style: F3 Quick Preview (instead of Space), F4 open in text editor, F5 copy to the other pane, F6 move to the other pane, Shift+F6 rename (instead of F2), F7 new folder, F8 delete, Shift+F8 delete permanently, Alt+F7 search, Ctrl+F6 / Ctrl+Shift+F6 focus the next / previous area (instead of F6), Ctrl+R refresh (instead of F5), Ctrl+D switch the sidebar to Favorites (the add-to-favorites key is removed)
  • AFXW style: while the file list has focus, single keys work: C copy to the other pane, M move to the other pane, D delete, K new folder, R rename, A select all, N copy path, E open in text editor, I properties, V Quick Preview, F search, L Drives, H History, J Recent Folders (the original keys such as Ctrl+C for these are removed; you can still type these letters normally in the path box and search box). Backspace goes up, Tab switches panes, Enter opens

docs.title: Zenith Standard keys
docs.text:
These are the keys you can change under Shortcuts in Settings (Zenith standard defaults).

General

Key Action Ctrl + Z Undo (rename, move, copy, create, a delete to the Recycle Bin, etc.) Ctrl + Y Redo (a rename, move or new folder undone with Ctrl + Z) Ctrl + Shift + E Toggle the app's visibility (global hotkey): when the app is the foreground window it is hidden (stored to the tray and removed from the taskbar in resident mode, otherwise minimized); when hidden/minimized/in the background it is brought to the front and focus moves to the active file pane. This is the one shortcut registered system-wide, so it cannot be claimed if another app — a background utility, for example — is already using the same combination. A warning then appears under Control Deck → "Shortcuts"; pick a free key there instead Ctrl + Shift + O Open Settings (Control Deck) Ctrl + Shift + P Command palette (find and run any action by name; see Command Palette) Ctrl + Shift + Space Ring Launcher (see Ring Launcher) Ctrl + P Quick Jump (search across favorites, history and frequent folders and go there) Ctrl + F / Ctrl + E Focus on the active pane's search bar (exits index search mode if active) Ctrl + Shift + F Focus on the search bar and enter index search mode Ctrl + Shift + G Switch to file content search (grep) mode Ctrl + I Filter the current folder in place (enters the search bar's Filter mode) Ctrl + Shift + Q Switch to single-pane mode (Pane A only) Ctrl + Shift + W Switch to dual-pane mode (Pane A + Pane B) Ctrl + Shift + ` Toggle between single-pane and dual-pane mode Ctrl + 3 Switch to top-bottom dual-pane mode

Tabs

Key Action Ctrl + T Open a new tab Ctrl + W Close the current tab Ctrl + Shift + T Reopen a closed tab (up to 20 until the app closes) Ctrl + Shift + D Duplicate tab Ctrl + N Duplicate the current tab's folder into the other pane (switches to dual-pane when only one is shown) Ctrl + L / Alt + D Focus on the address bar Ctrl + Shift + A Show tab list Ctrl + Shift + Alt + 1 Show Pane A's tab list Ctrl + Shift + Alt + 2 Show Pane B's tab list Ctrl + Tab Switch to the next tab Ctrl + Shift + Tab Switch to the previous tab

Sidebar (nav pane views)

Key Action Ctrl + Shift + 1 Switch sidebar to "Favorites" Ctrl + Shift + 2 Switch sidebar to "Tree" Ctrl + Shift + 3 Switch sidebar to "History" Ctrl + Shift + 4 Switch sidebar to "Index Search" Ctrl + Shift + 5 Switch sidebar to "Working Set" Ctrl + Shift + 6 Switch sidebar to "Recent Folders" Ctrl + Shift + 7 Switch sidebar to "Recent Files" Ctrl + Shift + 8 Switch sidebar to "Properties"

Window and panes

Key Action Space / Alt + P Quick Preview: Overlay preview of the selected file's contents (supports text, images, PDF, HTML, Excel/CSV, Office documents; press Space again or Esc to close) Tab Toggle focus between Pane A and Pane B. While renaming in place in the list, it commits the name and starts renaming the next row (Shift + Tab for the previous row) Left Arrow When focus is on Pane B, switch to Pane A (in icon view it moves the selection left instead) Right Arrow When focus is on Pane A, switch to Pane B (in dual-pane mode; in icon view it moves the selection right instead) F6 / Shift + F6 Step through the areas: left nav top → left nav bottom → address bar → search box → pane A → pane B → right nav top → right nav bottom (like File Explorer, it also stops at the address bar and search box; the address bar is skipped while hidden during a search). Closed areas, and pane B in single-pane mode, are skipped. This is also how you get out of the terminal Ctrl + Shift + L Open the window layout presets Ctrl + Shift + J Open the nav pane layout presets Ctrl + Shift + S Open working set quick access Ctrl + Shift + [ Show/hide the left navigation pane Ctrl + Shift + ] Show/hide the right navigation pane F11 Toggle full screen

File list

Key Action Enter Open folder / Execute file / Folder shortcuts (.lnk) open the link target folder in a new tab Backspace / Alt + Up Arrow Go up one level Alt + Left Arrow Go back to the previous folder Alt + Right Arrow Go forward to the next folder F5 / Ctrl + R Refresh folder contents F2 Rename Shift + F2 Batch Rename: rename the selected items in one pass, following a rule set (Batch Rename) Ctrl + Shift + N Create a new folder (focus moves to it with rename ready) Ctrl + C Copy Ctrl + X Cut Ctrl + V Paste Ctrl + A Select all Delete Delete (to recycle bin) Shift + Delete Delete permanently (skips the recycle bin; it cannot be undone, so you are always asked first) Ctrl + Shift + C Copy the full path of the selected files (the current folder's path when nothing is selected) Ctrl + D Add to favorites Alt + Enter Show the properties dialog for the selected file Application key Open the right-click menu for the selected files Ctrl + Shift + X Open the current folder in Windows Explorer

docs.title: Keys you cannot change
docs.text:
These keys are not in the assignment table and work the same under every scheme.

Key Action Shift + F10 Open the right-click menu for the selected files (same as the Application key) Ctrl + wheel Resize icons steplessly over the file list (also moves between list view and icon view) Left Arrow / Right Arrow (during preview) Switch to previous/next file during Quick Preview (directories are skipped, stops at list edges) F4 / Alt + Down Arrow (address bar) Show the history of folders you have opened Esc (in search bar) Multi-stage reset: 1st press clears keyword, 2nd press also clears size/date/scope filters and exits search A-Z / 0-9 / symbols / text typed with an IME Incremental search: Moves selection to a file/folder starting with what you type. Pressing the same key repeatedly cycles through items with the same initial letter. Typing different keys within about a second performs a prefix jump. Symbols such as _ and ~, and text confirmed with an IME, work too (excludes Ctrl/Alt combinations and spaces) Ctrl + Alt + F4 Full exit in resident mode Esc Close breadcrumb dropdown menus / Close sub-windows like changelog and manual

docs.title: Two keys for one action
docs.text:
An action can have a second key as well. The key list shows both, such as "Ctrl+L / Alt+D", and either one runs the action. In the standard set, these actions come with File Explorer's second key:

Action First key Second key Go up one level Backspace Alt + Up Arrow Address bar Ctrl + L Alt + D Search bar Ctrl + F Ctrl + E Refresh F5 Ctrl + R Quick Preview Space Alt + P

Some key schemes assign their own key to these actions, so the second key doesn't apply there. The second key can't yet be changed on screen (the row's "Reset to default" restores the default second key). Changing the first key leaves the second one in place.

Actions without a key: "Invert selection", "Select none", "Switch to tab 1–8", "Switch to last tab", "Close other tabs", "Copy to other pane", "Move to other pane", "Open in text editor", "Switch column width mode", the view switches ("Large icons", "List" and so on), "Toggle hidden files", "Toggle file name extensions" and others have no key in Zenith standard (some schemes give them one). Assign a key in the key settings, or use them from the Command Palette.

docs.title: Zenith 2 two-key shortcuts
docs.text:
Press Ctrl+K or Ctrl+B, then one more key — you can keep Ctrl held down, or let go; either works. Hold the prefix for a moment and the keys you can press next appear at the bottom of the window. Type straight through and the list never shows. The list is clickable. Esc, or two seconds of waiting, cancels.

Ctrl + K — open a view (focus moves there; press the same keys again to return to the file list)

Key View Key View F Favorites M Macros T Tree N Sites H History C Terminal Shift + H Search History Shift + C Terminal 2 I Index Search L Tab Management S Search Presets Shift + L AI Tab Management W Working Set O AI Folder Analysis R Recent Files / AI Manual Shift + R Recent Folders P Properties D Drives V Preview

Ctrl + B — panes and layout

Key Action Key Action 1 / 2 / 3 Single / side-by-side / top-bottom split L Window layout presets Z Toggle single ⇔ dual pane N Nav pane layout [ / ] Show or hide the left / right nav pane W Working set quick access C Copy the selection to the other pane M Move the selection to the other pane

Under Zenith 2 the sidebar keys Ctrl+Shift+1–8 and the pane keys Ctrl+Shift+Q/W/`/[/]/L/J/S and Ctrl+3 are replaced by the two above. Tab is released from pane switching and goes back to stepping through the elements on screen (moving between panes is what ← → are for).

docs.title: Keys inside the nav pane (the same everywhere)
docs.text:
Every nav pane view answers the same keys with the same meaning. Where a view has no such operation, the key does nothing at all — it never quietly means something else.

Key Meaning ↑ ↓ Pick a row Enter Use that row (open a folder, apply a set, run a macro, connect to a site) Esc Back to the file list (the view stays open) The same keys that opened the view Also returns to the file list F2 Rename (where the view has one) Delete Delete or unregister (where the view has one) Insert Add or save (where the view has one) Ctrl + F Filter within the view (where the view has a filter box)

Views without a list at all — preview, properties, macros, the AI panels — still answer Esc. The terminal is the one exception: inside it the app takes no keys whatsoever, and F6 is the only way out.

docs.title: Being told about shortcut keys
docs.text: Press a toolbar or status bar button with the mouse and, if that operation has a key bound to it, a notification says so: "'Dual pane' also runs with Ctrl+Shift+W". Three times per operation, then it goes quiet. Nothing appears when you use the keyboard. Turn it off with "Point out shortcut keys" at the top of Settings > Shortcuts.

docs.title: Settings Backup & Recovery
docs.text: From Control Deck (default: Ctrl+Shift+O) > "Recovery" category, you can manage settings backup and restoration.

docs.title: Creating Backups
docs.text:
Timing Behavior After a settings change (automatic) About 5 minutes after a change is detected, backups/settings_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss.json is generated. This works even if you run in resident mode and keep the app minimized to the tray instead of exiting On full exit / minimizing to tray (automatic) An additional backup is generated immediately at that moment, without waiting for the 5-minute delay above "Backup Now" button Immediately backs up the current settings.json, even if nothing has changed. Its summary is the difference from the previous backup, as with automatic backups At app start-up (automatic) If a backup could not be made last time (for example after a forced exit), it is made now. Nothing is created if the settings are unchanged Just before restoring a backup (automatic) Your current settings are saved as an "Auto-save before restore" snapshot first, so you can always undo an accidental restore

Automatic backups are skipped when the settings have not changed since the previous backup.

docs.title: Change Summary (Diff Summary)
docs.text:
Each backup has a summary of the differences from the previous backup, saved in a .desc file (e.g., "Updated Pane A home, search behavior"). The summary is written in the app's display language. The first backup is recorded as "Initial backup."

If generative AI is set up and "Backup AI Summary" is on under Control Deck › AI, the summary is replaced with one written by the AI: for the latest backup at start-up, and for the new backup when you press "Backup Now" (off at first on new installations). The changed settings are sent to the AI service for this (see Privacy Policy).

docs.title: Backup List (Inline Display)
docs.text:
Opening the "Recovery" category displays the backup list within the settings screen.

  • Columns: Date/Time / Lock status (lock icon) / Change summary / Edit button / Restore button
  • Edit summary: Click the pencil button to edit the change summary inline. Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel. Locked backups cannot be edited
  • Restore: Click the rotate-arrow button to display a confirmation dialog and restore to the selected point in time. After restoration, a restart prompt dialog appears; selecting "Yes" triggers automatic restart
  • Lock / Unlock: Click the lock icon to toggle lock status. Locked backups are excluded from the 30-day auto-deletion policy. Lock important settings for protection

docs.title: Automatic Cleanup
docs.text: On app startup, backups older than 30 days are automatically deleted. However, backups with a .lock file (locked) are not deleted.

docs.title: Feedback Reporting from Error Dialogs
docs.text: When an unexpected error occurs, "Report problem" on the error dialog opens the Feedback page right away. The error message and stack trace are filled into the title and message, and the category is set to "Bug report" (with system information and the log attached by default). Your Windows user name in paths is replaced with <user>. You can read, add to or remove any of it before sending.

docs.title: Reference Number
docs.text:
Besides the send button, you can send feedback by pressing Shift+Enter (or Ctrl+Enter) in the title or description box. Enter starts a new line.

When feedback is sent successfully, the message includes a reference number (e.g. Reference no. #220). The number, title, the text you sent, category and send time are kept in data\feedback_history.json and survive a restart (up to the 50 most recent; older entries are dropped first).

The app adds nothing that identifies the sender. If you attach the recent error log, your Windows user name in the paths is replaced with <user> before the preview is shown (other folder and file names stay as they are, so check the preview). The link between you and a reference number exists only in this local record.

docs.title: Your Submissions and Replies from the Developer
docs.text:
Your submissions are listed in a table at the bottom of the Feedback page. Each row shows status, reference number, type, subject, date sent and reply count, so you can see where each report stands at a glance.

Status Meaning Not checked Status has not been fetched yet (offline, etc.) In progress Received and being worked on Done The work is complete Not planned A decision was made not to act on it (by design or policy)
  • Click a row to expand it and see the text you sent at the top, followed by replies from the developer and your own replies in chronological order. The developer's replies are aligned left, yours to the right. Only the description you wrote is shown — any system information or logs you attached are not
  • Older entries kept before this existed have no stored text; it is filled in from the receiving end the next time you check for replies
  • You can drag across the text of any message to select it and copy it with Ctrl+C — handy for quoting part of a reply back (right-clicking to copy the whole thing works too)
  • You can reply on the spot. Replies can only be sent on reports you submitted yourself (a 60-second interval is required between replies). Press Shift+Enter (or Ctrl+Enter) in the reply box to send. Enter starts a new line, so you can write replies over several lines
  • When the developer replies that a report has been fixed, "It's fixed" and "Still happening" buttons appear in the expanded row once your app is on a version that includes the fix. One click lets the developer know how it went. "Still happening" also sends whatever you've typed in the reply box and puts the report back in progress. You're only asked once per fix
  • When there is an unread reply, a count badge appears on "Feedback" in the left menu and an accent bar appears at the left edge of the row. Opening the row marks it as read. Rows waiting for you to confirm a fix also get the accent bar (they don't add to the count badge)
  • Use "Check for replies" to refresh manually. Fetching happens only when you open the Feedback page in settings — never at app startup
  • If you are offline or the fetch fails, what is stored locally is still shown

Only replies to reports you submitted yourself are shown. There is no way to read someone else's report by entering its number.

docs.title: Log Specification
docs.text: The app's activity record (the log) is saved in data\logs\. Click the document button at the right end of the status bar to open this folder; press and hold it to open today's log (see Status Bar). When reporting a problem, "Attach recent error log" in Feedback lets you check exactly what will be sent first (see Privacy Policy).

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
File Contents Kept for log-yyyyMMdd.log The everyday activity record, one file per day The newest 31 files yyyy-MM-dd.log Records that must be written out at once, such as just before an unexpected error stops the app Not deleted automatically terminal\ Terminal screen records (.log) and Claude Code conversation records (.md), one file per session (see Terminal) 30 days

Logs stay on your PC and are never sent automatically.

docs.title: What a line looks like
docs.text:
[2026/10/25 09:41:03][INF] [STARTUP] Zenith Filer v… | Windows … | .NET … | x64 | PID=…
  • The line starts with the date and time, followed by a three-letter level: DBG (detail), INF (information), WRN (warning), ERR (error), FTL (fatal error).
  • Errors are followed by the exception type, its message and where it happened (the stack trace).
  • The […] at the start of the message tells you which part of the app wrote it. The main ones:
Tag What it records [STARTUP] Version, Windows, .NET and architecture at start-up [Update] Checking for, downloading and applying updates (see Auto-Update) [IndexService] / [IndexSync] / [IndexWatch] Building and updating the index, picking up changes [SettingsBackupService] Creating settings backups [Feedback] Sending feedback [CLOSING] Window state when it closes (position, size, resident mode)

Logs can contain folder and file paths. Check the contents before passing them to anyone.

docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text:
This page explains what Zenith Filer sends over the internet, when, and how to turn it off. Zenith Filer is made by one developer (sulkyjp).

In short:

  • Zenith Filer has no built-in analytics or telemetry, and no crash reporting. Your files, folder names and usage history stay on your PC unless you do something that sends them.
  • A few features talk to servers: the update check, the XP leaderboard, the Theme Store and Stickman Store, and feedback. Each one is described below, with how to turn it off. The time of your last leaderboard upload is also used to count how many people keep using the app (see XP leaderboard).
  • AI features send data only to the AI service you set up, and only after you have entered an API key or chosen Ollama or Claude Code. Only Ollama running on this PC keeps everything on your computer.
  • Your Pro license is checked on your PC. The license key is never sent anywhere.

docs.title: What stays on your PC
docs.text:
Settings, favorites, history, usage statistics, the search index, logs and your license file are all stored in the folder next to ZenithFiler.exe. None of them leave your PC except:

  • when you attach part of the log to feedback yourself (see Feedback)
  • when you use an AI feature. For example, "AI Usage Analysis" on the Statistics page sends your usage statistics, search history, the paths of folders you open often and more to the AI service (see AI features)

docs.title: What the app sends, and when
Update check
docs.text:
• What is sent: a request for the latest version number. The request carries the app's version (as the User-Agent) and, if you receive preview builds, that you want the preview channel. Nothing else.
  • Where: the developer's update server (on Cloudflare). If it does not answer, GitHub's release API is used instead. Update files are downloaded from GitHub releases.
  • When: 30 seconds after start, then every 4 hours, and whenever you press "Check for updates" on the About page.
  • Turn off: Control Deck › About › Auto Update.

docs.title: XP leaderboard
docs.text:
The app can post your experience points to an online leaderboard that other users can see.

  • What is sent: a random ID created for this installation (see Identifiers), a display name, your title (a nickname based on your achievements), XP, level, and a flag saying whether the upload comes from the developer's own PC (used to keep the developer off the rankings; it is always "no" for everyone else).
  • Off until you turn it on: a new installation does not upload anything to the leaderboard. (Installations from before this change upload anonymously unless they were turned off.)
  • Display name: with "Upload anonymously" the display name is a fixed "Anonymous Adventurer" (in the app's language). With "Upload", the name you entered for the leaderboard is used, or your store user name if that is empty. Your store user name starts out as the name you registered your license with; you can change it on the License or Theme page of Control Deck.
  • When: when you switch uploading on, when the app starts (at most once every 20 hours), and when you level up. On a level-up the app also sends the installation ID to look up your rank.
  • Stored: yes, on the developer's server: the ID, display name, title, XP, level and the time of the last upload. The time of the last upload is used to count how many people keep using the app. IP addresses are not stored.
  • Turn on or off: Control Deck › Challenges. Delete your entry: "Remove from ranking" on the same page.

docs.title: Theme Store and Stickman Store
docs.text:
• Browsing: the lists and files of themes and behaviors are downloaded from GitHub and the developer's server. When you open the theme settings or a store page, the installation ID is sent so the app can show the ratings you gave and the items you uploaded.
  • Installing: when you install a theme or behavior, its name is sent to the developer's server to count downloads (without the installation ID).
  • Rating, uploading and deleting: only when you do it. A rating sends the installation ID, the item name and the score.
  • A theme upload sends the installation ID and the theme file as it is, including the author name and description written in it.
  • A Stickman behavior upload sends the installation ID, the behavior's name, category, description and file. Before sending, the app replaces the author name in the file with your store user name (with Pro; the free version uses "Free User").
  • Stored: uploads and ratings are kept on the developer's server and shown to other users. You can delete your own uploads from the store.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text:
Feedback you send from Control Deck › Feedback is posted as an issue in the developer's private GitHub repository. Only the developer can read it.

  • Always sent: your category, title and message, plus the app version (added at the end of the message).
  • When opened from "Report problem" on an error dialog: the error message and stack trace are filled into the title and message in advance. You can read and edit them before sending. Your Windows user name in paths is replaced with <user>.
  • Only if you tick the box (you see a preview before sending). Both are on at first only when the category is "Bug report", because they are needed to look into a problem. For "Feature request" and "Other" they are off at first; tick them only if you want to send them. Changing the category puts them back to that category's starting state:
  • "Attach system information": app version, Windows version, .NET version, the app's architecture (such as x64), the app's memory use, screen size, DPI scaling and the current theme name.
  • "Attach recent error log": up to five recent warnings or errors from the app's log, each with the three informational entries just before it. These can contain folder paths. Your Windows user name in those paths is replaced with <user> before you see the preview, but other folder and file names stay as they are. Check the preview and untick the box if you do not want to share them.
  • Replies: when you open the Feedback page, the app reads the developer's replies to the feedback you sent from this PC. Replies you write, and "It's fixed" / "Still happening" answers, are posted the same way, with the app version.

docs.title: AI features
docs.text:
AI features are optional. Data is sent only to the service you choose in Control Deck › AI, and only after you have set one up (an API key for Claude, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI or Gemini, or choosing Ollama or Claude Code).

  • Where it goes: Claude, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and Gemini send to their own services. Claude Code (CLI) sends through the Claude Code on your PC to Anthropic's service; it does not run on your PC. Ollama sends to the Ollama server you set.
  • What is sent: the text needed for the task. Depending on the feature this includes folder paths, file and folder names, sizes and dates, the names, paths and descriptions of your favorites, tab paths, search keywords, or text you type. File contents are not sent by the built-in features; a macro you write can send whatever text it passes to the AI.
  • "AI Usage Analysis" on the Statistics page: only when you press "Analyze", it sends how often each feature was used, the paths and counts of folders you open often, your favorites' paths, the paths, counts and times of folders opened in tabs, pairs of folders you often open together, your search history, working set names and your AI usage.
  • Features that run on their own once AI is set up (each can be switched off under "Auto AI Features" on Control Deck › AI):
  • AI Rename Suggestion, when the rename dialog opens (folder path and nearby names)
  • Backup AI Summary, at start-up and when you press "Backup Now" on the Recovery page (the changed settings, which can include folder paths such as your favorites). Off at first on new installations
  • Challenge Title Generation and Backstory Generation, when your achievements change (achievement names only)
  • Off by default: AI Greeting and Descriptions when adding favorites.
  • Talk to Stickman: only when you talk to it, it sends what you typed, the last three exchanges, the time of day, the kind of thing you just did (a broad group such as working, tidying or sharing), how many operations you did in a row, the display language, Stickman's personality, and the names and descriptions of the moves Stickman can act out. No file or folder names or paths are sent. The first line Stickman says when you hover over it sends nothing.
  • Fully local: with Ollama on this PC, nothing leaves your computer.
  • The AI service handles the data under its own privacy policy. Note that Gemini's API receives the key as part of the request address; this is how Google's API works.

docs.title: Connections you set up
docs.text: FTP / FTPS / SFTP servers, Box, and an Ollama server on another computer are contacted only because you added them. The app sends what is needed to sign in and to list, read or write the files you work with.

docs.title: Downloads you start
docs.text: Installing Ollama or FFmpeg from the settings downloads them from their official sources (ollama.com and GitHub).

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text:
• When the app first starts, it creates a random installation ID. It is not derived from your name, your PC or your hardware. It is used only by the leaderboard and the stores, so that your entries, ratings and uploads stay linked to you.
  • The license file records a Windows machine ID so that the license works on this PC. It stays on your PC and is never sent.
  • The app never sends your Windows user name or computer name. It reads your user name only to hide it (replacing it with <user>) in logs and error text.

docs.title: How secrets are stored
docs.text: API keys, Box sign-in tokens and FTP/SFTP passwords are encrypted with Windows' data protection (DPAPI) for your Windows account before they are saved. They are sent only to the service they belong to.

docs.title: Purchases
docs.text: Pro is sold through Polar (outside Japan) and Vector (in Japan). Payment and your e-mail address are handled by them under their own privacy policies. The app itself does not contact either of them (the buy button in Control Deck › License just opens the store page in your browser); the license key you enter is checked on your PC. The name you register with becomes your initial store user name (see XP leaderboard).

docs.title: Services involved
docs.text: Service Used for GitHub Releases and update files, update fallback, theme and Stickman files, feedback Cloudflare The developer's server for updates, leaderboard and stores The AI service you choose (Anthropic for Claude Code) AI features Polar / Vector Purchases

docs.title: Deleting your data
docs.text:
• Leaderboard entry: Control Deck › Challenges › "Remove from ranking".
  • Themes and Stickman behaviors you uploaded: delete them from the store.
  • Ratings and feedback: ask through GitHub Issues or Control Deck › Feedback.
  • Everything on your PC: delete the Zenith Filer folder.

docs.title: Changes and contact
docs.text: When what the app sends changes, this page is updated together with the app. Questions: GitHub Issues or Control Deck › Feedback.

docs.title: Configuration File Structure
docs.text: Settings and theme files live in the data folder next to ZenithFiler.exe (for the whole folder layout, see Installation and Folder Structure). Changing things from Control Deck is the normal way. If you edit a file by hand, exit the app first — edits made while it is running are overwritten when it exits.

docs.title: settings.json
docs.text:
data\settings.json holds almost every setting in a single JSON file. The main properties (names exactly as they appear in the JSON):

Area Main properties Window placement Left, Top, Width, Height, State, PaneCount, PaneWidthRatio, PaneSplitDirection General SingleClickOpenFolder, ConfirmDelete, RestoreTabsOnStartup, NotificationDurationMs, ResidentMode Display ShowPathInTitleBar, ShowFileExtensions, ShowHiddenFiles, HideProtectedOsFiles, ListRowHeight New tab defaults DefaultGroupFoldersFirst, DefaultSortProperty, DefaultSortDirection A / B panes LeftPane, RightPane (per-pane sorting and so on) Index Inside Index: UpdateMode, UpdateIntervalHours, EcoMode, NetworkLowPriority, FullRebuildCooldownHours, IdleOnlyExecution, IdleCpuThreshold, FreshnessAggressive, FreshnessWarnStale. Per-folder settings are in IndexSchedules Effects EffectsAllOff, EffectsAutoLightweight, ShowStartupEffects, ShowGlowBar, ShowScanBar, ShowTabEffects, ShowPaneTransitions, ShowThemeEffects, ShowPreviewEffects, ShowListEffects, ShowDragEffects, ShowTactileEffects Stickman ShowMascotEffect (Show Stickman on status bar), StickmanChatEnabled Theme and language ThemeName, PreferredLanguage Favorites Favorites Shortcuts KeyMapPresetId, CustomKeyBindings (the bindings you changed yourself) Updates AutoUpdate, ReceivePreviewUpdates, LastUpdateCheck, SkippedVersion AI AiProvider, AiModelName, AiAzureOpenAiEndpoint. API keys are stored in AiClaudeApiKeyEncrypted and similar properties, encrypted with Windows' data protection (DPAPI); only the same PC and Windows account can read them

settings.json.bak in the same folder holds the previously saved contents and is used if settings.json cannot be read. Dated copies are kept in data\backups\ (see Settings Backup & Recovery).

docs.title: Theme JSON (data\themes\*.json)
docs.text:
• Category: one of Standard / WarmCozy (shown as Lifestyle) / Professional / Premium / RetroTech. When omitted, the app assigns a built-in default.
  • Description.ja, Description.en and so on, and Author: the per-language description and author name shown on the theme card.
  • Colour keys: colours grouped into sections such as Base, List and Search (for the list of keys, see Themes (Color Customization)). Customised differences are saved to data\themes\_custom\{theme name}.json.
  • Colour keys the app does not recognise are ignored when the theme is loaded.

docs.title: Language JSON (data\lang\*.json)
docs.text:
• 10 languages (ja, en, de, es, fr, ko-KR, pt, ru, zh-CN, zh-TW)
  • To add a language of your own, place a .json file with the same keys in this folder; it is detected automatically

docs.title: Stickman Behaviour JSON (data\stickman\*.json, data\stickman\rewards\*.json)
docs.text:
• For the syntax, see JSON Behavior Definition Reference
  • The unlock field ties a behaviour to an achievement (see Reward Behavior Patterns)
  • Write the description as description (shown for every language) and per-language keys such as description.ja and description.en

docs.title: Keymap presets (data\keymaps\*.json)
docs.text: These define the presets listed on the Shortcuts page. For the format, see Full List of App Settings (Control Deck).

docs.title: Full List of App Settings (Control Deck)
docs.text: The settings view, opened with Ctrl+Shift+O, is split into pages under the headings of the navigation on the left. This article covers every page in the order of that navigation. Where a page has its own detailed article, a link points there.

docs.title: Finding a setting
docs.text:
The navigation on the left groups the pages under six headings. The page you are on is marked with a vertical bar at its left edge.

Heading Pages Basics General, Language Appearance Display, Theme, File type colors, Effects Controls Tab, Shortcuts, Toolbar, Ring Launcher Features Search, Index, AI, Recovery, Stickman Collection Theme Store, Stickman Store, Challenges, Rewards, Statistics App License, Feedback, About

On each page, settings are listed one per row under headings. The settings under a heading are gathered in a single card with rounded corners, and the rows inside the card are separated by thin lines. The left side of a row shows the name and a description, and the right side has the control that changes it. Turn options on or off with the switch at the right end, and pick values from lists. A row with ⌄ at the right end opens to show its choices (picked with round radio buttons) or more detailed settings (the current value is shown on the right of the row).

If you don't know which page a setting is on, look it up by name in the search box at the top right.

  • Ctrl+F (or Ctrl+E) moves to the search box
  • As you type, matching settings appear in two lines: the name, and "page › heading". Full-width and half-width characters, katakana and hiragana, and upper and lower case are treated the same. When you type several words separated by spaces, only settings that contain all of them remain (for example, "display row")
  • English names work in any language (for example, "font" or "theme")
