  • Choose a result with ↑ ↓ and press Enter (or click it) to jump to that setting on its page. The setting is outlined for about 1.4 seconds while a light makes one lap around it from the top-right corner, where the search box is (the outline appears for the same time even when effects are turned off)
  • Shortcut names appear too. Choosing one opens the Shortcuts page filtered by that name
  • The first Esc closes the results and the second clears the text. When the search box is empty, Esc closes the settings window as before

Results include page names and the headings and item names of settings on each page. For now, you can jump to individual settings on the General, Language, Display, File type colors, Effects, Tab, Search, Index and Recovery pages. Other pages open by their page name.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Author's setup

Applies the setup the author uses every day in one go: the nav pane layout (the "Author's Layout" preset), the toolbar button layout ("Standard"), the level and title banners in the title bar, AI / Pro badges, feature recommendations, the theme notification on startup and the default Ring Launcher layout. The defaults for new users are kept quiet and close to an ordinary file manager, so this is the way in when you want to try the app the way it was meant to be used. It asks first, and if you have changed the Ring Launcher assignment without saving it anywhere, it tells you that assignment will be lost. XP ranking submission is not changed. Everything can be adjusted again individually afterwards.

Mouse

  • Open folders with single click: On for single click, off for double-click navigation (off by default).
  • Open folders in a new tab with middle-click: Opens folders in the file list in a background tab (on by default). See Tabs.
  • Rename with a slow second click: Click an already-selected item again after a pause to open Rename (off by default).
  • Go up one folder by double-clicking empty space: Double-clicking blank space in the list goes to the parent folder (on by default).

File operations

  • Context Menu: Selects which menu is shown when right-clicking in the file list.
  • App custom menu (Recommended): Instantly shows basic operations like Open, Copy, Delete, Rename, Favorites, Index Search. Use Shift+right-click for a temporary switch to the Explorer-compatible menu.
  • Explorer-compatible menu: Shows the Windows standard right-click menu (including shell extensions such as 7-Zip). The menu shown when you drop with a right drag also lists app items (see Drag & Drop).
  • Show confirmation dialog when deleting files: Off bypasses the shell confirmation and moves to Recycle Bin (on by default).
  • Use Windows to extract 7z, rar and other archives: Extracts archives other than ZIP and TAR (7z, rar, tar.xz and so on) with the same Windows archive support that File Explorer uses (on by default). On Windows versions without that support (such as Windows 10), the tar.exe that ships with Windows is used instead, and 7z, tar.xz and tar.bz2 archives that tar.exe cannot read are extracted with a component built into the app. Turning it off stops all of these and limits extraction to the built-in ZIP and TAR. See Archives (Extract and Compress).
  • Open archives as folders on double-click: Opens zip, 7z, rar and other archives inside the pane, read-only, with the same Windows archive folder as File Explorer (on by default). Turn it off to open them with the default app. Holding Shift also opens them with the default app.
  • ZIP compression level: The default strength for ZIPs made by Compress (No compression, Fastest, Standard, Smallest size or Auto; Standard by default). Auto stores files that are already compressed, such as photos, videos and archives, without shrinking them. To change it just once, right-click and choose Archive ▶ Compress with level. Does not apply to TAR.GZ. See Archives (Extract and Compress).
  • Copy progress window: see "Copy progress window" below.

Copy progress window

Starting a copy or a move opens a progress window. Operations are listed as rows in a single window, each showing speed, time remaining, file count, size and the file being processed. Every row can be paused, resumed or stopped, and the footer has Stop all and Clear finished. Closing the window does not stop the transfer — the bar at the bottom left of the main window takes over. Progress also appears on the taskbar icon, so you can follow it from another application. When everything succeeds, the window closes after 1 second. Tick Close when done in the footer (off by default) to have it close straight away; the choice is remembered for next time. Either way, the window stays open when something was stopped or failed, so you can read what happened, and the results also appear as a notification. Starting a new copy or move clears the finished rows from earlier operations.

You can choose when it appears: Always show (default), Only for large transfers (50 files / 50 MB), or Never (bar at the bottom left only).

Startup and exit

  • Restore previous tabs on startup: Off starts with only the home folder (on by default).
  • Auto-restore folder display settings: Remembers sort order and view mode per folder and applies them when you come back (on by default).
  • Start when I sign in to Windows: see below.
  • Startup Presets: Choose the Window Layout and Nav Pane presets and the Working Set to apply automatically at startup (see Presets and Working Sets).
  • A Pane Home / B Pane Home: Set the home folder for each pane. "Set to current folder" uses the folder now open; "Select folder" picks one in a dialog.

Start when I sign in to Windows

Launches Zenith Filer when you sign in to Windows. Off by default.

It works by placing a shortcut in your Startup folder and writes nothing to the registry. You can turn it off with this switch, or from Settings > Apps > Startup in Windows.

Turning it on also enables Resident Mode, because without it closing the window ends the process and the global hotkey (When the app hotkey does not work) stops working. Zenith starts minimized, so it will not come to the front every time you sign in.

Window

  • Resident mode (minimize to tray): Pressing the X button minimizes to the system tray instead of exiting (off by default). See Resident Mode for the operation table.
  • Snap window to screen edges: When enabled, dragging the window to within 15 px of a screen edge (the work area, excluding the taskbar) makes it snap into place like a magnet. All four sides and corners are supported, and snapping is evaluated against the monitor the window is on, so it behaves naturally in multi-monitor and high-DPI setups. Keep dragging to pull the window back off. Resizing does not snap, and it coexists with the standard Windows Aero Snap (Win + arrow, etc.). On by default.

Navigation pane

  • Auto-hide left nav pane: When on, the left nav pane is normally kept closed; bringing the cursor into the thin 12px strip along the window's left edge slides it in as an overlay after about 0.15 s. The band out to 32px opens it too, if you stay there for a second — a safety net for when you miss the very edge, so merely passing through does not open it. It slides out about 0.4 s after the cursor leaves. Useful when you want to give the A and B panes the maximum amount of room.
  • Auto-hide right nav pane: The same toggle for the right pane. The left and right sides can be enabled independently.
  • Pin: While the pane is auto-revealed, a pin button appears in the top-right of its header. Clicking it keeps the pane open even after the cursor leaves; clicking again releases the pin and the pane resumes auto-hiding. Pin state is reset when the app restarts.
  • Opening with the toggle key or the Ring Launcher: Even on an auto-hidden side, "Toggle Left Pane" / "Toggle Right Pane" (for example ◀ ▶ on the Ring Launcher) shows the pane temporarily. Repeat the same action or click outside the nav pane to close it. Closing it with the toggle also releases a pin. The auto-hide setting itself stays as it is.
  • Drag-and-drop / context-menu protection: While dragging an item over the nav pane, or while a context menu launched from it is open, the auto-hide timer is suppressed so the pane does not disappear mid-interaction.
  • Auto-hide is off by default on both sides.
  • Show Quick access in the tree (on by default) / Show Libraries in the tree (off by default) / Show Network in the tree (on by default): Choose which places the folder tree lists. See Nav Pane.
  • Recent Folder Exclusions: The folders you have kept out of "Recent folders". You can remove an exclusion here.

External apps

Specify the executable used by "Open in text editor". Bypasses the OS .txt association and launches your editor of choice (VS Code / Notepad++ / Sakura / Notepad, etc.) directly.

  • Executable path: Type the editor's .exe path or pick it via the [Browse…] button. Leave blank to fall back to the OS default app.
  • [Auto-detect]: Searches in this order — VS Code on PATH → VS Code's default install location → Notepad++ → Sakura → Windows Notepad — and fills in the first match.
  • If the configured path no longer exists, the app safely falls back to the OS default editor.
  • Additional extensions: Add extensions that show "Open in text editor", separated by commas (e.g. csv, dat). A leading . or *. is optional. The extensions included by default (.txt, .md, .json and so on) stay as they are, and their list is shown below the field. Added extensions also become targets of "Compare Text", which puts two files side by side.

Help and notices

  • Show what's new on startup: On the first launch after an update, a card summarises what changed in that version (on by default).
  • Show "First 5 steps": Shows the getting-started guide again.
  • Show theme notification on startup: When a theme is picked automatically, tells you at startup which one was applied (off by default for new users).
  • Display Duration: How long notifications stay: Short (1.5s) / Standard (3s) / Long (5s).

Data and sync

  • Achievement sharing across devices: Point it at an achievements.json on a USB stick or a cloud-synced folder (OneDrive and so on) to share achievements (level, XP, completed challenges and titles) between two PCs (off by default). Settings, favorites and the rest stay per PC. "Sync now" brings them in line at once.

docs.title: Language
docs.text: Choose the Display Language. Ten languages are available; translations other than Japanese are AI-generated. A language file added to the data\lang folder appears in this list (see Configuration File Structure).

docs.title: Display
docs.text:
Text and size

  • App Font: Choose the font for the whole app.
  • File List Row Height: Ultra Compact (20 px) / Compact (24 px) / Standard (32 px) / Relaxed (40 px). Reflected immediately in both A/B panes and persists across restarts.
  • List text / List icons / Tab text: Each can be sized independently. All three default to Auto (follow row height). Pick a size yourself and it stays put even when you change the row height. The tab text setting applies both to the A/B pane tabs and to the tab list in the navigation pane. Sizes are kept within readable bounds: 8–32 for text and 8–48 for icons.

Window

  • Show folder path in title bar: Shows the focused pane's full path in the title bar (on by default).

File list

  • Show file extensions: Off hides file extensions (on by default).
  • Show hidden files and folders: Toggles visibility of Windows hidden-attribute files (off by default).
  • Hide protected operating system files: Hides files and folders that carry both the hidden and system attributes ($RECYCLE.BIN, pagefile.sys and so on); on by default and the same as File Explorer's option of the same name. Items with only the system attribute, or the temporary attribute, are shown regardless. This applies to the file list, the breadcrumb folder lists, search, the nav pane tree and CSV / Excel export; index search is not affected.
  • Alternate row colors: When on, every other row in the file list is tinted a very subtle color, making rows easier to track in wide listings (off by default). The color is computed automatically against the current theme's background, so it looks natural on any theme.
  • Show an outline on the selected row: Marks the selected row with an accent-coloured outline in addition to the background fill (on by default), so the row under the pointer stays distinguishable from the row you picked with the keyboard.
  • Use check boxes to select items: Shows check boxes on items in the file list, so clicking one adds or removes just that item (off by default). See Standard File Operations for how it behaves.
  • Show size bar: Shows a bar in the Size column comparing file sizes (on by default). Turn on Animate size bars on every folder change (off by default) to have the bars grow in each time you change folders.
  • Count folder sizes automatically: When you open a folder, the sizes of the folders inside are counted in the background and shown in the Size column (on by default), the same way Explorer's Properties counts them. You can choose the Recount interval (Every time (default) / 10 minutes / 1 hour / 1 day), and whether to Also count on network drives and Also count in cloud folders (Box Drive, OneDrive, SharePoint) (both off by default). See View Options.
  • Show folder contents as thumbnails: In Large and Extra large icons, local folders holding pictures show a peek at their contents (on by default, as in File Explorer). Not shown in OneDrive, Box, network or slow locations.
  • Show app overlay marks on icons: Shows the overlay marks that apps such as Git and Dropbox put on icons, on the visible items of the file list (off by default): on the small icon in Details and List, and at the lower left of the large icon in icon views, Tiles and Content. It asks Windows about each item, so the marks appear shortly after a folder opens. Local locations only.

Sort order

  • New Tab Default View: Show folders first (on by default) and Default sort order (Name / Date modified / Size / Extension × Ascending / Descending). Applied to new tabs opened via Ctrl+T or path input; not applied to search result tabs or existing tabs.
  • Sort Downloads folder by date modified: On applies newest-first sort when navigating to Downloads, reverting to the original sort elsewhere (on by default).
  • Adjust the view to each folder's contents: When you open a folder for the first time, picks Pictures, Music, Videos or Documents from its file extensions and applies that view (off by default). See View Options.

Markers

  • Spotting what's new: Bolds the modified date of recently changed files. Range: Off / Today / 24 hours (default) / 3 days / 7 days.
  • Mark items that were just updated (on by default): Shows ✨ to the right of the file name for How long the ✨ mark stays after an update (1 minute to 7 days; 10 minutes by default).
  • Show when the folder is on a network: Marks the tab and address bar while you have a network folder open (on by default).

Banners and badges

  • Show AI / Pro badges, Show challenge title banner in header and Show level banner in header bar: all off by default for new users. "Author's setup" on the General page turns them on in one go.

Thumbnails

  • Show hover thumbnail: In Details view, hovering over an image file shows a thumbnail next to the cursor (on by default).
  • Video thumbnails (optional download): Thumbnails for formats Windows supports — mp4, mov, mkv and so on — work with nothing to install. Install the extension (FFmpeg) here only if you also want thumbnails for formats Windows cannot produce one for, such as flv. It downloads about 130 MB into data\ffmpeg\. Once installed, it is used only for formats Windows could not handle. It is not bundled with the app so that people who do not need it are not made to carry the size. The download is an LGPL build, used unmodified and invoked as a separate program, so it does not affect this app's licence. Use "Remove" to delete it when it is no longer needed (an FFmpeg you put on your PATH yourself is left alone).

docs.title: Theme
docs.text: Pick a theme from the list, or have one chosen automatically (random, by category, or switching between day and night). The page also covers per-pane themes, colour customization, creating themes with AI and uploading to the Theme Store; the user name used in the stores can be changed here as well. See Themes (Color Customization).

docs.title: File Type Colors
docs.text:
Colors file names in the file list by file type, based on extension (off by default). This dedicated settings page lets you configure:

  • Color file names by type: Turning it on colors file names in the list according to the rules below.
  • Recommended rules (7 categories): A ready-made set of extension/color pairings is included for images, videos, audio, archives, executables, documents, and code.
  • Free editing: Every rule's target extensions, color (#RRGGBB), and enabled state (the switch at the right end of each rule) can be edited. Use "Add rule" to create a new rule; rules you add can also be removed (the 7 built-in rules can only be disabled, not deleted).
  • Reset to defaults: A single button restores the recommended rule set.
  • Just like alternate row colors, the actual displayed color is automatically adjusted against the current theme's background, so it never becomes hard to read on any theme.

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
Groups in-app effects into categories you can turn on or off individually with the switch at the right end. The page is divided under the headings See the effects, Overall, Speed and load, and Effect types, and each effect type row lists the effects in that category below its description. See Effects Categories for the full table with target UI.

  • See the effects: Press "Play" to see five effects in turn: switching tabs, results landing, confirming, a notice, and a name.
  • Turn off all effects (instant display): Switches the display instantly without animation. Feedback on actions is one of the categories. See Effects Categories for details.

Automatically reduce effects on slow systems (on by default): Automatically detects remote desktop sessions, software rendering, and environments where screen transitions are actually slow, and turns off the decorative effects (Tab Operations, Pane Transitions, Theme, Preview, File List, Drag & Drop) all at once to prioritize responsiveness. A toast notification is shown when the reduction kicks in. Progress indicators (GlowBar, Scan Bar) and startup effects are not affected. Even after automatic reduction, turning this setting off restores effects according to each category's setting as before.

Automatic I/O thinning (on by default): Automatically detects drives with slow file I/O from measurements taken during normal use, and skips thumbnail generation, previews of large images (over 2MB), and the speculative pre-listing done before folder tree icons are fetched (the Box Drive warm-up). This covers cloud-synced drives such as Box and OneDrive, slow network shares, and local drives slowed down by monitoring software. The decision is held per drive, so with a cloud-synced folder in pane A and a local drive in pane B, operations on the fast side are entirely unaffected. It reverts on its own once the drive stops being slow. No new disk queries are added in order to make the decision, so the feature itself can never become a source of delay. The decision uses time per unit of data as well as elapsed time, so "this image was simply large" is never mistaken for a slow drive. Image thumbnails on cloud-synced drives (Box) are held back only when the drive measures slow (files that have not finished syncing are excluded). Images of 2MB or less are still shown even on a slow drive, so the preview feature is never lost. Folder tree icons are still fetched (only the pre-listing that precedes the fetch is skipped). This is a separate setting from "Automatically reduce effects on slow systems" above (that one looks at rendering speed, this one at file I/O speed).

docs.title: Tab
docs.text:
• Tab Width: Fixed Width (default) / Auto-adjust to Folder Name.
  • Fixed Width Size: The maximum tab width in fixed-width mode (100, 120, 150 (default), 200 or 250 px).
  • Tab Wrapping: Single Row (Scroll) (default) / Multiple Rows (Wrap).
  • Sync tab row height between panes: In wrap mode, keeps the tab rows of Pane A and Pane B the same height so the address bars line up (on by default).
  • Hide tab bar when Tab List view is active: Hides the A/B pane tab bars while the Tab List view is shown in the nav pane (off by default).

For working with tabs themselves, see Tabs.

docs.title: Shortcut Keys
docs.text:
• Customize the keyboard shortcut for any action.
  • Click an action's input field and press a key to rebind; individual reset available.
  • Export / Import buttons migrate settings via JSON (structure and operations covered in How Keybindings Work).
  • The first-run guide asks you to choose a key layout (key map preset); "Zenith 2 (two-key)" is selected by default. You can change it later on this page.

docs.title: Finding a key
docs.text:
The bindable actions are grouped into File List, Tab, Sidebar, Window, Search, Global and Macros. The bar at the top of the page stays in place while you scroll, and that is where you search from.

  • Filter — works from the name or from the key.
  • "copy" → finds Ctrl+C
  • Ctrl+D → shows what that key is currently used for (the direction you need when hunting for a free key)
  • The + is optional (ctrlc still finds Ctrl+C)
  • Separate words with a space to narrow to entries containing all of them (full-width spaces work too)
  • Descriptions and group names are searched as well
  • Count — while filtering, "matches of total" is shown, so when nothing matches you can tell "there is none" apart from "the filter is wrong".
  • Jump to a group — press a group name in the bar to scroll to that heading. While filtering, only the surviving groups are listed.

docs.title: Key map presets
docs.text:
Apply another file manager's key layout in one go, from the buttons at the top of the page.

  • Zenith standard — returns every assignment to its default
  • Total Commander style — F5 copy, F6 move, F7 new folder, F8 delete, Shift+F6 rename, F3 quick preview, Ctrl+R refresh, Ctrl+D favorites, Alt+F7 search
  • Zenith 2 (two-key) — Ctrl+K followed by one key opens a view; Ctrl+B followed by one key drives the panes. You only memorise the two entry keys, and holding the first one for a moment lists the keys you can press next. See Zenith 2 two-key shortcuts
  • AFXW style — C copy, M move, D delete, K new folder, R rename. A single-key layout that uses no modifiers. Assignments of this shape act only while you are in the file list — anywhere you type text, such as the path box, the search box or an inline rename, they go in as characters. Inside the list an assignment takes precedence over type-ahead, so C copies rather than jumping to names beginning with C

  • Explorer style — Backspace goes back, Alt+Up goes to the parent. It looks like a small change, but it closes the divergence people trip over first: Backspace means "up" in Zenith and "back" in Windows Explorer.

  • The breakdown is always shown before you press. How many assignments will change, and how many of those replace assignments you changed yourself. If a key would end up shared by two actions after applying, those combinations are listed too.

  • Anything the preset does not mention is left alone. Other file managers have no keys corresponding to Zenith's own features (AI, macros, themes). Those keep their current assignment, and your own individual customizations survive there as well.

  • "Zenith standard" puts everything back at any time, so trying a preset costs nothing.

  • You can add your own presets. Like themes and language files, presets are JSON read from data\keymaps\ in the execution folder. Drop in one file of the same shape and a new button appears in settings.

{
  "id": "my_layout",
  "nameKey": "keymap.preset.total_commander",
  "descriptionKey": "keymap.preset.total_commander_desc",
  "bindings": [
    { "actionId": "FileList.Delete", "key": "F8", "modifiers": "" },
    { "actionId": "FileList.AddToFavorites", "key": "", "modifiers": "" }
  ]
}

An empty key means unassigned — use it to free a default key so another action can take it. modifiers joins Control / Alt / Shift with +.

docs.title: Macro keys
docs.text:
Macros you have registered appear here too, under the Macros group. You assign keys to them exactly as you would to any other action, and you are warned if the key is already taken. If you assign one to the first stroke of a two-key shortcut such as Ctrl+K, Zenith tells you it will never fire. Two-key shortcuts (Ctrl+K then M, for example) can be assigned as well.

Note that a bare single character with no modifier (just M, say) cannot be assigned to a macro, because that character would stop working when you type a file name or filter a list.

docs.title: Moving between panes with the arrow keys
docs.text:
Whether Left and Right move between pane A and pane B can be changed from this screen. If you would rather use the arrow keys to walk the folder hierarchy, clear the assignment or move it to another key.

Note that in icon view (small, medium and large icons) Left and Right never move between panes while you are in the file list. Icons are laid out across as well as down, so moving the selection sideways takes priority. Use Tab or F6 to move between panes. If you have assigned pane movement to a key other than Left / Right, that key still works in icon view.

docs.title: When the app hotkey does not work
docs.text:
The hotkey that summons the app from outside (Ctrl+Shift+E by default) is a system-wide hotkey, and Windows grants it to one application only. If another resident program is already using the same combination, Zenith Filer cannot register it.

When that happens, a warning appears on this screen, and if you have just changed the key you also get a notification. Choose a different key, or check the settings of the program that claimed it first.

docs.title: Two-pane staples
docs.text:
• Copy to other pane / Move to other pane — sends the selection to the folder open in the other pane. It runs through exactly the same processing as drag and drop, so the name-collision prompt, the progress display and Ctrl+Z all work as usual. Nothing is sent while a single pane is shown — with the destination off screen there would be no way to tell where the files went, so it stops and says why in the status bar.
  • Open in text editor — opens the selected files in a text editor.
  • None of the three is bound to a key by default. F5 currently means Refresh, and taking it would betray the fingers of anyone coming from Explorer. Apply the Total Commander preset, or assign keys of your choosing on this page.

docs.title: Toolbar [Pro]
docs.text:
Customize the quick-access toolbar in the pane header (Back / Forward / Refresh, view-mode switches, etc.) freely.

  • Number of buttons (also in the free version): "Fewer" shows the 9 buttons File Explorer also has (Back, Forward, Up, Refresh, New Folder, Details / Medium icons / Large icons and Sort); "Standard" is the default layout (with List, Tiles and Content hidden). New users start with "Fewer".
  • Reorder: Drag buttons to change their order.
  • Show / hide: Toggle visibility per button (at least one button always remains).
  • Separators: Add or remove divider lines to group buttons.
  • Changes apply instantly across the whole app (both Pane A and Pane B) and persist across restarts. A Restore default layout button returns to the initial state.
  • Reordering, showing / hiding and separators are Pro features. In the free version only "Number of buttons" can be chosen; the rest is shown locked with guidance.

docs.title: Ring Launcher
docs.text:
Decides what goes on the ring that the left+right mouse buttons — or Ctrl+Shift+Space — bring up around the cursor (see Ring Launcher). The page is split into Basic, Assignment, and Design.

Basic

  • Explains how to summon the ring and shows the current trigger key. "Open shortcut settings" takes you to the Shortcut Keys page with that row already filtered.
  • Mode: choose 8 slots (single layer) or Multi-level. Single layer uses one ring only and is the least to remember. Multi-level unlocks sub-rings on the Assignment tab.
  • While even one sub-ring is attached, single layer is held back (otherwise it would still open outward after you switched it off). The reason is shown along with [Detach all sub-rings].
  • Restore everything to default returns to the initial arrangement (eight entries, no sub-rings). Sub-rings are deleted — use the button on the Assignment tab if you only want the slots back. The design is untouched.

Assignment

  • Assign any feature to each of the eight slots. "Change" opens the same search window as the command palette, so every feature in the app — and any macro you have saved — can be found by name.
  • The preview on the left is a live copy of the ring. Move over a row and the matching sector lights up, so you can see where that feature will sit.
  • Each row starts with its direction (up, upper right, right …) and its number. The number is the digit key you press while the ring is open.
  • × empties that slot. An empty slot stays as a faint "+" and cannot be picked on the ring — the number of slots never changes, because each direction carries meaning.
  • Sub-ring (shown only in multi-level mode): creates a second ring beyond that slot. Whatever was in the slot moves to the child's first position. Creating one takes you straight into editing it, with a trail such as Root › Sub-ring 1 above; click any step to go back.
  • Ring name: appears only while you are editing a sub-ring. Clear it to return to the default name.
  • Open: descends from a slot that leads to a sub-ring into editing its contents.
  • ↺ (on each row): restores just that slot to its default. The button is disabled on a slot that is already at its default — it is greyed out rather than hidden, so the columns never shift under your finger. It does not appear while you are editing a sub-ring.
  • Restore default assignment: restores the eight slots alone to the starting layout. The design and the mode are untouched, and no sub-ring is deleted — a detached ring stays under "Unused rings". A sub-ring has no default layout, so the button only works while you are editing the root.
  • Saved definitions (at the very bottom of the page): keep the current assignment under a name. [Save the current assignment] stores it and [Apply] brings it back. Sub-rings are kept too, names and all, so what you built comes back exactly as it was. [Overwrite] re-captures the current state; the pencil renames and the bin deletes (deleting always asks first).
  • The top two come with the app and are impossible to delete or rename. However far you wander, they are always one click away
    • 🔒 Preset (single layer, 8 slots): the factory eight
    • 🔒 Preset (two layers, 64 items): the two-ring layout, already built. Applying it switches the mode to multi-layer and turns the eight root slots into Screen / Tabs / Nav views / Find / File actions / Panes / Go / Tools, each holding eight more — 64 in all, with not a single slot left empty. The directions carry over from the single-layer preset (inside "Screen", upper-left is one pane, up is two side by side, left is the left nav…), so what your hand already knows still applies. Swap whatever you disagree with and keep it under your own name with [Save the current assignment], and you can move between the two freely
  • You are only asked before applying when the current assignment is not saved in any definition; if it is saved, you can move back and forth freely
  • Up to 20 of your own. The design is not included — that lives on its own tab
  • The section sits at the very bottom so that growing the list never pushes the assignment settings down
  • Unused rings: rings that no slot points to. Emptying a slot with × does not delete the ring itself — it lands here, so reattaching it or removing it stays your call.
  • Rearranging and sub-rings are the Pro features. In the free version, summoning the ring and its eight starting entries still work.

Design (available to everyone)

Choose the ring's shape and motion from five presets. The colours come straight from your theme, so it never clashes when you switch themes.

Design Character Standard A line of light runs out from the direction you last chose and the ring blooms behind it; the light then follows wherever you point Swift Appears by the shortest path with no bounce — smooth over remote desktop or on slower machines Bloom Opens wide, and the light chases your hand with a long trail Slate Nothing moves; only the colour changes, quietly. A flat look with the gaps closed up Pulse Lights the selected slot in a strong colour
  • Picking one plays it in the preview right away (it opens, points in three directions, and chooses). Play replays it whenever you like.

How names are shown (above the designs)

Option What you see Horizontal labels (default) Names sit next to the icons in horizontal text, cut to fit inside the ring; the full name appears in the centre Icons only The ring shows only slightly larger icons, and the name of whatever you point at appears large in the centre Curved text Smaller text curves along the outer edge of the ring

For how the motion works, see Ring Launcher under "Light and motion". - When "I. File List" is off on the Effects page, every design appears instantly; the page says so.

docs.title: Search (Search UI)
docs.text:
Search bar

  • Move search bar to second row in dual-pane mode: In dual-pane (side-by-side) mode, the toolbar and the search bar are split into two rows so the search box gets more room.
  • One-press full reset with Esc: Pressing Esc in the search bar clears the text, the filter and the scope at once (off by default). When off, the first Esc clears the text and the second clears the filter.
  • Auto-switch to single pane mode when searching: On expands results into single-pane (off by default). Searching from Pane B moves the search tab to Pane A.
  • Search file contents with the Windows index: In normal search, places covered by the Windows index (the one File Explorer's search uses) also return files whose contents contain the words, including PDFs and Office documents (off by default). See Search Features.

Opening search results

  • Search Behavior (select from 3 patterns for where results are displayed)
  • Same pane, new tab: Enter opens results in a new tab in the same pane.
  • Same pane, current tab: Enter shows results in the current tab; clearing returns to the list.
  • Other pane, new tab: Enter opens results in a new tab in the other pane. In single-pane, automatically switches to dual-pane.
  • Search Result Path Click Behavior (select from 3 patterns for clicking the path column)
  • Show in same tab: Switches from search results back to the normal list.
  • Same pane, new tab: Opens a new tab in the same pane.
  • Other pane, new tab: Opens a new tab in the other pane (auto-switches to dual-pane if needed).

docs.title: Index (Indexing & Freshness)
docs.text:
See Index Settings for details.

Update Timing

  • Auto-detect changes (Recommended): Watches for file changes and takes in the differences right away.
  • Update at regular intervals (default): Updates the registered folders every 1 hour / 2 hours (default) / 4 hours / day. Pick the interval from the list that appears below this choice when you select it.
  • Update only when needed: Updates only when you press "Create Unindexed" or "Full Rebuild…" in the Index view. No automatic indexing at startup.

Performance & Load

  • Update index in eco mode: Throttles CPU and disk use to reduce impact on other apps (on by default; see Idle Execution (CPU load avoidance)).
  • Process network drives with lower priority: Processes UNC and mapped drives slower than local, reducing bandwidth and server load (on by default).
  • Minimum Full Re-index Interval: 6 hours / 12 hours / 24 hours (default). Manual full rebuilds inside the interval are converted to incremental updates.
  • Update index only when CPU load is low (off by default): When on, updates run only while CPU use is below the CPU usage limit (10% / 20% (default) / 30%).

Search Result Freshness

  • Keep as up-to-date as possible (freshness priority): Starts background incremental updates and unindexed-creation for all target folders in parallel with search (off by default).
  • Show a message when the index may be outdated: Displays a warning above search results when unindexed folders exist. Dismissible with the X on the right (on by default).

Per-Item Settings

Lists how each registered folder is updated. Open a row to change that folder's detailed settings (see Per-Folder Settings).

docs.title: AI
docs.text:
Sets up the services used by AI features. Along the top of the page are Overview and a tab for each provider (Ollama, Gemini, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Claude, Claude Code). For setup steps see Setting Up Generative AI; for what is sent see Privacy Policy.

Overview

  • Enable AI features: When off, all AI features are turned off.
  • Active Provider: Choose from Claude / OpenAI / Azure OpenAI / Gemini / Ollama / Claude Code (CLI).
  • Response wait time: How long to wait for a reply. Automatic (the default), 30 sec, 1 min, 2 min, 5 min or 10 min. Automatic follows whatever you are talking to (30 seconds for cloud providers, 2 minutes for reasoning models, 4 minutes for Claude Code, 5 minutes for locally run models such as Ollama); raise it only if replies get cut off.
  • Auto AI Features: Switch off, one by one, the features that call AI without you asking: AI Greeting (off by default), AI Rename Suggestion, Challenge Title Generation, Backstory Generation, Backup AI Summary (off by default for new users) and Descriptions when adding favorites (off by default).

Provider tabs

  • API Key (Claude, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Gemini): Enter it and press "Save". Keys are encrypted with Windows' data protection (DPAPI), kept on your PC and used only for requests to that provider. "Clear" removes a saved key.
  • Azure Endpoint (Azure OpenAI): Specify the Azure resource URL.
  • Test Connection: Verify the API key.
  • Model: Pick from the models available for the provider (empty uses the default model). "Fetch latest models from API" refreshes the list. Newer-generation models can be specified too, and the request format is chosen automatically.
  • Ollama: Status, Endpoint (an Ollama on another PC works too), "Install Ollama", "Start Server", and "Pull" for recommended models. No key needed.
  • Claude Code: Status, Executable path (override) and "Validate Model". No key needed — it works if you are signed in to Claude Code on this PC.

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text: Lists settings backups and handles "Backup Now", restoring and locking. See Settings Backup & Recovery.

docs.title: Stickman
docs.text:
Settings for the mascot that walks along the status bar. Show Stickman on status bar is off by default, so turn it on here to use it.

  • Show dog companion (on by default) and Dumbo octopus in terminal (on by default)
  • Talk to Stickman (on by default): Hover to make Stickman stop and say something; click to chat using generative AI (5 times a day in the free version; generative AI must be set up).
  • Personality (default "Whimsical") and Reaction frequency (default "Normal")
  • Lists of Behavior Patterns, Reactions and Achievement Rewards, and "Generate behavior with AI"

See Mascot (Stickman).

docs.title: Theme Store
docs.text: Browse, install and rate themes made by other users, and upload or delete your own. See Theme Store.

docs.title: Stickman Store
docs.text: Browse, install and rate Stickman behaviors made by other users. See Mascot (Stickman).

docs.title: Challenges
docs.text: Shows challenge progress, level and title, and sets XP ranking uploads (Don't upload / Upload / Upload anonymously; new users start with "Don't upload"). "Remove from ranking" deletes your entry. See Challenges & Achievements; for what is sent, see Privacy Policy.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text: Lists the Stickman reward behaviors you have unlocked through challenges. See Reward Behaviors.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
• Feature Usage Count: How often each feature was used — search, file operations, tab operations, theme changes, AI features and so on.
  • Reset clears all statistics.
  • Most Viewed Folders: The top 50 folders by number of views, with "Open in Explorer" and "Add to favorites".
  • AI Usage Analysis: Press "Analyze" and generative AI summarises how you use the app. This sends your usage statistics, search history, the paths of folders you open often and more to the AI service (see Privacy Policy).
  • AI Token Usage: Usage by provider and model, and by feature, with an estimated cost.

docs.title: License
docs.text:
• Shows whether you are on the free version or Pro, and today's usage for each feature with a daily limit. Free-version counts reset every day.
  • Buy Pro (free version only): The button opens the store page in your browser. With the Japanese UI, Vector (¥2,310, tax and fees included) is shown first; with any other language, Polar ($15, tax and fees included) comes first, and the other store is listed below it. After purchase, your license key arrives by email.
  • Register license key: Enter the key from the email (it starts with ZFS-) and a user name, then press Register. Once registered, every feature can be used without limits. The key is checked on your PC and is never sent anywhere. The name you register becomes the initial Username used as your author name in the stores and on the XP ranking (you can change it on this page).
  • When you use up a free allowance, the notice that tells you so has a How to buy button that opens this page. The button appears only once per feature each time you start the app, and disappears after 10 seconds. The app never suggests buying at startup or on a timer.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: Send bug reports and requests to the developer, and read the replies to what you sent. How to send, reference numbers and your submission history are covered in Settings Backup & Recovery; what is sent is in Privacy Policy.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
• Shows the current version and what's new in this version (What's New).
  • Auto Update › Enable: Toggle periodic checks (on by default).
  • Also receive preview builds (off by default): Receive preview builds with changes in progress, on top of the weekly release (see Auto-Update).
  • Check for updates button: Manual check.
  • After a new-version download completes, a "Restart and apply" button appears (see Auto-Update).

docs.title: Auto-Update
docs.text: When a new version comes out, the app downloads it in the background and swaps it in only when you press "Restart". If you quit without pressing it, nothing is changed.

docs.title: How an update happens
docs.text:
1. Check: Shortly after startup the app checks for a new version, and keeps checking every few hours while it runs. To check right away, press "Check for updates" in Control Deck › About
  2. Download: When a new version is found, it is downloaded and extracted in the background without interrupting your work. Progress shows in the GlowBar
  3. Restart prompt: When everything is ready, a toast says "Update to vX.Y.Z complete. Please restart to apply" with a "Restart" button. After you close the toast, you can still apply it with "Restart and apply" on the About page
  4. Swap and restart: Press "Restart" and the app closes, switches to the new version, and starts again on its own. It then shows "Updated to version X.Y.Z", and if "Show what's new on startup" is on in Control Deck › General, a card listing the changes appears too

If you quit without pressing "Restart", the update is not applied. The next time you start the app, it checks and downloads again.

Your settings, license, themes, indexes and other data carry over through every update.

docs.title: Delta and full packages
docs.text:
Updates come in two kinds of package, and the app picks one for you.

  • Delta: Only the files that changed since the previous version. It is chosen when the version you are running matches the version the delta was built from, so the download stays small
  • Full: The whole app. If you skip versions (so the delta no longer matches), the app uses this automatically

To update by hand, download the full or delta ZIP from the Releases page (https://github.com/sulkyjp/zenithFiler_update/releases/latest ) and extract it over your existing folder. Your settings and license are kept.

docs.title: Release and preview builds
docs.text:
Updates come in two series.

Series How often Version number Who gets it Release Once a week Three parts Everyone Preview Changes in progress, several times a day if needed The previous release's number plus a fourth part Only people who turn on "Also receive preview builds" under About → Auto Update (off by default)
  • Preview builds let you try fixes and new features early, but they may still have bugs
  • Even on a preview build, you move up to the next release when it comes out (the release carries the newer number)
  • If you turn the option off again, you keep the preview build you have and return to release versions from the next release (the app never goes back to an older release)
  • Preview builds appear on GitHub Releases as pre-releases
  • While you use a preview build, the changelog (the document viewer you open from the title bar and elsewhere) lists the changes of each preview build at the top, under versions marked as previews. You can read them again there after closing the update card. When the next release comes out, the preview versions disappear and their changes are listed under the release (an item that a later preview build changed again is listed under the later one)
  • After updating to a preview build, "What's New" also appears at startup and lists only the changes that arrived in preview builds newer than the one you last saw. Each changelog entry carries the number of the preview build it first shipped in

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause and what to do "Update apply failed. Details: …" appears Swapping the files failed, so the app restarted on the old version. Antivirus software or another program may have been holding the files; wait a moment and try "Check for updates" again. Include the log location shown in the toast when you report the problem "Download failed. Opened release page in browser" appears Requests to the update server are temporarily limited. Download the ZIP from the page that opened and update by hand, or wait a while Pressing "Restart" does not bring the new version Check whether the failure toast above appeared. If not, "Check for updates" on the About page shows the current state You want to stop automatic checks Turn off "Enable" under Auto Update in Control Deck › About. You can still update by hand with "Check for updates"

docs.title: Log spec
docs.text: Checks, downloads and file swaps are recorded in the logs under data\logs, on lines starting with [Update]. Attach this log when you report an update problem. See Log Specification for how to read the logs.

docs.title: Installation and Folder Structure
docs.text: There is no installer. Extract the ZIP to any folder and double-click ZenithFiler.exe. The app is portable: it does not use the registry, and all settings and data stay inside the folder you extracted.

docs.title: System requirements
docs.text:
• Windows 10 / 11 (64-bit)
  • The .NET runtime is bundled, so there is nothing else to install
  • Generative AI features need an API key for the provider you choose, or a local LLM (Ollama). You only need this if you use AI

docs.title: Folder Structure
docs.text:
The top of the extracted folder holds just three items.

Name What it is ZenithFiler.exe A small launcher. Double-click this to start the app ZenithFiler_Readme.txt Overview, system requirements, uninstall instructions and more data The app itself and everything it uses

Do not delete the data folder. It contains the program itself (data\bin) as well as your settings, license and search indexes.

Main contents of data:

  • bin: The program itself and its components, including the helper programs used by the terminal
  • settings.json: Your settings: favorites, tab state, window placement, key bindings, search presets and so on
  • .zenith_license: Your license key (created when you apply a license)
  • backups: Automatic backups of settings.json. One is made about 5 minutes after you change a setting, and also when you close the window in resident mode and when the app exits. Backups older than 30 days are removed, except locked ones
  • index: The search index and the history database
  • logs: Activity logs and error details, useful when you report a problem
  • lang: Display language files (10 languages). Everything except Japanese is machine-translated by AI. Drop in a .json file to add your own language
  • themes: Theme files. Drop in a .json file to add your own theme. When you customize a theme, only the differences are saved under themes\_custom; the original file is never changed
  • stickman: Stickman behavior files. Drop in a .json file to add your own behavior (Writing Behavior JSON)
  • apps: The End User License Agreement (EULA) and the license notices for the bundled open-source components (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt)
  • Also the manual and changelog (docs), saved macros (macros), the manual search index (manual_index), resources for the terminal display (Assets) and more

If you update from an older version, files that the old layout kept at the top of the folder are moved into data automatically, once, on the first launch after the update. Settings, themes and indexes carry over unchanged.

docs.title: Moving to another PC or backing up
docs.text: Copy the whole data folder. That takes your settings, license and indexes with it.

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text:
1. Quit Zenith Filer. If resident mode is on, right-click the tray icon and choose "Exit"
  2. Delete the folder you extracted. Nothing is left anywhere else

docs.title: EULA (End User License Agreement)
docs.text: The welcome screen on first launch includes a "Software License Agreement" page. Turn on "I agree to the license agreement" to enable "Next". The version you agreed to is recorded in settings.json, so the page does not appear again.

docs.title: Resident Mode
docs.text: With resident mode on, the × button no longer quits the app. The window is minimized and the app keeps running, so it is back instantly the next time you need it, with no startup wait.

docs.title: Operation table
docs.text:
Action Resident mode off (default) Resident mode on × button on the title bar Quits Minimizes and keeps running × button while holding Ctrl Quits Quits Double-click the tray icon Brings the window to the front Restores the window Right-click the tray icon → "Exit" Quits Quits Taskbar button Shown Shown (stays while minimized)

The tray icon is always shown, whether resident mode is on or off. Its right-click menu has these items:

  • Open: Brings the window to the front
  • Move to main monitor: Moves the window back to the main monitor (handy if it ended up off-screen)
  • Move to current monitor: Moves the window to the monitor the mouse cursor is on
  • Window layout: Applies a saved window layout
  • Exit: Quits completely, even with resident mode on

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text:
Use Resident mode (minimize to tray) under Control Deck › General › Window (off by default).

Turning on Start when I sign in to Windows, also on the General page, turns resident mode on as well. Because the app stays running after you close the window, the global hotkey (default Ctrl+Shift+E, the "Focus Active Pane" shortcut) can show or hide it at any time.

Closing the window in resident mode also creates an automatic settings backup (see Installation and Folder Structure).

docs.title: Screen Capture
docs.text:
You can save any region of the screen as a PNG (Pro only). Once a Pro license is applied, a PRO badge appears on the title bar.

  • Capture: Double-click the PRO badge. You can also choose "Capture" from the badge's right-click menu
  • Select a region: The whole screen dims; drag over the area you want with the left mouse button. Press Esc to cancel. Selecting a tiny area (a few pixels) also cancels
  • Save: The region is saved to the save folder as capture_<date>_<time>.png. The default save folder is Screenshots in your user folder
  • Path to the clipboard: After saving, the file's full path is copied to the clipboard automatically, ready to paste into another app
  • Notification: A toast says "Screenshot saved: "
  • Change the save folder: Right-click the PRO badge and choose "Save Folder...". The menu also shows the name of the current folder. If the chosen folder cannot be written to, the image goes to the default Screenshots folder instead

    • The menu, tooltip and notification for this feature are in English whatever the display language.

docs.title: Startup Sequence
docs.text: Zenith Filer shows its window first and finishes the heavier preparation in the background afterwards, so you can start working without waiting.

docs.title: The first launch
docs.text:
A welcome screen opens and walks you through these steps. Use "Next" and "Back" to move between them.

  1. Language: Choose the display language
  2. Choose a theme: Pick a theme from the featured set or from a category. You can change it any time later
  3. Choose how the keyboard should feel: Choose "Zenith 2 (two-key)" (selected to begin with) or "Zenith standard". You can change this later in Control Deck › Shortcuts
  4. Software License Agreement: Turn on "I agree to the license agreement" to continue
  5. You're all set!: Press "Let's go" to open the main window

The "First 5 steps" card appears at the bottom right of the main window. Try each action it lists and it gets checked off one by one.

A fresh install starts out looking like a plain, conventional file manager:

  • The toolbar uses "Fewer" buttons (switch to "Standard" under "Number of buttons" in Control Deck › Toolbar)
  • Stickman is not shown on the status bar (Mascot (Stickman))
  • The level banner and the title banner are not shown on the title bar (turn on "Show level banner in header bar" and "Show challenge title banner in header" in Control Deck › General)
  • To apply the author's own setup in one go, use "Apply the author's setup" in Control Deck › General

docs.title: Later launches
docs.text:
• The welcome screen does not appear; the main window opens straight away
  • If "Restore previous tabs on startup" is on in Control Deck › General, the tabs you had open come back
  • A short welcome message plays on the status bar for about two seconds. Turn off "A. Startup & Global" in Control Deck › Effects to show the normal status bar immediately
  • The first launch after an update shows "What's New", a summary of the changes (Auto-Update)
  • If you have earned a title from challenges, it appears in the greeting in the Properties view of the nav pane (Challenges & Achievements)

After the window appears, things such as the tray icon and the update check are set up a moment later.

docs.title: When the app is already running
docs.text:
• Opening ZenithFiler.exe again does not start a second copy; the running window comes to the front
  • Right-clicking the app's taskbar button offers "Move to main monitor", "Move to current monitor" and your saved window layouts, which helps when the window has ended up off-screen
  • If you closed the window in resident mode, bring it back from the tray icon or with the global hotkey (Resident Mode)

docs.title: Challenges & Achievements
docs.text: A gamification feature that shows how deeply you use Zenith Filer. Open it from Control Deck › Challenges.

docs.title: How Challenges Work
docs.text:
Your everyday actions are counted automatically, and achievements are recorded across 15 categories.

Each category has 10 tiers, and you move to the next tier when you meet its requirement (150 challenges in total).

Challenge categories: Navigation, Search, Create, Preview, Favorites, Color Tag, Icons, Theme, Working Set, Quick Jump, Terminal, Compare, AI, Store, Feedback

Completing a challenge immediately unlocks the Stickman reward behavior for that category and tier (Reward Behaviors).

docs.title: Level and XP
docs.text:
Using the app earns experience points (XP), which raise your level. Your level appears on the Challenges page in Control Deck and can also be shown in a level banner on the title bar, which glows when you level up.

On a fresh install the level banner and the title banner are hidden. Turn on "Show level banner in header bar" and "Show challenge title banner in header" in Control Deck › General to show them. Clicking the level banner opens your achievement history.

docs.title: XP distribution and calculation
docs.text:
• XP sources: how many times you did something, times what that action is worth. Completing a challenge does not itself grant XP (it grants a coin). Actions are weighted by how much they ask of you:
XP Action 30 Rating a theme (only the first time you rate a given theme) 20 Giving a favourite an icon 15 Switching themes / colour tags 12 Downloading from the theme store / working sets 10 Adding a favourite / comparing files 8 Search / terminal 5 AI features 3 Quick jump / creating something new 2 Preview 1 Moving between folders / sending feedback

Favourites, icons, and colour tags are counted by how many you currently have, so adding and removing them in a loop does not add up. - Level calculation: one level per 100 XP, flat. Your current level and progress to the next appear on the Challenges page and in the level banner. - Ranking submission: XP Ranking in Control Deck › Challenges offers 3 options: - "Don't upload" - "Upload" (you appear under the name in "Name shown on the ranking") - "Upload anonymously" (no name is sent; you appear as "Anonymous Adventurer") - A fresh install starts on "Don't upload". Choose one of the others yourself if you want to take part Submission runs in the background when the app starts (at most once every 20 hours) and when you level up. What is sent is your display name, title, XP, level, and a random ID that keeps your entry linked to you. No personal information is included. - While submission is on, a one-time toast tells you so, with a shortcut to the setting - Choosing "Don't upload" stops all submission. Anything already sent can be removed with "Remove from ranking" - How the ranking is presented: "View" opens a level distribution, not a ranked list. It shows where you sit as a top-percentage and a rank, with a bar chart of how many people are in each level band. It also shows the XP remaining to your next level and roughly where that would place you. The view is designed to stay meaningful while you participate anonymously. - Below the distribution is "Everyone's titles", ordered by level, with identical titles folded into a single row carrying a count such as "×3". The row holding your own title is tinted - The footer shows the number of participants, the highest level, and how many have launched within 30 days - If you are participating anonymously, "Show my name" takes you to the display-name setting - The developer's own machines are excluded from every rank, count, and distribution - Name shown on the ranking: Set it in the field directly under the "View" button inside the XP Ranking card. Whatever you type there is how you appear on the ranking (up to 24 characters). - The field starts out holding the name currently in use. If you have set an "author name" on the license/store page, that is the initial value - Leaving it blank falls back to the store "author name". If both are blank, the anonymous name is sent - While "Upload anonymously" is selected no name is sent, so the field is disabled - Changes take effect on the next submission (on level-up, or when you switch the submission mode)

docs.title: Epithets (Titles)
docs.text:
Your title (epithet) is built by combining the highest title you hold in each category. It is rebuilt whenever that combination changes, that is, whenever you reach a higher tier somewhere.

  • When generative AI is on and "Challenge Title Generation" is on in Control Deck › AI, the AI writes the title in your current display language. Otherwise the titles are combined into one without AI
  • Each title comes with a narrative backstory of a few sentences. With "Backstory Generation" on and AI available, the AI writes it; otherwise it is assembled from a fixed pattern
  • The title appears at the top of the Challenges page and can also be shown in the title banner on the title bar. Hover over the banner to read the backstory
  • Once you have a title, it also appears in the greeting in the Properties view of the nav pane

Title history: The dialog opened with "View History" has a "Title History" tab listing every title so far, with the date, the titles it was built from, and its backstory (up to 200 entries are kept). Clicking the title banner on the title bar opens Title History directly.

docs.title: Challenge Cards
docs.text:
Each challenge is displayed in its own card.

A card shows your progress, the current tier, what it takes to complete, and its backstory. Every challenge has a narrative backstory, available in all 10 languages.

Click a card to read the full story. Challenges that have reached the highest tier (Tier 10) display a crown icon with a gentle pulsing glow animation.

docs.title: Feature Recommendation System (Just-in-time Tips)
docs.text: Looks at how you use the app and suggests features you haven't tried yet at a good moment. Hints appear in the Properties view. It is off at first; turn on "Show feature recommendations" in the settings opened from the gear in the Properties view's heading.

docs.title: Top Level (Behavior)
docs.text: Field Type Required Default Description name string Yes "" Behavior name (should be unique). Also shown in settings weight int No 1 Selection weight. Higher values mean more frequent selection (values below 1 count as 1) description string No — Description text shown in the settings page description.{language} string No — Description for one language (for example "description.en"). The one for the display language is used if present; otherwise description category string No "special" "basic" = basic behavior; anything else = special behavior reactive string No null For a behavior that reacts to an event, the triggering event name (Events and Personality). Such a behavior is never picked as an ordinary behavior pro bool No false true makes it a Pro-only behavior tier int No 1 Rarity (1–10). Higher tiers are picked more often unlock string No null The challenge ID that unlocks it (for example "nv_100"). It is never picked until that challenge is completed (Reward Behaviors) rare bool No false true makes it a rare behavior. It is never picked normally; instead, each time a behavior is picked there is a 1% chance that one of the rare behaviors plays hidden bool No false true keeps it out of the behavior list and it is never picked author string No — Author name origin string No — "user" marks a behavior you made yourself. Behaviors made with AI carry it, which enables "Edit" and "Upload to store" in the behavior list's right-click menu phases array Yes — Array of behavior phases (at least one required)

docs.title: Phase (Each Element in the phases Array)
docs.text: Field Type Required Default Description duration number or [min, max] No 1 Phase duration in seconds. Use an array for a random range pose string No "stand" Stick figure pose (Poses, Dog Commands and Props). Names not in the list are drawn standing speed number or [min, max] No 0 Movement speed (px/sec). Use an array for a random range. The personality's speed multiplier applies movement string No null "forward" to move in the current direction. null to stay still reverseAtEdge bool No false true to turn around on reaching the status bar edge limbAnimation bool No false Limb animation ON/OFF limbSpeed number No 8 Limb animation speed jump object No null Jump settings (see below) flipInterval number No null Reverse direction at this interval (seconds) dogBehavior string No null Command for the companion (Dog Commands). null for normal follow moveTo string No null "edge" heads for an edge and ends the phase on arrival: the nearer edge the first time, then the opposite edge from last time. Use it with "movement": "forward" and speed, and not together with reverseAtEdge yOffset number No 0 Base height offset (px). Negative values move upward. Sets the baseline altitude for the phase; can be combined with jump followers int No 0 Number of followers (up to 8). That many stick figures walk along with the leader aura bool No false true shows rotating, flickering rays (a halo) around the head scale number No 1.0 Rendering scale (1.0 = normal, 2.0 = double). Zero or less counts as 1.0 projectileType string No null (bone) The thrown object's shape during the throw pose. "bone" (two crossed lines) / "frisbee" (flattened ellipse) / "ball" (circle) prop string No null Prop key (Available Props)

docs.title: Jump Settings (jump Object)
docs.text: Field Type Default Description height number 5 Jump height (px) period number 0.4 Time for one jump cycle (seconds). Smaller = faster

docs.title: How to Add Custom Behaviors
docs.text:
Add JSON files to the stickman folder inside the data folder to create your own behavior patterns. "Open stickman folder" in Control Deck › Stickman opens this folder.

  1. Create a .json file in data\stickman (any file name). One folder level below is fine too (files inside the archive folder are not loaded)
  2. Write the JSON following the reference above
  3. Restart the app to load it
  4. Toggle behaviors on or off in Control Deck › Stickman

Notes: - Files with an empty or missing phases array are skipped - JSON syntax errors will not crash the app — only the affected file is skipped - Comments (//) and trailing commas in the JSON are accepted - If multiple behaviors share the same name, all are loaded, but unique names are recommended so you can tell them apart in settings - You can have as many behaviors as you like react to the same event; one of them is picked each time - A behavior that fails while playing is not picked again until the next startup

docs.title: Reactive Event List
docs.text:
These are the event names you can put in the reactive field of a behavior JSON. When you do the matching action, a behavior for that event may cut into the current one (not every time; see How reactions play).

The groups in the table are the same as the groups in the "Reactions" list in Control Deck › Stickman.

Group Event name Trigger Working with files Worked You used a file or tool action that none of the rows below covers Working with files Created You created a new folder, a new text file, a new item or a shortcut Working with files Copied You copied, cut, pasted, moved or dragged and dropped Working with files Renamed You renamed something or ran a batch rename Working with files Deleted You deleted something Tidying and archiving Archived You compressed something Tidying and archiving Extracted You extracted or tested an archive Sharing and exporting Shared You did something to share, such as a share link, copying a Box path, or cloud or remote permissions Sharing and exporting Listed You exported or copied a list Looking around Looked You used tabs, preview, the view, the command palette, a context menu or quick jump, or switched panes Looking around Sorted You sorted Looking around ViewChanged You changed the view mode, icon size or column widths Looking around Inspected You looked inside something with Properties, hashes, compare, folder sync or Quick Look Looking around SearchStarted A search started Looking around SearchCompleted A search found results Looking around SearchEmpty A search found nothing Places and layout FolderNavigated You moved to another folder Places and layout TabSwitched You switched tabs Places and layout FavoriteAdded You added a favorite Places and layout NavJumped You switched the view in the nav pane Places and layout LayoutChanged You changed the nav pane layout, the window, or the toolbar state Places and layout WorkingSetSwitched You used a working set Tools AiUsed You used an AI feature (except talking to Stickman) Tools MacroRan You ran a macro Tools TerminalUsed You used the terminal (including opening a terminal tab and sending to Claude) Tools ThemeChanged You changed the theme Moments and milestones AppStartup The app started (once) Moments and milestones LevelUp You leveled up Moments and milestones FileOperationCompleted A file operation such as a copy, move or delete finished Moments and milestones Combo You repeated the same action (with gaps of 6 seconds or less: 8 times on Quiet, 5 on Normal, 3 on Lively) Moments and milestones LateNight You used the app between midnight and 5 a.m. (now and then, not every time) When things go wrong Oops You used undo or redo When things go wrong ErrorOccurred You cancelled an operation partway through

Combo and LateNight are special reactions that play instead of the ordinary one. After one plays, there is a longer wait before the next special reaction (5 minutes on Quiet, 2 on Normal, 1 on Lively).

docs.title: How reactions play
docs.text:
• Stickman does not react to every action. "Reaction frequency" in Control Deck › Stickman sets the chance that a reaction plays and the pause that follows it
Reaction frequency Chance Pause after a reaction Quiet 15% 25 seconds Normal (the default) 35% 10 seconds Lively 80% 4 seconds

Before the same reaction plays again, the pause is doubled. The higher the personality's reaction sensitivity, the more often reactions play and the shorter the pauses - AppStartup and LevelUp always play, with no pause - You can give one event as many behaviors as you like; one of them is picked each time - Behaviors you switched off in the "Reactions" list, and Pro behaviors in the free version, never play. If an event has no behavior that can play, nothing happens - While you are talking to Stickman, it does not react

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Choose the personality under "Personality" in Control Deck › Stickman.

Personality Share of basic behaviors Reaction sensitivity Speed Character Calm (calm) 70% Low (×0.5) ×0.7 Mostly basic behaviors; moves slowly and walks further Playful (playful) 30% Normal ×1.3 Mostly special behaviors; quick, with shorter walks Whimsical (random, the default) 50% Normal ×1.0 Balanced, standard speed Diligent (reactive) 60% High (×1.5) ×1.1 Reacts readily to what you do

docs.title: How behaviors are chosen
docs.text:
• Between behaviors, Stickman walks a distance that suits its personality
  • For the next behavior, the personality's share of basic behaviors first decides between basic behaviors ("category": "basic") and special ones (everything else); one is then picked by weight within that group
  • Higher-tier behaviors are more likely to be picked (Tiers 1–3 ×1, 4–6 ×1.5, 7–9 ×2, 10 ×3)
  • Recently played behaviors are less likely (the last one ×0.1, the one before ×0.3, the one before that ×0.6)
  • Each time a behavior is picked, there is a 1% chance that a rare behavior (the bear sighting) plays instead (Reward Behaviors)
  • Reward behaviors you have not unlocked, behaviors you switched off, and Pro behaviors in the free version are never picked

docs.title: Exporting a Behavior as an Animated GIF
docs.text:
You can export a Stickman behavior you created or saved as an animated GIF that looks exactly like the preview (for sharing on X and similar services).

  • From the AI generation dialog: Use the "Save as GIF" button on the result screen after generating a behavior.
  • From the saved list: Under "Behavior Patterns" in Control Deck › Stickman, right-click a behavior and choose "Save as GIF" (locked behaviors cannot be exported).

The exported GIF loops forever and uses the theme's Stickman preview color (a solid background). Dog, props, aura, followers and other effects are included just as in the preview. One loop is recorded, and long behaviors are automatically capped at a fixed duration.

docs.title: Generating a behavior with AI (condition chips)
docs.text:
From "Generate behavior with AI" in Control Deck › Stickman, you can have the AI create a new stickman behavior.

  • Availability: It unlocks when your challenge level reaches 50. Before that, pressing it tells you your current level and the level needed. Generative AI must be on and set up
  • Limits: Twice a day in the free version (a use is counted when you save the behavior; opening and closing the dialog does not count). Unlimited with Pro

In addition to free text, you can specify details with categorized chips, just like the AI theme generator.

  • Vibe / theme (multi-select): pick the mood of the motion from comical, heroic, fighting, chaotic, mystical and more. Left-click to pick, right-click to mark "never use" (NG).
  • Composition presets (one each): choose companion (solo / dog / crowd), tempo (relaxed / normal / frantic), spectacle (subtle / standard / flashy) and length (short / medium / long). Leaving a row on "Auto" lets the AI decide.
  • Fine detail (optional, multi-select): force specific poses, props or dog actions to be included. Poses and props can also be right-clicked to mark "never use".

Your selections are passed to the AI as constraints: anything marked "must include" always appears, and anything marked "never use" never does. The selections carry over into "Refine" (fine-tuning with an extra instruction) and "Regenerate".

Press "Save" and the new behavior joins Stickman's behaviors right away, no restart needed, and appears in the "Behavior Patterns" list. From that list's right-click menu you can also "Edit" it (rework it in the AI dialog), "Upload to store" or "Delete" it (Mascot (Stickman)).
